  "new_string": "    async def _project_users_to_slots(\n        self, credential_type: CredentialType\n    ) -> dict[int, SlotCredential]:\n        \"\"\"\n        Project the lock's users to a slot -> ``SlotCredential`` map for\n        the given ``credential_type``.\n\n        Every managed slot is present even when empty: the projection\n        starts from ``managed_slots`` mapped to ``SlotCredential.empty()``\n        and then overlays the credentials of ``credential_type`` read via\n        ``async_get_users``. This preserves the slot-keyed contract the\n        coordinator, sync manager, and slot entities depend on -- a\n        managed slot missing from the map is treated as unavailable, not\n        empty, so the empty placeholders are load-bearing. Occupied slots\n        the lock reports that are not managed are surfaced too.\n        Credentials of other types are dropped here -- the seam keeps\n        everything below it slot-shaped and single-type this round.\n\n        This is the chokepoint for \"the base class filters per credential\n        type before passing to the coordinator/entities\" (Option A in the\n        design discussion). Adding a second supported type means calling\n        this helper from a second projection method -- providers store\n        every type they can map, so no provider changes are required.\n\n        TODO(option-b): when the integration adds a second supported\n        credential type (Z-Wave User Credential CC also exposes\n        ``PASSWORD``), revisit whether the coordinator/entities should\n        instead be type-scoped from the top -- one set of slot entities\n        per credential type -- rather than threading the type through a\n        single projection. The provider-side model is already ready for\n        that move; the open question is configuration / user experience\n        (do users configure \"PIN slots 1-10\" and \"password slots 1-5\"\n        separately, or is each slot polymorphic?).\n        \"\"\"\n        codes = {slot: SlotCredential.empty() for slot in self.managed_slots}\n        codes.update(\n            {\n                credential.slot: credential.state\n                for user in await self.async_get_users()\n                for credential in user.credentials_of_type(credential_type)\n            }\n        )\n        return codes\n\n    async def async_get_usercodes(self) -> dict[int, SlotCredential]:\n        \"\"\"\n        Return the slot -> ``SlotCredential`` map for Personal Identification\n        Numbers.\n\n        Thin Personal-Identification-Number-shaped wrapper over\n        ``_project_users_to_slots``; preserved as a stable name because\n        the coordinator, sync manager, and slot entities are all\n        Personal Identification Number-scoped today.\n        \"\"\"\n        return await self._project_users_to_slots(CredentialType.PIN)"

An unrepresented credential type returns an empty list, not None.\n        assert user.credentials_of_type(CredentialType.NFC) == []\n\n    def test_pin_credentials_delegates_to_credentials_of_type(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"pin_credentials is the Personal Identification Number flavor of the generic accessor.\"\"\"\n        pin = Credential(\n            type=CredentialType.PIN, slot=3, state=SlotCredential.known(\"1234\")\n        )\n        password = Credential(\n            type=CredentialType.PASSWORD, slot=4, state=SlotCredential.known(\"pwd\")\n        )\n        user = User(user_id=3, credentials=[pin, password])\n        assert user.pin_credentials == user.credentials_of_type(CredentialType.PIN)\n\n    def test_credential_for_returns_first_match_or_none(self) -> None:\n        empty_pin = Credential(\n            type=CredentialType.PIN, slot=3, state=SlotCredential.empty()\n        )\n        user = User(user_id=3, credentials=[empty_pin])\n        assert user.credential_for(CredentialType.PIN) is empty_pin\n        assert user.credential_for(CredentialType.RFID) is None"

> AGENT

`b392f114` pushed to PR 1227 — full suite 1030 passing.

**What I shipped (Option A):**
- `User.credentials_of_type(type)` — the generic primitive; `pin_credentials` and `credential_for` now delegate to it
- `BaseLock._project_users_to_slots(credential_type)` — the chokepoint that turns users into a slot-keyed map for any single credential type
- `async_get_usercodes()` is now a thin PIN wrapper over that helper, so coordinator/sync/slot-entity callers stay PIN-scoped
- TODO(option-b) comment on `_project_users_to_slots` capturing the entity-type scoping question for when a second type lands
- `zwave_js.async_get_users` collapsed: build `users_by_id` dict once, walk credentials once, attach by reference; map covers PIN/PASSWORD/RFID/NFC/FACE/FINGERPRINT
- Tests for `credentials_of_type`, the parametric projection across PIN/RFID/PASSWORD, and orphan-credential drop in the provider

**On passwords / Option B (saved to memory as `project_password_credential_expansion`):**

My take on the modeling question:

The Z-Wave User Credential CC indexes credentials as `(user_id, type, slot)` — slot 1 PIN and slot 1 password can coexist independently. That naturally argues for **type-scoped slot ranges in the config**, not polymorphic slots. Something like: the user adds a "PIN slots" config block (slots 1–10) and optionally a "password slots" block (slots 1–5), each with its own entity tree. From a user-experience standpoint that's cleaner than one entity that can be either type — automations and dashboards work per-type without conditional logic on a `credential_type` attribute.

If you go that route, Option B (separate entity classes per type) starts to earn its complexity right when password support lands. Until then, Option A is doing its job. I'd recommend:

1. **Don't pre-build Option B** when you start password support — exercise the existing `_project_users_to_slots` chokepoint with `PASSWORD` first and see how far the slot-keyed-but-type-parametric model gets you in practice.
2. **The polymorphic-vs-type-scoped slot question is a config flow question**, not a base class question. Sketch the config UX for "user wants both PIN and password slots" before deciding whether the coordinator needs to multiplex.
3. **Matter side might lag**: DoorLock cluster has credential types, but I don't know the state of `lock_helpers` password support — if it's PIN-only there too, Z-Wave-only password support is a reasonable first cut.

The relevant historical context: the `User.credentials` list and the `CredentialType` enum (including `PASSWORD`) were already in place from the original credential model PR — the seam was always designed for this. PR #1227's refactor just made sure the provider doesn't silently swallow types the seam can already represent.

287	def user_from_slot(slot: int, state: SlotCredential, name: str | None = None) -> User:
288	    """
289	    Build the single-credential user for a managed slot.
290	
291	    Realizes today's one-managed-slot to one-user to one-PIN-credential
292	    projection: the user identifier shares the slot index, the user owns
293	    exactly one PIN credential at that index, and the user is active exactly
294	    when the slot holds a code. A future multi-credential world only appends
295	    to ``credentials`` -- no field changes here.
296	    """
297	    return User(
298	        user_id=slot,
299	        name=name,
300	        active=state.is_present,
301	        credentials=[credential_from_slot(slot, state)],
302	    )

> AGENT

Good context — the slot=user model simplifies a lot. Here's how I'd think about both questions with that mental model.

## Config schema with multi-type credentials per slot

```yaml
1:
  name: Alice
  pin: "1234"
  password: "hunter2"  # optional, future
  enabled_condition: ...
```

Backward-compatible — existing configs (just `pin`) keep working, new fields are additive. Inside LCM: slot 1 = user_id 1 with N credentials, one per supported type. The base orchestration just calls `_project_users_to_slots` once per type (PIN today, PIN+PASSWORD when password lands).

## Question 1: First upgrade

**Best case — 700/800-series Z-Wave locks (User Credential CC supported):**
LCM 1.x set codes via the legacy User Code CC at user_id=slot. On firmware that supports User Credential CC, the lock typically reflects those legacy codes through the new CC view too — so `node.access_control.get_users_cached()` returns user_id=1 with PIN at slot 1, exactly matching LCM's 1:1:1 convention. The coordinator reads, matches the configured value, and sync stays quiet. Clean migration with zero writes.

**Worst case — 500-series locks (no User Credential CC):**
`node.access_control.*` doesn't exist on these nodes. The first read currently raises a cryptic `AttributeError`/`ValueError` from `lock_helpers`. We should mirror what matter.py does in `async_setup` — call `lock_helpers.async_get_credential_capabilities(node)` once at setup and raise a clear `LockCodeManagerProviderError` if it doesn't return the expected shape. Something like:

```python
async def async_setup(self, config_entry):
    ...
    try:
        caps = await lock_helpers.async_get_credential_capabilities(self.node)
    except (BaseZwaveJSServerError, HomeAssistantError) as err:
        raise LockCodeManagerProviderError(
            f"{self.lock.entity_id}: this Z-Wave lock does not support User "
            f"Credential CC, which is required by Lock Code Manager 2.x. "
            f"Older Z-Wave 500-series locks need a prior LCM version. ({err})"
        ) from err
    if not caps.get("supports_user_management"):
        raise LockCodeManagerProviderError(...)
```

This belongs in **PR 1227** — it's a small addition and prevents a confusing first-upgrade failure.

The bigger question: do you want to **keep a User Code CC fallback** in tree for 500-series locks? If so, that's a substantial side-by-side codebase. My recommendation: don't. Document the firmware floor in release notes, stamp it on the manifest's HA-version requirement, and tell 500-series users to pin LCM 1.x. The credential model isn't worth straddling.

## Question 2: Existing user with multiple credentials

Yes, **clear only the PIN, not the user** — and the existing `_drop_credential` already does this correctly:

| Scenario | Today's behavior with my refactor |
|---|---|
| LCM sets PIN on slot 1, lock has user 1 with PIN+RFID | `async_set_user` adopts user 1 (cache hit), PIN gets replaced, RFID untouched ✓ |
| LCM clears slot 1, user 1 has PIN+RFID | PIN cleared, `_drop_credential` sees `len(remaining_credentials)>0`, user 1 survives, RFID still works ✓ |
| LCM clears slot 1, user 1 has PIN only | PIN cleared, `_drop_credential` deletes user 1 ✓ |
| LCM sets PIN on slot 1, lock has user 5 with PIN at slot 1 (out-of-band) | LCM forces user_id=1, write either reassigns slot 1's PIN to user 1 or fails; user 5 is left credential-less |

That last row is the only weird case and it's a side effect of forcing `user_id == slot`. I think this is **fine and aligns with your "slot per user, keep it simple" preference**: LCM owns the convention "slot N = user_id N". Out-of-band state that violates it gets normalized on first write. The orphan user 5 doesn't break anything — it's just a dead row that the user can clean up via HA's Z-Wave UI if they care.

What I would NOT do:
- Adopt by slot owner (like Matter does) — that breaks the slot=user_id invariant and makes future debugging hairier. Matter has to do it because Matter auto-allocates user_index; Z-Wave lets us pick, so we should pick the value that maintains the simple mental model.
- Sweep non-PIN credentials when "taking over" a slot — that's overreach. The integration manages credential types it knows about; everything else is the user's business.

1. **In PR 1227** (small): add the User Credential CC setup gate with a clear error message. 5-line change.
2. **Release notes** (in PR 1227 or a docs PR): document the firmware requirement and the "first upgrade adopts existing codes" behavior.
3. **Follow-up issue** (when password support lands): expand the config schema to accept `password:` alongside `pin:`. The base class projection is already type-parametric; the work is config schema + UI + slot entity for the new type.
4. **Open question for later**: do you want a "purge slot" service that nukes the entire user record (including non-LCM credentials)? Default behavior preserves; a service gives the user an explicit escape hatch. Doesn't have to ship now.

async def async_get_users(node: Node) -> UsersResult:
    """List all users with their credential references."""
    supported = await node.access_control.is_supported()
    if not supported:
        raise HomeAssistantError(
            translation_domain=DOMAIN,
            translation_key="access_control_not_supported",
        )

    user_caps = await node.access_control.get_user_capabilities_cached()
    users = await node.access_control.get_users_cached()
    all_credentials = await node.access_control.get_all_credentials_cached()

    credentials_by_user: defaultdict[int, list[Credential]] = defaultdict(list)
    for cred in all_credentials:
        credentials_by_user[cred.user_id].append(
            Credential(
                type=CREDENTIAL_TYPE_MAP.get(cred.type, str(cred.type)),
                slot=cred.slot,
            )

    user_list: list[UserEntry] = [

            user_id=user.user_id,

        )
        for user in users
    ]

    return UsersResult(

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
`homeassistant.components.zwave_js.lock_helpers.async_get_users()` exists and does exactly the join I just hand-rolled in our provider. BUT it drops the credential `data` field (PIN value), so we can't use it directly for our "readable PIN" projection — that's why the provider reaches into `node.access_control` for `get_all_credentials_cached()`. You're right on both counts. Here's how I'd split them:

## On point 2 (500-series, abstract API)

We don't need to sniff CCs. Every `lock_helpers` function starts with `await node.access_control.is_supported()` and raises a structured `HomeAssistantError(translation_key="access_control_not_supported")` if not. That's the abstract API doing its job — it tells us "this lock can't do User Credential", we translate.

The fix in `async_setup`: probe via the helper, catch the known error, raise a clear LCM error.

```python
async def async_setup(self, config_entry):
    self._clear_listeners()
    try:
        await lock_helpers.async_get_credential_capabilities(self.node)
    except HomeAssistantError as err:
        if getattr(err, "translation_key", None) == "access_control_not_supported":
            raise LockCodeManagerProviderError(
                f"{self.lock.entity_id}: this Z-Wave lock does not expose "
                f"the User Credential Command Class, which Lock Code Manager "
                f"requires. Older Z-Wave 500-series locks need a prior LCM "
                f"version. ({err})"
            ) from err
        raise LockDisconnected(f"{self.lock.entity_id}: capabilities probe failed: {err}") from err
    self._listeners.append(...)
```

No CC enum imported in our code, no `.is_supported()` introspection. We trust the helper to know, and we translate its "can't" into our typed error. If HA's `lock_helpers` ever grows a User Code CC fallback for 500-series, we get it for free without touching this file.

## On point 1 (name reconciliation on 700/800)

I'd split this in two:

**Free win (already happens):** Every time the seam writes a credential, `_put_credential` calls `async_set_user(user)` with the config-side name. Our `async_set_user` truncates to `_max_user_name_length` and calls `lock_helpers.async_set_user`. So any slot whose PIN changes also gets its name fixed.

**The gap:** A slot whose PIN already matches won't trigger a set, so a stale lock-side name survives. The cases:
- First upgrade where firmware reported max=14 and a 16-char config name was set previously
- Out-of-band name edit via the Z-Wave UI
- Firmware update changes max length

For this, a **setup-time pass**: read users, compare `user.name` against the truncated config name per slot, fix mismatches via `async_set_user` (which is a metadata-only write — no PIN touched). Small loop, runs once per setup, idempotent.

```python
# Inside async_setup, after the capabilities probe:
desired_names = self._desired_user_names()  # slot -> truncated config name
for user in await self.async_get_users():
    desired = desired_names.get(user.user_id)
    if desired is not None and user.name != desired:
        await self.async_set_user(
            User(user_id=user.user_id, name=desired, active=user.active)
        )
```

This needs `_desired_user_names()` to read from `self.managed_slots` and config — small helper that already half-exists.

## What the current PR did

Replaced the legacy User Code CC implementation entirely. Net effect on a 500-series lock today: `node.access_control` doesn't exist, every primitive blows up at the first call.

## What we want

Both backends live in the provider, picked at setup by what the lock actually supports — not by us inspecting CC enums.

```python
@dataclass(repr=False, eq=False)
class ZWaveJSLock(BaseLock):
    lock_config_entry: ConfigEntry = field(repr=False)
    _backend: _CredentialBackend = field(init=False)

    async def async_setup(self, config_entry: ConfigEntry) -> None:
        self._clear_listeners()
        # node.access_control.is_supported() is the abstract probe — no
        # CC enum sniffing on our side. The Z-Wave JS library decides
        # what "supported" means.
        if await self.node.access_control.is_supported():
            self._backend = _UserCredentialCCBackend(self)
        else:
            self._backend = _UserCodeCCBackend(self)
        await self._backend.async_setup(config_entry)
        self._listeners.append(...)

    async def async_get_users(self) -> list[User]:
        return await self._backend.get_users()

    async def async_set_user(self, user: User) -> SetUserResult:
        return await self._backend.set_user(user)

    # ... every primitive delegates ...
```

Two backend classes, same internal interface:

- `_UserCredentialCCBackend` — everything I added in PR 1227 (uses `lock_helpers`, `node.access_control`, multi-credential model, name truncation, hard refresh via `get_users`/`get_all_credentials`).
- `_UserCodeCCBackend` — the legacy path from main, lifted into a class. PIN-only by definition (User Code CC has no concept of named users or non-PIN credentials), so `async_get_users` returns the slot-keyed view shimmed into 1:1 Users with `user_id == slot` and `name=None`.

The base orchestration doesn't change. The 1:1:1 mapping the seam already assumes is exactly what User Code CC gives you natively; the User Credential CC backend is what unlocks the "user with multiple credentials, names, etc." future.

## Setup gate and name reconciliation, with this architecture

- The setup probe is just `node.access_control.is_supported()` — no error to translate, no CC enum imported. If the lock has neither (effectively impossible — a Z-Wave lock always supports User Code CC), the legacy backend still tries to write and surfaces a clean LockDisconnected.
- Name reconciliation only applies to the credential-CC backend (legacy has no names). Lives inside `_UserCredentialCCBackend.async_setup`, runs the per-slot truncation-vs-lock check we discussed. Legacy backend's setup is a no-op for name fixing.

## Scoping question

The amount of code to lift back from main is meaningful (~600 lines of legacy paths) plus the new abstraction. Three reasonable shapes:

1. **Land it all in PR 1227.** ~+800 lines on top of what's there. Big diff, but ships a complete, non-regressive feature in one go.
2. **Two PRs, abstraction first.** PR α: introduce the `_CredentialBackend` strategy pattern with the legacy code as the only backend (no behavior change, pure refactor of main's provider into a backend class). PR β: add `_UserCredentialCCBackend` and the dispatch. Cleaner review surface but front-loads a "looks like nothing changed" PR.
3. **Revert PR 1227, redo on top of α.** Lose the work done so far, gain a cleaner sequence.

My recommendation is **(2)**. PR α is mechanical (extract-class refactor of existing legacy code), PR β reuses everything in PR 1227 as the new backend. Each PR has a clear narrative: "no functional change, just shape the seam"; then "add a second backend behind the seam". Tests come with each PR — PR α inherits the existing legacy tests, PR β brings the new tests I already wrote.

Caveats / things I want to flag:

- **Push subscriptions differ** between the two CCs. The legacy backend has the value-update / duplicate-sniff path (the one PR 1227 dropped). The credential CC backend uses access-control node events. Both `setup_push_subscription` / `teardown_push_subscription` need to delegate to the backend.
- **Notification event handling** (the `_handle_zwave_js_event` for lock/unlock state) is CC-agnostic, lives on the provider, stays as-is.
- **Capabilities** differ — User Code CC has no `max_user_name_length`. The legacy backend returns `LockCapabilities(supports_user_management=False, max_users=N, credential_types={PIN: ...})` from the User Code CC's own capability surface. That makes `supports_user_management=False` the signal the future config flow could read to say "this lock cannot do passwords, hide the password field".
- **The whole password-credential expansion plan goes from "works on all Z-Wave locks" to "works on 700/800-series only".** Worth flagging in the password discussion — `supports_user_management` becomes the gate for showing the password config field.

Which sequencing do you want — (1), (2), or something else?

# --- Business logic functions ---


async def async_get_credential_capabilities(
    node: Node,
) -> CredentialCapabilitiesResult:
    """Query access-control capabilities for the node."""
    supported = await node.access_control.is_supported()
    if not supported:
        raise HomeAssistantError(
            translation_domain=DOMAIN,
            translation_key="access_control_not_supported",
        )

    user_caps = await node.access_control.get_user_capabilities_cached()
    cred_caps = await node.access_control.get_credential_capabilities_cached()

    supported_credential_types: dict[str, CredentialTypeCapability] = {}
    for cred_type, capability in cred_caps.supported_credential_types.items():
        type_str = CREDENTIAL_TYPE_MAP.get(cred_type)
        if type_str is None:
            continue
        supported_credential_types[type_str] = CredentialTypeCapability(
            num_slots=capability.number_of_credential_slots,
            min_length=capability.min_credential_length,
            max_length=capability.max_credential_length,
            supports_learn=capability.supports_credential_learn,
        )

    return CredentialCapabilitiesResult(
        supports_user_management=True,
        max_users=user_caps.max_users,
        supported_user_types=[
            USER_TYPE_MAP[ut]
            for ut in user_caps.supported_user_types
            if ut in USER_TYPE_MAP
        ],
        max_user_name_length=user_caps.max_user_name_length or 0,
        supported_credential_rules=[
            CREDENTIAL_RULE_MAP[cr]
            for cr in user_caps.supported_credential_rules
            if cr in CREDENTIAL_RULE_MAP
        ],
        supported_credential_types=supported_credential_types,
    )

            LOCK_USERCODE_ID_PROPERTY: code_slot,
            LOCK_USERCODE_STATUS_PROPERTY: CodeSlotStatus.ENABLED,
            LOCK_USERCODE_PROPERTY: usercode,
        }
        for code_slot, usercode in codes.items()
    ]
    # https://zwave-js.github.io/node-zwave-js/#/api/CCs/UserCode?id=setmany
    data = await node.async_invoke_cc_api(
        CommandClass.USER_CODE, "setMany", cc_api_codes, REDACTED
    )

    if not data:
        raise ValueError("Received unexpected response from User Code CC setMany API")

    return SupervisionResult(data)

> AGENT

Confirmed on capabilities. `lock_helpers.async_get_credential_capabilities` hardcodes `supports_user_management=True` (line 244 of HA 2026.6.1's `lock_helpers.py`) — `max_user_name_length > 0` is the actual "lock has real users with names" signal. `supports_user_management` as a feature gate is misleading.

One detail I want to confirm before sketching the rest: in current HA 2026.6.1, `lock_helpers.async_get_credential_capabilities` still gates on `node.access_control.is_supported()` and raises `access_control_not_supported` if not. It doesn't yet project User Code CC into the user+PIN shape itself — that projection has to happen in our legacy backend. If you're saying that's planned upstream, our legacy backend gets a sunset path; if it's already shipped on a newer HA branch I missed, point me at it and I'll switch to it.

## Sync state: name + every credential, written granularly

The "in sync" predicate becomes ALL of:
- `lock.user.name == truncated(config.name)` (trivially true on User Code CC because both sides are None)
- For each managed credential type T: `lock.user.credential_of_type(T) == config.credential_for(T)`

The slot is out of sync until every field matches. Sync writes only the deltas — name-only via `async_set_user`, credential-only via `async_set_credential` per mismatching type, both if both differ. The base orchestration's `_put_credential` is the "both" combinator; expose the name-only path as `_put_user_name` (just `async_set_user` with the rollback omitted — there's no follow-up write to roll back to). Sync layer calls the granular primitives.

Concrete check, per slot:

```python
desired = ConfigSlot(name="Alice Smith", pin="1234", password=None)  # later: more types
lock_user = lock_users_by_slot.get(slot)  # User from async_get_users (lock side)

if lock_user is None:
    # Slot empty on lock; create via _put_credential (name + PIN in one go).
    needs = ["create"]
else:
    name_matches = lock_user.name == truncated(desired.name, max_user_name_length)
    pin_matches = lock_user.credential_for(PIN) and lock_user.credential_for(PIN).matches(desired.pin)
    needs = []
    if not name_matches:
        needs.append("name")
    if not pin_matches:
        needs.append("pin")
    # future: same for PASSWORD, etc.

# Dispatch on `needs`:
# - {} -> in sync, no write
# - {"name"} -> async_set_user(user) only
# - {"pin"} -> async_set_credential(...) only
# - {"name","pin"} or "create" -> _put_credential (full lifecycle, rollback on PIN fail)
```

For the **User Code CC backend**, `name` is structurally None on both sides, so the name comparison is a no-op — `needs` is always either `{}` or `{"pin"}`. The sync layer doesn't need to know which backend it's talking to; the data shape carries the truth.

This requires the coordinator/sync to carry richer state than `dict[int, SlotCredential]` — at minimum `dict[int, User]` so name is visible. The slot-projection chokepoint I added in `_project_users_to_slots` is fine for slot entities (the entity tree is still PIN-shaped today), but the **sync manager** wants the full User. Easy: add a parallel `async_get_users_by_slot()` helper that maps `slot -> User` (where slot is the user's owning PIN credential slot today), or have the sync manager call `async_get_users()` directly and key by `user.user_id`.

## Capability-driven config UI (for the password discussion)

With `max_user_name_length > 0` as the proper signal:
- **User Credential CC lock**: config shows `name`, `pin`, future `password` fields per slot.
- **User Code CC lock**: config shows only `pin` (name and password fields hidden / disabled).
- The form schema for a slot becomes capability-derived rather than hardcoded.

This dovetails with the password-credential expansion memo: a future PASSWORD field on a config slot is gated by `caps.credential_types[PASSWORD]` being present, which only the User Credential CC backend ever advertises.

## Where this leaves PR 1227

The base-class changes I already landed in `b392f114` (parametric `_project_users_to_slots`, `credentials_of_type`) are still correct and stay. The sync expansion to include name is independent of the backend split and could land in either order:

- Backend split first: PR α (extract legacy User Code CC into a backend class, no behavior change) → PR β (add User Credential CC backend behind same interface, restoring what PR 1227 dropped for 500-series) → PR γ (sync expansion to include name + smart granular writes).
- Sync expansion first: PR γ (richer sync state, currently exercised only on User Credential CC test fixtures) → PR α → PR β.

I'd still lean PR α → β → γ — the backend split is the regression fix, sync expansion is the enhancement. Want to confirm that ordering and that I should start PR α next? And do you want PR 1227 held as-is (with the breaking change for 500-series until α + β land), or should I open a PR α that targets `zwave-js-credential-migration` so PR 1227 picks up the non-regression on merge?

> AGENT

You were completely right. I traced through all three layers; here's what `is_supported()` actually means.

## The trace

**Layer 3 — node-zwave-js v15.23.4** (`packages/zwave-js/src/lib/node/endpoint-mixins/index.ts:13`):

```typescript
public get accessControl(): AccessControlAPI | undefined {
    if (
        !this.supportsCC(CommandClasses["User Credential"])
        && !this.supportsCC(CommandClasses["User Code"])
    ) {
        return undefined;
    }
    this._accessControl ??= new AccessControlAPI(this);
    return this._accessControl;
}
```

The driver exposes `accessControl` if the endpoint supports **either** CC. The API itself then has a private `#usesUserCredentialCC` flag and every method branches internally — `getUsersCached`, `setUser`, `getCredentialCapabilitiesCached`, etc. all have a `#u3cAPI()` path and a User Code CC fallback.

**Layer 2 — zwave-js-server** (`src/lib/endpoint/access_control/message_handler.ts`):

```typescript
case EndpointAccessControlCommand.isSupported: {
    return { supported: endpoint.accessControl !== undefined };
}
```

So `is_supported` literally returns "does the endpoint expose `accessControl`" — true for both 500-series and 700/800-series locks.

**Layer 1 — zwave_js_server-python** (`zwave_js_server/model/access_control.py:525`): bare RPC pass-through, returns the bool.

**The HA wrapper** (`lock_helpers.async_get_credential_capabilities`): the `access_control_not_supported` error only fires if the lock supports neither CC — effectively never for a real lock. For a UC lock, `get_user_capabilities_cached` returns `max_user_name_length=0` (UC has no names), so the helper returns `supports_user_management=True, max_user_name_length=0`. Exactly what you said.

## What this means for PR 1227

**The backend split I was about to propose is unnecessary.** The driver already does the CC abstraction inside `accessControl`. PR 1227 works on a 500-series lock today — `node.access_control.get_users_cached()` and `get_all_credentials_cached()` route through the User Code CC path in the driver, return UserData/CredentialData with no names and PIN values, and our `_project_users_to_slots` (PIN-only today) produces the right slot map.

What I was wrong about:
- I assumed `node.access_control` existed only on User Credential CC locks. It exists on both.
- I assumed lock_helpers needed to grow a User Code CC fallback. The fallback is one layer deeper, in the driver, where it belongs.
- I told you to expect a regression for 500-series users. There isn't one.

What still holds:
- `max_user_name_length > 0` is the right capability gate for name-aware UX and future password support (UC locks will report 0 and not appear in `credential_types[PASSWORD]`).
- Sync state should include name when present; trivially equal when both sides are None on UC locks.
- The HA integration's zwave-js version floor matters — name + multi-credential surfaced via `accessControl` requires zwave-js 15.23.4+. HA 2026.6.1 pulls that version; we should make the manifest's HA version requirement explicit so older HA versions (which would pull older zwave-js) fail loudly at install rather than silently misbehave.

## Revised follow-up scope

Drop the "backend split PR α / PR β" idea entirely. The fast-follows that remain are:

1. **Setup probe** (in PR 1227): keep the `async_get_credential_capabilities` call wrapped, but the error message changes — it's not "your lock doesn't support User Credential CC" anymore, it's "this lock exposes neither User Credential CC nor User Code CC" (i.e., it's not really a lock the integration can manage). Edge case, but the typed error is still nicer than a raw AttributeError.
2. **Sync name reconciliation** (separate PR): expand the sync "in sync" predicate to include `user.name == truncated(config.name)` and add the granular `name-only` write path. Skipped on UC locks because the comparison is trivially equal.
3. **Capabilities-gated config schema** (when adding password): per-slot fields appear based on `caps.credential_types` and `max_user_name_length > 0`.

Sound right? If so I'll wire the smaller setup probe into PR 1227 next.

  "content": "---\nname: project_zwave_credential_cc_abstraction\ndescription: node-zwave-js v15.23.4+ unifies User Code CC and User Credential CC behind a single accessControl API. is_supported() is True for both 500-series and 700/800-series locks. PR #1227's credential migration does NOT drop legacy lock support — the CC dispatch is at the driver layer.\nmetadata:\n  type: project\n---\n\nThe biggest discovery from working through PR #1227's User→Credential migration: the User Code CC vs User Credential CC dispatch is **already done inside node-zwave-js**, not in LCM or in HA's `lock_helpers`. PR #1227 looked like a breaking change for 500-series Z-Wave locks; it isn't.\n\nTraced through all three layers at v15.23.4:\n\n**node-zwave-js** (`packages/zwave-js/src/lib/node/endpoint-mixins/index.ts:13`):\n```typescript\npublic get accessControl(): AccessControlAPI | undefined {\n    if (\n        !this.supportsCC(CommandClasses[\"User Credential\"])\n        && !this.supportsCC(CommandClasses[\"User Code\"])\n    ) {\n        return undefined;\n    }\n    this._accessControl ??= new AccessControlAPI(this);\n    return this._accessControl;\n}\n```\n\nThe `AccessControlAPI` class then has a private `#usesUserCredentialCC` flag and every method (`getUsersCached`, `setUser`, `getCredentialCapabilitiesCached`, `getUserCapabilitiesCached`, ...) branches internally between the U3C path and the User Code CC fallback.\n\n**zwave-js-server** (`src/lib/endpoint/access_control/message_handler.ts`):\n```typescript\ncase EndpointAccessControlCommand.isSupported: {\n    return { supported: endpoint.accessControl !== undefined };\n}\n```\n\n`is_supported` literally returns \"does the endpoint expose `accessControl`\" — true for both 500-series and 700/800-series locks. Only a lock that supports neither CC (effectively never for a real Z-Wave lock) returns false.\n\n**zwave_js_server-python** and **HA lock_helpers**: bare RPC pass-through plus a thin shape projection. `lock_helpers.async_get_credential_capabilities` hardcodes `supports_user_management=True` and returns `max_user_name_length = user_caps.max_user_name_length or 0`. For UC locks the underlying value is 0 (UC has no names); for U3C locks it's the real max.\n\n**Why:** `supports_user_management` is NOT the gate for \"lock has real users with names\" — it's always True per the helper. The actual signal is **`max_user_name_length > 0`**. Use that to gate name-aware UX and future password support (UC locks will report 0 and not appear in `credential_types[PASSWORD]`).\n\n**HA version floor:** the unified `accessControl` API on the driver requires zwave-js >= 15.23.4. HA 2026.6.1 pulls that. The integration's manifest should pin an HA-version floor that guarantees this; below it, PR #1227 would silently misbehave because the driver wouldn't expose `accessControl` at all.\n\n**How to apply:**\n- Do NOT add a backend-split / dispatch layer in LCM's zwave_js provider. The driver does the dispatch.\n- Stop worrying about \"this PR breaks 500-series users\" — it doesn't, as long as the HA version floor is enforced.\n- For future capability-gated features (passwords, names): key on `max_user_name_length > 0` and `credential_types` mapping, not `supports_user_management`.\n- One caveat: `lock_helpers.async_get_users()` drops the credential `.data` field (only carries type+slot). Our provider has to call `node.access_control.get_users_cached()` + `get_all_credentials_cached()` directly to keep the PIN value for the readable projection. See [[project_credential_mgmt_refactor]].\n"

  "content": "---\nname: project_pr1227_sync_state_design\ndescription: Design direction agreed during PR #1227 review — sync \"in sync / out of sync\" is per-slot across name AND every managed credential type, with smart granular writes. Slot = user_id invariant preserved.\nmetadata:\n  type: project\n---\n\nSettled during PR #1227 discussion (June 2026). When the LCM sync layer expands beyond PIN-only:\n\n**In-sync predicate per slot** is the conjunction of:\n- `lock.user.name == truncated(config.name, max_user_name_length)` — trivially equal on User Code CC locks because both sides are None\n- For each managed credential type T: `lock.user.credential_of_type(T) == config.credential_for(T)` (today only PIN; future PASSWORD etc.)\n\nSlot is \"out of sync\" until every field matches. Sync writes only the deltas — name-only via `async_set_user`, credential-only via `async_set_credential` per mismatching type. `_put_credential` is the \"both/create\" combinator and stays the rollback-bearing path.\n\n**Slot = user_id invariant kept.** LCM enforces the convention \"slot N = user_id N\" — adopt-by-existing-owner (the Matter pattern) is NOT brought to Z-Wave even though the User Credential CC would allow it. Reasons:\n- Matches the existing 1:1:1 mental model.\n- An orphan user with no credentials (left over when LCM normalizes out-of-band state) is harmless and visible in HA's Z-Wave UI.\n- Simpler debugging — slot number always equals user_id.\n\n**Multi-credential user adoption.** When LCM manages slot 1 and the lock has user 1 with PIN + RFID (set out-of-band), LCM:\n- Adopts user 1 (cache hit on `get_user_cached(user_id=1)`)\n- Updates only the PIN, leaves the RFID untouched\n- On clear: removes only the PIN; `_drop_credential` keeps the user because RFID remains\n- Eventually deletes the user when its last credential is removed (existing seam logic)\n\nLCM manages credentials it knows about; everything else is the user's business. NO sweep of non-managed credential types.\n\n**Config schema direction** (when password support lands):\n```yaml\n1:\n  name: Alice\n  pin: \"1234\"\n  password: \"hunter2\"  # capability-gated, only shown if max_user_name_length>0 and PASSWORD in credential_types\n  enabled_condition: ...\n```\nSlot per user; each slot can carry one credential per supported type. Polymorphic-slot vs type-scoped-slot debate resolved by user as \"slot per user, keep it simple\". See [[project_password_credential_expansion]].\n\n**Why:** the alternative — clear non-PIN credentials on takeover — was rejected as overreach. The right principle: LCM is the source of truth for the credential types it manages, not for the user record as a whole.\n\n**How to apply:** when expanding the sync layer beyond PIN-only, replace `dict[int, SlotCredential]` \"desired vs actual\" comparisons with `dict[int, User]` (or equivalent) so the comparison sees name + every credential type. Granular write primitives already exist (`async_set_user`, `async_set_credential`); the work is in the sync manager, not the providers. See [[project_password_credential_expansion]] for the broader roadmap and [[project_zwave_credential_cc_abstraction]] for the driver-level CC dispatch that makes this work transparently across 500/700/800-series locks.\n"
}

Assumptions about what an abstract API \"must mean\" routinely go wrong without the trace.\nmetadata:\n  type: feedback\n---\n\nWhen working on Z-Wave-related questions, trace through ALL of: the Python client (`zwave_js_server`), the Node.js server (`zwave-js-server`), and the driver itself (`node-zwave-js`). All three are checked out at `~/projects/`. **Pull latest in each repo before searching** — local checkouts can be on feature branches or behind the released version that's installed in the venv.\n\n**Why:** Lost real time during PR #1227 review by reasoning from the surface API alone. I assumed `node.access_control.is_supported()` meant \"User Credential CC supported\" because the namespace name (`access_control`) sounded like it. Wrong — tracing to the driver showed the API is exposed for either User Credential CC OR User Code CC, and dispatch happens INSIDE the API. I was about to propose a big backend-split refactor for a problem that didn't exist. The user caught it with a single pointed question.\n\n**How to apply:**\n- Before drawing an architectural conclusion from an abstract API (\"we need to do X because the API requires Y\"), trace through every layer. The thing you assume the API requires may be handled one layer down.\n- For Z-Wave specifically:\n  - HA integration: `~/projects/lock_code_manager/.venv/lib/python3.14/site-packages/homeassistant/components/zwave_js/`\n  - Python client: `~/projects/zwave-js-server-python/`\n  - Node.js server: `~/projects/zwave-js-server/`\n  - Driver: `~/projects/node-zwave-js/`\n- The venv version often LEADS the local main checkout — installed packages may have features not yet in your local main, or behind tags you need to check out explicitly (see the v15.23.4 dance for `accessControl`).\n- The user's instinct \"the whole point of the abstract API is to not have to know this\" is correct — if the abstraction looks leaky, the leak is probably in your reading, not the API.\n"
}

				? data
				: Bytes.from(data);
			const result = await api.set(
				userId,
				status as number,
				codeData,
			);
			let succeeded: boolean;
			if (result == undefined) {
				const verified = await api.get(userId);
				succeeded = verified?.userCode === codeData;
			} else {
				succeeded = supervisedCommandSucceeded(result);
			}
			if (succeeded) {
				const node = this.endpoint.tryGetNode();
				if (node) {
					node.emit(
						existingCred
							? "credential modified"
							: "credential added",
						this.endpoint as any,
						{
							userId,
							credentialType: type,
							credentialSlot: userId,
							data,
						},
					);
				}
			}
			return succeeded
				? SetCredentialResult.OK
				: SetCredentialResult.Error_Unknown;
		}
	}

	/**
	 * Deletes the given credential.
	 * This communicates with the node.
	 */
	public async deleteCredential(
		userId: number,
		type: UserCredentialType,
		slot: number,
	): Promise<SetCredentialResult> {
		if (this.#usesUserCredentialCC) {
			this.#assertValidSlot(type, slot);

			const api = this.#u3cAPI();
			const raw = await api.setCredential({
				operationType: UserCredentialOperationType.Delete,
				userId,
				credentialType: type,
				credentialSlot: slot,
			});
			if (raw) await this.endpoint.tryGetNode()?.handleCommand(raw);
			return u3cCredentialReportTypeToSetCredentialResult(
				raw?.reportType,
			);
		} else {
			// User Code CC stores exactly one credential per user slot. Ignore the
			// caller-provided unified slot and write back to the owning user's slot
			// so events and cached state stay internally consistent.
			this.#assertValidSlot(type, userId);
			const existed = this.#getCredentialCached_UC(
				type,
				userId,
			) != undefined;
			const api = this.#ucAPI();
			const result = await api.clear(userId);
			let succeeded: boolean;
			if (result == undefined) {
				const verified = await api.get(userId);
				succeeded = existed
					&& verified?.userIdStatus === UserIDStatus.Available;
			} else {
				succeeded = supervisedCommandSucceeded(result) && existed;
			}
			if (succeeded) {
				const node = this.endpoint.tryGetNode();
				if (node) {
					node.emit("credential deleted", this.endpoint as any, {
						userId,
						credentialType: type,
						credentialSlot: userId,
					});
					node.emit("user deleted", this.endpoint as any, { userId });
				}
			}
			return succeeded
				? SetCredentialResult.OK
				: SetCredentialResult.Error_Unknown;
		}
	}

> AGENT

Traced through. **Events are identical across CCs — but the write ordering isn't.** Push subscriptions are safe; one provider-level guard is still needed.

## Events: same for both CCs

`AccessControlAPI` emits the same event names regardless of which CC backs the operation:
- `"user added"` / `"user modified"` / `"user deleted"`
- `"credential added"` / `"credential modified"` / `"credential deleted"`

For UC the events are synthesized inside the API methods themselves; for U3C they're driven by report handling. Same payload shape: `{userId, credentialType, credentialSlot, data?}`. PR 1227's push subscription wires those three credential events and `_pin_state(args.data)` handles the present/absent value uniformly. **No push subscription split needed.**

One nuance worth knowing — UC's `deleteCredential` fires BOTH `"credential deleted"` AND `"user deleted"` (because UC ties them together), so our handler will see two events for a single clear. Currently harmless because our handlers are idempotent per slot.

## Reads / capabilities: same shape

Everything from `getUsersCached`, `getAllCredentialsCached`, `getCredentialCapabilitiesCached`, `getUserCapabilitiesCached` returns the same Python types regardless of CC. UC just populates them with `max_user_name_length=0`, names=None, `credential_types={PIN: {...}}` (PIN-only). **No read-path split needed.**

## Writes: the one real asymmetry

`AccessControlAPI.setUser()` on a UC lock (`feature-apis/AccessControl.ts:540` area):

```typescript
const existingCode = this.getValue<string>(UserCodeCCValues.userCode(userId)...);
if (!existingCode) {
    throw new ZWaveError(
        "User Code CC requires a credential to be set before modifying the user. Use setCredential() first.",
        ZWaveErrorCodes.Argument_Invalid,
    );
}
```

UC has no concept of a userless user — the user IS the code. So:
- **Empty slot, U3C lock**: `_put_credential` → `async_set_user` (creates user) → `async_set_credential` (attaches PIN). Works.
- **Empty slot, UC lock**: `_put_credential` → `async_set_user` **throws** → no PIN written. **Regression.**
- **Occupied slot, UC lock**: `async_set_user` works (code already exists, can re-send to update active/status). `async_set_credential` overwrites the value. Works.

So the seam's "set user first, then credential" ordering breaks on UC for the create case specifically. The driver doesn't paper this over because it's a real semantic difference, not a CC-API difference.

## Fix

Smallest change: have `async_set_user` skip the driver call on UC locks. Detect UC structurally — UC's capabilities are `max_user_name_length == 0` AND the credential-types map has PIN only with no other entries. (We already cache `max_user_name_length`; the PIN-only check is one capabilities-read away.)

Sketch:

```python
@property
def _is_legacy_user_code_cc(self) -> bool:
    """
    UC vs U3C heuristic from capabilities.

    User Code CC locks always report max_user_name_length=0 and expose
    only the PIN credential type. A U3C lock could theoretically also
    report 0-length names, but it would still advertise the full
    credential vocabulary — the conjunction is the practical signal.
    """
    return (
        self._max_user_name_length == 0
        and self._supported_credential_types == {CredentialType.PIN}
    )

async def async_set_user(self, user: User) -> SetUserResult:
    ...resolve caps as today...
    if self._is_legacy_user_code_cc:
        # UC: the user record doesn't exist independently of the credential.
        # Skip the driver call; async_set_credential will create the user
        # implicitly. Report created=False so _put_credential doesn't try
        # to roll back a user it didn't actually write.
        return SetUserResult(user_id=user.user_id, created=False)
    # ...existing U3C path with name truncation + lock_helpers.async_set_user...
```

Trade-off: we lose the ability to update `active`/`userType` on UC locks. LCM doesn't model `userType` today and treats slots as always-active, so the practical impact is zero. If we ever wanted active-toggling on UC, we'd add a "credential exists?" pre-check and only call setUser when it does (matter.py-style).

Tests:
- Add a UC-fixture test that walks through `_put_credential` on an empty slot — should succeed with one `set_credential` call and zero `set_user` calls.
- Existing U3C tests stay green because the guard only fires when `max_user_name_length == 0`.

## Summary

| Surface | UC vs U3C | LCM split needed? |
|---|---|---|
| Push events | Identical names + shape | No |
| Capabilities | Same fields, UC has 0/PIN-only | No |
| Read paths (`getUsers*`, `getAllCredentials*`) | Same shape | No |
| `setCredential` | Same call site, works without prior `setUser` | No |
| `setUser` empty-slot | UC throws | **Yes — provider-level guard, ~10 lines** |
| `deleteCredential` | UC fires extra `"user deleted"` event | No (idempotent) |
| `deleteUser` | Both work; UC clears the underlying code | No |

So: one guarded branch in `async_set_user`, plus the structural UC-detection helper. Belongs in PR 1227 with the setup probe. Want me to wire it in?

> AGENT

Yes, I think it's a good idea — with a couple of edges to think about up front.

## My take

**Strongest part**: the "skip locks where the capability doesn't apply" rule. Without it you'd be stuck choosing between constraining everything to the UC-level (no names ever) or pretending UC locks have names (they don't). The skip rule lets each capability aggregate over only the locks that actually have it, which is the right semantic.

**The aggregation rule is correct for numeric bounds** (min via max, max via min, both monotone). It generalizes cleanly to PIN length, name length, slot counts, and any future numeric capability.

**Where I'd want explicit design choices before shipping**:

1. **Impossible aggregates**. If lock A says 4–6 and lock B says 8–12, the LCD is min=8, max=6 — empty. Fail-loud at setup with a config error ("these locks have incompatible PIN length requirements; split them into separate config entries") is better than silently clamping to one or the other. Worth deciding the failure shape now.

2. **Different shapes per capability kind**. Numeric bounds aggregate as min/max. Boolean flags (e.g. `supports_learn` for RFID — if relevant later) aggregate as AND across locks that support the type. Type availability (does any lock support PASSWORD?) is a disjunction over the contributing-locks set. So "LCD" is really three rules dressed up as one — easy enough but worth documenting per type.

3. **Per-type capability gating is separate from length aggregation**. If two locks support PASSWORD and one doesn't, you've got a choice: hide the password field entirely (safe, restrictive), or show it and have sync only write to supporting locks (flexible, possibly confusing). My preference: show it with an attribute or footnote indicating which locks will receive the value — but this is a UX call, not an engineering one.

4. **Reactivity on lock add/remove**. Adding a tighter-bound lock to an existing config entry can invalidate previously-valid configured PINs/names. Plan: re-validate slot configs at setup against the new aggregate, mark invalid slots disabled with a clear warning, surface in the UI.

Bottom line: the principle is right and the design generalizes well; the failure modes (empty aggregate, mixed type support) are where it earns or loses its UX.

In\n        particular, User Code CC's ``setUser`` requires an existing\n        credential because the user IS the code, so the base\n        orchestration's \"set user first, then credential\" sequence has\n        to be adapted for that backend.\n\n        The unified API does not expose the underlying CC directly. The\n        practical signal is the capability conjunction: User Code CC\n        always reports ``max_user_name_length=0`` (no names) and only\n        the Personal Identification Number credential type. A User\n        Credential CC lock that happened to report 0-length names would\n        still advertise the broader credential-type vocabulary, so the\n        conjunction is what disambiguates.\n\n        Returns ``False`` when capabilities have not yet been resolved\n        -- caller defaults to the User Credential CC path, which is the\n        more common case today and degrades gracefully if the heuristic\n        is wrong (the driver surfaces a clear ``ZWaveError`` we map to\n        ``LockOperationFailed``).\n        \"\"\"\n        if (\n            self._max_user_name_length is None\n            or self._supported_credential_types is None\n        ):\n            return False\n        return self._max_user_name_length == 0 and self._supported_credential_types == {\n            CredentialType.PIN\n        }"

The\n    subsequent async_set_credential creates the user implicitly. We\n    return ``created=False`` because there is no separate user record\n    for _put_credential to roll back if the credential write fails.\n\n    Detection signal: ``max_user_name_length == 0`` AND only PIN in\n    ``supported_credential_types`` — the conjunction is the practical\n    User Code CC indicator.\n    \"\"\"\n    pin_type_str = lock_helpers.CREDENTIAL_TYPE_MAP[UserCredentialType.PIN_CODE]\n    mock_lock_helpers[\"async_get_credential_capabilities\"].return_value = {\n        \"supports_user_management\": True,\n        \"max_users\": 30,\n        \"supported_user_types\": [],\n        \"max_user_name_length\": 0,\n        \"supported_credential_rules\": [],\n        \"supported_credential_types\": {\n            pin_type_str: {\n                \"num_slots\": 30,\n                \"min_length\": 4,\n                \"max_length\": 8,\n                \"supports_learn\": False,\n            }\n        },\n    }\n\n    user = User(user_id=5, name=\"alice\", active=True)\n    result = await zwave_js_lock.async_set_user(user)\n\n    assert result == SetUserResult(user_id=5, created=False)\n    mock_lock_helpers[\"async_set_user\"].assert_not_called()\n\n\nasync def test_async_set_user_calls_driver_for_user_credential_cc_with_no_name_support(\n    zwave_js_lock: ZWaveJSLock,\n    mock_access_control: MagicMock,\n    mock_lock_helpers: dict,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"\n    A degenerate U3C lock with ``max_user_name_length == 0`` but multi-type\n    support is NOT treated as User Code CC -- the driver call still goes\n    through with ``user_name=None``.\n\n    Guards against an over-broad UC heuristic: max_user_name_length alone\n    is not enough; the credential-type set must also be PIN-only.\n    \"\"\"\n    pin_type_str = lock_helpers.CREDENTIAL_TYPE_MAP[UserCredentialType.PIN_CODE]\n    rfid_type_str = lock_helpers.CREDENTIAL_TYPE_MAP[UserCredentialType.RFID_CODE]\n    mock_lock_helpers[\"async_get_credential_capabilities\"].return_value = {\n        \"supports_user_management\": True,\n        \"max_users\": 30,\n        \"supported_user_types\": [],\n        \"max_user_name_length\": 0,\n        \"supported_credential_rules\": [],\n        \"supported_credential_types\": {\n            pin_type_str: {\n                \"num_slots\": 30,\n                \"min_length\": 4,\n                \"max_length\": 8,\n                \"supports_learn\": False,\n            },\n            rfid_type_str: {\n                \"num_slots\": 30,\n                \"min_length\": 4,\n                \"max_length\": 16,\n                \"supports_learn\": False,\n            },\n        },\n    }\n    mock_access_control.get_user_cached.return_value = None\n    mock_lock_helpers[\"async_set_user\"].return_value = {\"user_id\": 5}\n\n    user = User(user_id=5, name=\"alice\", active=True)\n    result = await zwave_js_lock.async_set_user(user)\n\n    assert result == SetUserResult(user_id=5, created=True)\n    mock_lock_helpers[\"async_set_user\"].assert_called_once_with(\n        zwave_js_lock.node,\n        user_id=5,\n        user_name=None,\n        active=True,\n    )"

> AGENT

Different shapes. Reporting back so you can decide before I wire it up.

**Z-Wave `lock_helpers.async_get_credential_capabilities` returns:**
```python
{
    "supports_user_management": bool,         # hardcoded True
    "max_users": int,
    "supported_user_types": list,
    "max_user_name_length": int,              # ← key field
    "supported_credential_rules": list,
    "supported_credential_types": dict[str, {
        "num_slots", "min_length", "max_length", "supports_learn"
    }],
}
```

**Matter `lock_helpers.get_lock_info` returns:**
```python
class GetLockInfoResult(TypedDict):
    supports_user_management: bool
    supported_credential_types: list[str]
    max_users: int | None
    max_pin_users: int | None
    max_rfid_users: int | None
    max_credentials_per_user: int | None
    min_pin_length: int | None
    max_pin_length: int | None
    min_rfid_length: int | None
    max_rfid_length: int | None
    # NO max_user_name_length field
```

Matter's helper does **not** expose `max_user_name_length`. The Matter DoorLock cluster spec does define a UserName field with `MaxLength = 32` bytes UTF-8, but the HA helper doesn't surface that attribute today. Matter does always support user-record writes (we already require `set_lock_user` before `set_lock_credential` for new slots), so it's the lock_helpers exposure that's missing, not the lock capability.

So your proposed gate — `supports_user_management == True AND max_user_name_length > 0` — works cleanly for zwave_js but needs help on the Matter side. Three ways to bridge:

1. **Hardcode Matter's `max_user_name_length = 32`** in the provider, matching the spec's `UserName` field MaxLength. Pros: simple, no upstream dep, gate works as-is. Cons: lock-specific quirks (Aqara U300 rejecting names with spaces, per the TODO) aren't reflected.

2. **Add the field upstream to Matter's `GetLockInfoResult`** — read the `UserCommandSupport` / cluster attributes that bound name length. Cleanest long-term. Slower path.

3. **Add a separate `requires_user_writes: bool` field to LockCapabilities**, set by the provider directly — not derived from `max_user_name_length`. Pros: each provider knows its semantics, decouples the gate signal from the name-length hint. Cons: another field, semantic overlap with `supports_user_management`.

My recommendation: **(1) for PR 1227** — hardcode Matter to 32, gate on `caps.supports_user_management and caps.max_user_name_length > 0` in the base. File the upstream Matter helper improvement as a follow-up. Lets us ship the unified base gate now and refine the Matter side later without changing the LCM API.

Want me to go with (1)?

class _NativeStubLock(BaseLock):
    """Synthetic native-user provider: records primitive calls, in-memory users."""

    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs) -> None:
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
        self.calls: list[tuple] = []
        self.last_set_credential: dict | None = None
        self._users: dict[int, User] = {}

    @property
    def domain(self) -> str:
        return "test"

    @property
    def supports_native_users(self) -> bool:
        return True

    async def async_set_user(self, user: User) -> SetUserResult:
        created = user.user_id not in self._users
        self.calls.append(("set_user", user.user_id, user.name))
        self._users[user.user_id] = User(
            user_id=user.user_id, name=user.name, active=user.active
        )
        return SetUserResult(user_id=user.user_id, created=created)

    async def async_delete_user(self, user_id: int) -> None:
        self.calls.append(("delete_user", user_id))
        self._users.pop(user_id, None)

    async def async_set_credential(
        self,
        user_id: int,
        credential: Credential,
        *,
        name: str | None,
        source: Literal["sync", "direct"],
    ) -> bool:
        self.calls.append(("set_credential", user_id, credential.slot))
        self.last_set_credential = {
            "user_id": user_id,
            "slot": credential.slot,
            "name": name,
            "source": source,
        }
        self._users[user_id].credentials = [credential]
        return True

    async def async_delete_credential(self, ref: CredentialRef) -> bool:
        self.calls.append(("delete_credential", ref.user_id, ref.slot))
        user = self._users.get(ref.user_id)
        if user is None:
            return False
        user.credentials = []
        return True

    async def async_get_users(self) -> list[User]:
        return list(self._users.values())


class _DegenerateStubLock(BaseLock):
    """Synthetic slot-only provider: implements only credential primitives."""

the credential-type set must also be PIN-only.\n    \"\"\"\n    pin_type_str = lock_helpers.CREDENTIAL_TYPE_MAP[UserCredentialType.PIN_CODE]\n    rfid_type_str = lock_helpers.CREDENTIAL_TYPE_MAP[UserCredentialType.RFID_CODE]\n    mock_lock_helpers[\"async_get_credential_capabilities\"].return_value = {\n        \"supports_user_management\": True,\n        \"max_users\": 30,\n        \"supported_user_types\": [],\n        \"max_user_name_length\": 0,\n        \"supported_credential_rules\": [],\n        \"supported_credential_types\": {\n            pin_type_str: {\n                \"num_slots\": 30,\n                \"min_length\": 4,\n                \"max_length\": 8,\n                \"supports_learn\": False,\n            },\n            rfid_type_str: {\n                \"num_slots\": 30,\n                \"min_length\": 4,\n                \"max_length\": 16,\n                \"supports_learn\": False,\n            },\n        },\n    }\n    mock_access_control.get_user_cached.return_value = None\n    mock_lock_helpers[\"async_set_user\"].return_value = {\"user_id\": 5}\n\n    user = User(user_id=5, name=\"alice\", active=True)\n    result = await zwave_js_lock.async_set_user(user)\n\n    assert result == SetUserResult(user_id=5, created=True)\n    mock_lock_helpers[\"async_set_user\"].assert_called_once_with(\n        zwave_js_lock.node,\n        user_id=5,\n        user_name=None,\n        active=True,\n    )",
  "new_string": "async def test_set_usercode_user_code_cc_skips_set_user_and_writes_credential_only(\n    hass: HomeAssistant,\n    zwave_js_lock: ZWaveJSLock,\n    mock_access_control: MagicMock,\n    mock_lock_helpers: dict,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"\n    On a User Code CC lock, the seam orchestration skips set_user entirely.\n\n    The unified accessControl API's setUser cannot run before a credential\n    exists on a UC lock (the user IS the code), so the base orchestration\n    in _put_credential takes the no-user-write path when the capabilities\n    report ``max_user_name_length == 0``. async_set_credential creates\n    the user implicitly. End-to-end check via async_set_usercode covers\n    the gate, the cache, and the provider-level credential write.\n    \"\"\"\n    lcm_entry = MockConfigEntry(\n        domain=DOMAIN,\n        data={\n            CONF_LOCKS: [zwave_js_lock.lock.entity_id],\n            CONF_SLOTS: {\"5\": {}},\n        },\n    )\n    lcm_entry.add_to_hass(hass)\n    # UC-shaped capabilities: real user-record support is hardcoded to\n    # True by the driver, but max_user_name_length == 0 signals the user\n    # is implicit in the credential.\n    pin_type_str = lock_helpers.CREDENTIAL_TYPE_MAP[UserCredentialType.PIN_CODE]\n    mock_lock_helpers[\"async_get_credential_capabilities\"].return_value = {\n        \"supports_user_management\": True,\n        \"max_users\": 30,\n        \"supported_user_types\": [],\n        \"max_user_name_length\": 0,\n        \"supported_credential_rules\": [],\n        \"supported_credential_types\": {\n            pin_type_str: {\n                \"num_slots\": 30,\n                \"min_length\": 4,\n                \"max_length\": 8,\n                \"supports_learn\": False,\n            }\n        },\n    }\n\n    changed = await zwave_js_lock.async_set_usercode(5, \"9999\", name=\"alice\")\n\n    assert changed is True\n    mock_lock_helpers[\"async_set_user\"].assert_not_called()\n    mock_lock_helpers[\"async_set_credential\"].assert_called_once()"

class TestFullSetupLifecycle:
    """Verify LCM correctly discovers and sets up the Z-Wave JS provider."""

    async def test_provider_discovered_as_zwave_js(
        self,
        hass: HomeAssistant,
        lcm_config_entry,
        lock_entity: er.RegistryEntry,
    ) -> None:

1024	    async def _get_cached_capabilities(self) -> LockCapabilities:
1025	        """
1026	        Return the lock's capabilities, populating the cache on first call.
1027	
1028	        Provider-agnostic chokepoint for capability-driven base decisions
1029	        (today: whether ``_put_credential`` writes a user record before the
1030	        credential). The cache is per-instance and lives for the lifetime
1031	        of the provider, which is recreated on each integration reload --
1032	        so a firmware update or capability change is naturally picked up
1033	        the next time the integration loads. Errors propagate to the
1034	        caller so the same backoff/retry the provider already wraps
1035	        ``async_get_capabilities`` in keeps applying.
1036	        """
1037	        if self._capabilities_cache is None:
1038	            self._capabilities_cache = await self.async_get_capabilities()
1039	        return self._capabilities_cache
1040	
1041	    @final
1042	    async def _put_credential(
1043	        self,
1044	        user: User,
1045	        credential: Credential,
1046	        *,
1047	        name: str | None,
1048	        source: Literal["sync", "direct"],
1049	    ) -> bool:
1050	        """
1051	        Run the create-on-first user lifecycle around a credential write.
1052	
1053	        Native-user only (the slot adapters call the primitives directly for
1054	        slot-only providers). On locks that expose a real user record --
1055	        ``supports_user_management`` AND ``max_user_name_length > 0`` --
1056	        the owning user is created or updated first and its resolved
1057	        identifier (which the integration may allocate) is threaded into
1058	        the credential write. On locks where the user is implicit in the
1059	        credential (Z-Wave User Code CC: the user IS the code and the
1060	        unified ``accessControl`` API's ``setUser`` cannot run before a
1061	        credential exists), the user write is skipped and the credential
1062	        write creates the implicit user. Returns True if the value
1063	        changed.
1064	
1065	        ``user`` carries the user record (identifier, name, active state)
1066	        for ``async_set_user`` on the real-user path; ``credential`` is
1067	        the specific credential to write. They are independent arguments:
1068	        the slot adapter's ``user`` happens to also list this credential
1069	        (an artifact of the one-to-one slot projection), but only
1070	        ``credential`` drives the write here.
1071	
1072	        If the credential write fails, a user this call newly created is
1073	        rolled back so the lock is not left with a credential-less user
1074	        (which the slot-keyed coordinator cannot see and would never
1075	        reconcile away). A pre-existing user is left untouched -- it may
1076	        still own other credentials. On the no-user-write path there is
1077	        nothing to roll back -- the implicit user only exists while the
1078	        credential does.
1079	        """
1080	        caps = await self._get_cached_capabilities()
1081	        needs_user_write = (
1082	            caps.supports_user_management and caps.max_user_name_length > 0
1083	        )
1084	        if needs_user_write:
1085	            result = await self.async_set_user(user)
1086	            credential_user_id = result.user_id
1087	            rollback_user_id = result.user_id if result.created else None
1088	        else:
1089	            # Implicit-user lock (e.g. Z-Wave User Code CC). The
1090	            # credential write creates the user implicitly; address the
1091	            # credential by the slot-shaped user identifier the seam
1092	            # already carries.
1093	            credential_user_id = user.user_id
1094	            rollback_user_id = None
1095	        try:
1096	            return await self.async_set_credential(
1097	                credential_user_id, credential, name=name, source=source
1098	            )
1099	        except Exception:
1100	            if rollback_user_id is not None:
1101	                try:
1102	                    await self.async_delete_user(rollback_user_id)
1103	                except Exception as rollback_err:
1104	                    LOGGER.warning(
1105	                        "Lock %s: failed to roll back newly created user %s "
1106	                        "after a failed credential write: %s",
1107	                        self.lock.entity_id,
1108	                        rollback_user_id,
1109	                        rollback_err,
1110	                    )
1111	            raise
1112	
1113	    @final

485	        """
486	        Set up lock by provider.
487	
488	        Prime the base capability cache so the orchestration's
489	        ``_put_credential`` gate (write a user record only when the lock
490	        has ``supports_user_management`` and ``max_user_name_length > 0``)
491	        is resolved before the first write, and surface a clear typed
492	        error if the lock exposes neither User Credential CC nor User
493	        Code CC (i.e. the unified ``accessControl`` API is not available
494	        at all -- effectively never for a real Z-Wave lock, but worth
495	        catching cleanly rather than as an opaque attribute error
496	        downstream).
497	
498	        Idempotent: clears existing listeners before re-registering.
499	        """
500	        self._clear_listeners()

503	        # typed LCM errors and prevent integration setup -- a Z-Wave lock
504	        # that exposes neither CC is not a lock LCM can manage.
505	        await self._get_cached_capabilities()

Both PRs updated and pushed. Summary of what shipped in this round:

**PR 1227 — `3f68291e` then `6410b35e`:**
- `LockCapabilities.max_user_name_length: int = 0` (backward-compatible default).
- `BaseLock._capabilities_cache` + `_get_cached_capabilities` helper.
- `_put_credential` now gates the user-record write on `caps.supports_user_management AND caps.max_user_name_length > 0` — locks that don't meet both skip the user write and let `async_set_credential` create the user implicitly. Rollback is a no-op on the skip path.
- `BaseLock.async_get_capabilities` raises `ProviderNotImplementedError` by default; providers routing through `_put_credential` must override.
- zwave_js: dropped the provider-specific UC heuristic (`_supported_credential_types`, `_uses_user_code_cc`, the inline guard, the inverse type map). Setup now primes the cache via the same helper. The setup probe surfaces a typed error if the lock exposes neither CC under `accessControl`.
- Stub `_NativeStubLock` in `test_seam.py` implements `async_get_capabilities` so the gate finds real capability data in tests.
- Event/e2e test fixtures pick up `mock_lock_helpers` + `mock_access_control`.
- TODO.md: added "Sync state expansion", "LCD capability aggregation" (with the failure-mode + re-validate-on-change refinements), and merged "Password expansion + Option B" into one entry covering the architectural decision the type expansion forces.
- Docstring trim: `_put_credential`, `_get_cached_capabilities`, `_capabilities_cache`, `LockCapabilities.max_user_name_length`, zwave_js `_max_user_name_length` field, `async_set_user`, `async_setup` — all now state purpose without restating the code.

**PR 1228 — `00ab2b17` then `bdbb2fae`:**
- Same `LockCapabilities.max_user_name_length` field add (kept in sync so either merge order works).
- Matter hardcodes 32 (Matter DoorLock spec UserName cap) until upstream `matter.lock_helpers` surfaces a real attribute. Comment trimmed to that one-liner.
- Matter test asserts the value.

All 1030 tests pass, pre-commit clean on both branches.

Memory notes saved earlier this session: `project_zwave_credential_cc_abstraction`, `project_pr1227_sync_state_design`, `feedback_trace_through_layers`, `project_password_credential_expansion`, `project_lcd_capability_aggregation`.

## Proposed change

Migrates the Z-Wave JS lock provider off the legacy User Code Command Class path onto Home Assistant's unified credential API (`node.access_control` + `homeassistant.components.zwave_js.lock_helpers`), implementing the `BaseLock` credential primitives introduced in #1225. This is PR 4 of the credential-management refactor (PR 3 = #1225, the seam).

The provider now:
- Sets `supports_native_users = True` and implements `async_set_user` / `async_delete_user` / `async_set_credential` / `async_delete_credential` / `async_get_users` / `async_get_capabilities`, and **drops its `async_set_usercode` / `async_clear_usercode` / `async_get_usercodes` overrides** — the base orchestration from #1225 now drives set/clear/get.
- **Reads PIN values directly from `node.access_control`** (`get_users_cached()` + `get_all_credentials_cached()`), so codes read back as `known(pin)` when the lock returns them. This gives the sync loop a fixed point (`actual == desired` → no-op) so it no longer re-writes every managed slot on each restart. Writes and capability queries go through `lock_helpers`.
- **Duplicate detection** uses the lock's typed `credential_rejected_duplicate` result (mapped to `DuplicateCodeError`), replacing the brittle `NEW_USER_CODE_NOT_ADDED_DUE_TO_DUPLICATE_CODE` notification-sniffing.
- **Push** moves from User Code CC value events to the access-control credential node events (`credential added` / `modified` / `deleted`); lock/unlock **operation** notifications still drive the code-slot events. A 1-hour `hard_refresh_interval` backstops missed events.
- **Transient Z-Wave write failures** (e.g. a sleeping/battery lock) map to `LockDisconnected` (retry), not a slot suspension.

`hacs.json` already requires HA 2026.6.0 (#1221), where `lock_helpers` shipped — no version bump needed.

## Type of change

- [ ] Dependency upgrade
- [ ] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix/feature causing existing functionality to break)
- [ ] Code quality improvements to existing code or addition of tests

## Additional information

- Net `−511` lines in the provider; the legacy User Code CC code, V1 post-write verification, and duplicate-notification sniffing are removed.
- Z-Wave PIN reads are now `known` (readable) again via the direct access-control read path — an explicit design choice (vs the helper, which withholds data) so the sync loop has a fixed point and avoids re-writing slots on restart.
- Test suite rewritten onto the unified API (mocked `lock_helpers` + `node.access_control`); covers readable/unreadable projection, capability mapping, created-vs-updated user derivation, typed duplicate → `DuplicateCodeError`, transient failure → `LockDisconnected`, credential-event push (incl. value-carrying events), partial-subscription cleanup, and a full LCM e2e lifecycle. Full suite: 1005 passing.

## Proposed change

Migrates the Matter lock provider onto Home Assistant's unified DoorLock credential API (`homeassistant.components.matter.lock_helpers`), implementing the `BaseLock` credential primitives from #1225. This is PR 5 of the credential-management refactor (parallels the zwave_js migration in #1227).

The provider now:
- Sets `supports_native_users = True` and implements `async_set_user` / `async_delete_user` / `async_set_credential` / `async_delete_credential` / `async_get_users` / `async_get_capabilities`, and **drops its `async_set_usercode` / `async_clear_usercode` / `async_get_usercodes` overrides** — the base orchestration drives set/clear/get.
- **Honors Matter's independent `user_index`**: Matter allocates the user index separately from the credential slot. `async_set_user` auto-allocates on create (`set_lock_user(user_index=None)`) and reuses the slot owner's index on update (from `get_lock_credential_status`), returning the real index so the base threads it into the credential write; the clear path resolves the owner from `async_get_users`.
- **PINs remain write-only** (occupied → `SlotCredential.unreadable()`); this is unchanged Matter behavior.
- **Duplicate detection** uses the typed `SetCredentialFailedError` (`status == "duplicate"`), preserving the sync-only clear-and-retry; direct sets raise `DuplicateCodeError`.
- **Optimistic push** on LCM-initiated writes (Matter doesn't emit `LockUserChange` for them); the DoorLock `LockOperation`/`LockUserChange` push handlers are kept for local changes.
- **Exception discipline:** `ServiceValidationError` → `CodeRejectedError`/`LockOperationFailed` (reachable); other `HomeAssistantError` → `LockDisconnected` (transport, retried).

## Type of change

- [ ] Dependency upgrade
- [ ] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix/feature causing existing functionality to break)
- [ ] Code quality improvements to existing code or addition of tests

## Additional information

- Depends on #1225 (merged). `hacs.json` already requires HA 2026.6.0 (#1221), where `matter.lock_helpers` shipped.
- Tests rewritten onto the unified API (mock the `lock_helpers` boundary + node); cover write-only projection, capability mapping, create-vs-update user_index allocation, typed duplicate (direct raise / sync retry-success / sync persistent), optimistic push, transport-vs-validation error mapping, and a full LCM e2e lifecycle through the real base orchestration. Full suite: 1032 passing.
