## Proposed change

Migrates the five slot-only lock providers — `virtual`, `zha`, `zigbee2mqtt`, `schlage`, `akuvox` — onto the `BaseLock` credential-primitive interface from #1225. This is PR 6 of the credential-management refactor (the "degenerate fixed point"), completing the provider layer alongside zwave_js (#1227) and matter (#1228).

These providers have **no native user concept**, so they keep `supports_native_users = False` (the default). The base orchestration then routes `async_set_usercode → async_set_credential(user_id=slot, …)` and `async_clear_usercode → async_delete_credential(ref)`, ignoring the user layer entirely. Each provider:
- implements `async_set_credential` (the old `async_set_usercode` body, using `credential.readable_pin`/`credential.slot`), `async_delete_credential` (old clear body, using `ref.slot`), and `async_get_users` (old `async_get_usercodes` dict wrapped via `user_from_slot`);
- drops the `async_set_usercode` / `async_clear_usercode` / `async_get_usercodes` overrides — the base orchestration + get-projection (which seeds empty managed slots) take over;
- preserves everything else: `zha`/`zigbee2mqtt` keep their optimistic `_push_credential_update` and push subscriptions; `schlage`/`akuvox` keep their `[LCM:<slot>]` tagging + setup; all keep `async_hard_refresh_codes`, connection/availability, and `supports_push`.

**Behavior is unchanged** — this is a pure refactor onto one interface. The `get → async_get_users → base projection` round-trip is lossless (`user_from_slot` then flatten is identity on the slot→state map), and empty-managed-slot / unmanaged-occupied handling is preserved.

## Type of change

- [ ] Dependency upgrade
- [ ] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix/feature causing existing functionality to break)
- [x] Code quality improvements to existing code or addition of tests

## Additional information

- Depends on #1225 (merged). Independent of #1227 (zwave_js) and #1228 (matter).
- Tests rewritten to drive the primitives + base orchestration end-to-end while keeping every legacy behavioral assertion (same device/store calls, same optimistic push, same known/empty/unreadable projection), plus new seam/projection coverage. Full suite: 1044 passing; ruff + providers mypy clean.

> DEVELOPER

for 1227, should we normalize what capabilities we get back from zwave_js and matter and hoist e.g. max length of name and stuff to the base?

> AGENT

Yes — there's real DRY to capture. The cleanest move is to make `LockCapabilities` the single source of truth and have providers stop caching the same fields a second time.

## What's redundant today

`zwave_js.py` has its own `_max_user_name_length: int | None` field, populated from `async_get_capabilities` and used in `async_set_user` for name truncation. But the value also lands in `BaseLock._capabilities_cache.max_user_name_length` via the same call. Two caches, one value. The provider field can go away — `async_set_user` reads `(await self._get_cached_capabilities()).max_user_name_length` and truncates from there. Matches what `_put_credential` already does for the gate.

## What could move to the base

**Name truncation.** Today it lives in `zwave_js.async_set_user`. The base could enforce it once for every native-user provider before calling `async_set_user`, by either:
- Truncating in `_put_credential` before threading `user` into `async_set_user`, or
- A small `_truncate_user_name(name) -> str | None` helper on `BaseLock` that providers can call (less invasive, providers still own the call site).

I'd lean toward the helper — it leaves provider-specific quirks (Matter Aqara U300 rejecting spaces, future ones we don't know about yet) at the call site to layer on top.

**Capability-derived gates.** The "should I do X" predicates that `_put_credential` already does (`supports_user_management AND max_user_name_length > 0`) could grow into a small property on `BaseLock`:

```python
@property
async def _supports_user_records(self) -> bool:
    caps = await self._get_cached_capabilities()
    return caps.supports_user_management and caps.max_user_name_length > 0
```

Useful when the sync-state expansion lands and the sync layer needs the same gate to decide whether to compare names at all.

## What should stay provider-specific

- Each provider's `async_get_capabilities` body — they map fundamentally different helper return shapes (`CredentialCapabilitiesResult` vs `GetLockInfoResult`) and you can't share that mapping.
- Per-provider quirk handling — Aqara U300's name-with-spaces rejection, future lock-firmware oddities. Those layer on top of the shared truncation.

## What I would NOT do yet

Avoid expanding `LockCapabilities` with fields nothing consumes today (Matter's `max_pin_users` vs `max_users` split, `max_credentials_per_user`, etc.). Add them when a base-orchestration consumer materializes — LCD aggregation, multi-credential-type entity sizing — not speculatively. Speculative fields invite providers to populate them inconsistently before there's a contract.

## Concrete proposal for PR 1227

Two-commit cleanup:

1. **Drop `zwave_js._max_user_name_length`** — replace reads with `(await self._get_cached_capabilities()).max_user_name_length`. Same behavior, one cache. Net negative LOC.
2. **Add `BaseLock._truncate_user_name`** — call from `zwave_js.async_set_user` (and `matter.async_set_user` for symmetry, even though Matter doesn't truncate today because its hardcoded 32 is always >= what we'd write).

The `_supports_user_records` property I'd hold for the sync-state expansion PR — it's the right home for it but there's no second caller today.

Want me to wire (1) and (2) into PR 1227, or hold them as fast-follows after merge? Either works; (1) is small enough that landing it in 1227 keeps the "we cache capabilities once" story complete in that PR.

  "new_string": "async def test_async_set_user_falls_back_when_capabilities_fetch_fails(\n    zwave_js_lock: ZWaveJSLock,\n    mock_access_control: MagicMock,\n    mock_lock_helpers: dict,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"\n    Caps-read failure drops the name for this call without poisoning the cache.\n\n    Failure surfaces as ``LockDisconnected``/``LockOperationFailed`` which the\n    base ``_truncate_user_name`` catches; the cache stays None so the next\n    call retries instead of pinning a 0 sentinel that would silently strip\n    all user names for the provider instance lifetime.\n    \"\"\"\n    mock_lock_helpers[\n        \"async_get_credential_capabilities\"\n    ].side_effect = FailedZWaveCommand(\"cmd\", 1, \"caps unavailable\")\n    mock_access_control.get_user_cached.return_value = None\n\n    user = User(user_id=1, name=\"alice\", active=True)\n    result = await zwave_js_lock.async_set_user(user)\n\n    assert result == SetUserResult(user_id=1, created=True)\n    assert zwave_js_lock._capabilities_cache is None\n    mock_lock_helpers[\"async_set_user\"].assert_called_once_with(\n        zwave_js_lock.node,\n        user_id=1,\n        user_name=None,\n        active=True,\n    )\n\n\nasync def test_async_set_user_retries_capabilities_after_failure(\n    zwave_js_lock: ZWaveJSLock,\n    mock_access_control: MagicMock,\n    mock_lock_helpers: dict,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"After a transient caps-fetch failure, the next call retries and the name lands.\"\"\"\n    mock_lock_helpers[\"async_get_credential_capabilities\"].side_effect = [\n        FailedZWaveCommand(\"cmd\", 1, \"caps unavailable\"),\n        {\n            \"max_user_name_length\": 10,\n            \"supports_user_management\": True,\n            \"max_users\": 5,\n            \"supported_credential_types\": {},\n        },\n    ]\n    mock_access_control.get_user_cached.return_value = None\n\n    # First call: caps fetch fails, name dropped, base cache stays unset.\n    await zwave_js_lock.async_set_user(User(user_id=1, name=\"alice\", active=True))\n    assert zwave_js_lock._capabilities_cache is None\n\n    # Second call: caps fetch retries, cache warms, name is now written.\n    await zwave_js_lock.async_set_user(User(user_id=2, name=\"bob\", active=True))\n    assert zwave_js_lock._capabilities_cache is not None\n    assert zwave_js_lock._capabilities_cache.max_user_name_length == 10\n    assert mock_lock_helpers[\"async_get_credential_capabilities\"].call_count == 2\n    last_call = mock_lock_helpers[\"async_set_user\"].call_args_list[-1]\n    assert last_call.kwargs[\"user_name\"] == \"bob\""

> AGENT

Pushed `ef4892ef` to PR 1227. Summary of what landed:

**Base hoists** (`BaseLock`):
- `_supports_user_records()` — `supports_user_management AND max_user_name_length > 0`. Currently called from `_put_credential` (replaces the inline predicate); future call site is the sync-state expansion when it needs to ask the same question.
- `_truncate_user_name(name)` — reads `_get_cached_capabilities()`, trims to `max_user_name_length`, returns `None` for implicit-user locks. Caps-fetch failure (`LockDisconnected`/`LockOperationFailed`) caught and falls back to `None` without poisoning the cache.

**zwave_js cleanup**:
- Dropped the redundant `_max_user_name_length: int | None` field and its lazy prime block in `async_set_user`.
- `async_set_user` now does `user_name = await self._truncate_user_name(user.name)` — one line replaces the previous capability-prime + length-check + truncate block.
- Dropped the unused `contextlib` import.

**Tests**:
- 7 new base-helper tests (`_supports_user_records` true/false matrix, `_truncate_user_name` within/over/zero/None/caps-fail paths).
- zwave_js retry-after-failure test now asserts against `_capabilities_cache` instead of the removed field.
- Full suite: 1030 → 1038 passing.

Net `-3` source LOC, all behavior preserved. PR 1227's "we cache capabilities once" story is now complete — the provider no longer keeps a shadow copy.

The Matter side already populates `max_user_name_length=32` (from the earlier PR 1228 commit), so when PR 1228 rebases on top of PR 1227 it gets `_supports_user_records` returning True for Matter for free. If you want Matter's `async_set_user` to also adopt `_truncate_user_name`, that's a one-line follow-up in PR 1228 — let me know and I'll wire it.

Rolls back a newly-created user when the credential\n        write fails so the lock isn't left with a credential-less user\n        the slot-keyed coordinator can't reconcile. Returns True if the\n        value changed.\n        \"\"\"\n        if await self._supports_user_records():\n            result = await self.async_set_user(user)\n            credential_user_id = result.user_id\n            rollback_user_id = result.user_id if result.created else None\n        else:\n            credential_user_id = user.user_id\n            rollback_user_id = None",
  "new_string": "    @final\n    async def _put_credential(\n        self,\n        user: User,\n        credential: Credential,\n        *,\n        name: str | None,\n        source: Literal[\"sync\", \"direct\"],\n    ) -> bool:\n        \"\"\"\n        Run the create-on-first user lifecycle around a credential write.\n\n        Native-user only (the slot adapters call the credential primitive\n        directly). Truncates ``user.name`` to the lock's advertised limit\n        before handing the user to the provider, so each provider's\n        ``async_set_user`` can write the name verbatim. Rolls back a\n        newly-created user when the credential write fails so the lock\n        isn't left with a credential-less user the slot-keyed coordinator\n        can't reconcile. Returns True if the value changed.\n        \"\"\"\n        if await self._supports_user_records():\n            truncated = await self._truncate_user_name(user.name)\n            user_for_write = (\n                user if truncated == user.name else replace(user, name=truncated)\n            )\n            result = await self.async_set_user(user_for_write)\n            credential_user_id = result.user_id\n            rollback_user_id = result.user_id if result.created else None\n        else:\n            credential_user_id = user.user_id\n            rollback_user_id = None"
}

  "old_string": "async def test_async_set_user_falls_back_when_capabilities_fetch_fails(\n    zwave_js_lock: ZWaveJSLock,\n    mock_access_control: MagicMock,\n    mock_lock_helpers: dict,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"\n    Caps-read failure drops the name for this call without poisoning the cache.\n\n    Failure surfaces as ``LockDisconnected``/``LockOperationFailed`` which the\n    base ``_truncate_user_name`` catches; the cache stays None so the next\n    call retries instead of pinning a 0 sentinel that would silently strip\n    all user names for the provider instance lifetime.\n    \"\"\"\n    mock_lock_helpers[\n        \"async_get_credential_capabilities\"\n    ].side_effect = FailedZWaveCommand(\"cmd\", 1, \"caps unavailable\")\n    mock_access_control.get_user_cached.return_value = None\n\n    user = User(user_id=1, name=\"alice\", active=True)\n    result = await zwave_js_lock.async_set_user(user)\n\n    assert result == SetUserResult(user_id=1, created=True)\n    assert zwave_js_lock._capabilities_cache is None\n    mock_lock_helpers[\"async_set_user\"].assert_called_once_with(\n        zwave_js_lock.node,\n        user_id=1,\n        user_name=None,\n        active=True,\n    )\n\n\nasync def test_async_set_user_retries_capabilities_after_failure(\n    zwave_js_lock: ZWaveJSLock,\n    mock_access_control: MagicMock,\n    mock_lock_helpers: dict,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"After a transient caps-fetch failure, the next call retries and the name lands.\"\"\"\n    mock_lock_helpers[\"async_get_credential_capabilities\"].side_effect = [\n        FailedZWaveCommand(\"cmd\", 1, \"caps unavailable\"),\n        {\n            \"max_user_name_length\": 10,\n            \"supports_user_management\": True,\n            \"max_users\": 5,\n            \"supported_credential_types\": {},\n        },\n    ]\n    mock_access_control.get_user_cached.return_value = None\n\n    # First call: caps fetch fails, name dropped, base cache stays unset.\n    await zwave_js_lock.async_set_user(User(user_id=1, name=\"alice\", active=True))\n    assert zwave_js_lock._capabilities_cache is None\n\n    # Second call: caps fetch retries, cache warms, name is now written.\n    await zwave_js_lock.async_set_user(User(user_id=2, name=\"bob\", active=True))\n    assert zwave_js_lock._capabilities_cache is not None\n    assert zwave_js_lock._capabilities_cache.max_user_name_length == 10\n    assert mock_lock_helpers[\"async_get_credential_capabilities\"].call_count == 2\n    last_call = mock_lock_helpers[\"async_set_user\"].call_args_list[-1]\n    assert last_call.kwargs[\"user_name\"] == \"bob\"\n\n\n",

Pushed `6c6904c6` to PR 1227. Net `-63` LOC overall.

Now the contract is:
- **Base** (`_put_credential`) — truncates `user.name` via `_truncate_user_name` before calling `async_set_user`. Uses `dataclasses.replace` so the caller's `User` isn't mutated.
- **Provider** (`async_set_user`) — receives a `User` with `name` already shaped to the lock's limit. Just writes it verbatim.

For Matter: PR 1228 already populates `LockCapabilities.max_user_name_length=32` from earlier. When it rebases on top of PR 1227's `6c6904c6`, `matter.async_set_user` automatically receives pre-truncated names — names longer than 32 bytes get trimmed at the seam without touching matter.py.

For future providers: zero work to pick up truncation. They just implement `async_set_user` to write `user.name` to the lock.

The 8 base helper tests (`_supports_user_records` matrix + `_truncate_user_name` matrix) still cover the helper directly; the end-to-end zwave_js test `test_async_set_usercode_truncates_name_to_lock_limit` verifies the seam wires through correctly. Full suite: 1036 passing.

> AGENT

Reviewed both PRs end-to-end. Here's the inventory.

## Hoists worth doing

**1. Base `async_setup` validates required capabilities.** Both providers do this manually today with different code paths:
- zwave_js: `await self._get_cached_capabilities()` (raises on no-CC)
- Matter: explicit `get_lock_info` call + checks for `supports_user_management` and `pin` in supported types

A base `async_setup` (gated on `supports_native_users`) could prime the cache and assert `CredentialType.PIN in caps.credential_types`. Subclasses call `super().async_setup()` then add their listener/push wiring. Saves ~10 lines in Matter, ~2 in zwave_js, and forces a uniform error message for "unmanageable lock."

**2. `_assert_credential_type_supported(credential)` defensive guard.** zwave_js's `async_set_credential` and `async_delete_credential` check `credential.type is CredentialType.PIN` and raise `CodeRejectedError`. Matter doesn't have the guard — Copilot didn't flag it because LCM's seam only sends PIN today, but it's the same defensive contract. A base helper:

```python
async def _assert_credential_type_supported(self, credential: Credential) -> None:
    caps = await self._get_cached_capabilities()
    if credential.type not in caps.credential_types:
        raise CodeRejectedError(
            code_slot=credential.slot,
            lock_entity_id=self.lock.entity_id,
            reason=f"unsupported credential type: {credential.type}",
        )
```

…lets zwave_js drop its hardcoded `is CredentialType.PIN` check (which becomes wrong the moment we add password support — zwave_js would silently reject valid passwords), and gives Matter the same guard for free. Adopts naturally to PASSWORD when capabilities advertise it. Symmetric helper for `CredentialRef` on the delete path.

## Hoists that look tempting but aren't

**3. Exception mapping (`ServiceValidationError → LockOperationFailed`, `HomeAssistantError → LockDisconnected`).** Both providers wrap helper calls in this pattern, but the directions are **inverse**:
- zwave_js maps `HomeAssistantError → LockOperationFailed` (HA error means the lock rejected)
- Matter maps `HomeAssistantError → LockDisconnected` (HA error means transport problem)

A generic wrapper would have to take the mapping as a parameter, at which point the call site is the same shape as today's `try/except`. No real win, and the inversion would actively mislead anyone reading the wrapper signature.

**4. `async_is_device_available` default.** Each provider has different "is it really available" semantics (matter probes `get_lock_info`, zwave_js checks `NodeStatus`). A base default like "call `async_get_capabilities` and return True/False" is technically possible but would weaken both providers' diagnostics. Skip.

**5. Orphan-owner guard in `async_set_user`.** Matter-specific — it's about Matter's auto-allocated `user_index`. zwave_js writes `user_id=slot` directly so it can't get into the "credential exists but no owner" state. Not portable.

**6. UPDATE-branch name-set failure tolerance.** Matter-specific to Matter's `set_lock_user` being a metadata-only write on UPDATE. zwave_js's `set_user` reads existing user from cache and either modifies (preserving credentials) or creates; failure means a real write failure, not metadata churn. Not portable.

**7. Cap-cache mirroring.** zwave_js used to have its own `_max_user_name_length` field — that's already done (`6c6904c6`). Matter never had a mirror cache. No more duplication to clean up.

## Things both providers should adopt that aren't on either yet

**8. `_assert_credential_ref_supported(ref)` for the delete path** (sibling of #2). zwave_js has `ref.type is CredentialType.PIN` inline; Matter has no check.

## What I'd land in PR 1227

- **#1** (base `async_setup` validates PIN support, gated on `supports_native_users`) — small, makes the setup contract uniform
- **#2 + #8** (`_assert_credential_type_supported(credential)` and `_assert_credential_ref_supported(ref)`) — defensive guards belong in the base; replaces zwave_js's hardcoded PIN check with a capability-driven one that automatically handles password expansion later

Matter would also drop its setup `get_lock_info` block + the redundant `supports_user_management`/PIN checks once PR 1228 rebases on PR 1227.

Want me to wire all three, or just #1 to keep PR 1227 from sprawling further?

> AGENT

My take on the rename: I'd keep `async_get_users`. The return type is `list[User]` and the `User` type owns its credentials — that's already in the domain model. Renaming would make the seam verb-ier without surfacing information the type signature doesn't already provide. We'd also have a consistency problem with `async_set_user` / `async_delete_user` (which write/delete the user record *and* its credentials per the lifecycle invariant) but don't carry `_and_credentials` in their names. The relationship between users and credentials is a property of the domain types, not a per-method qualifier.

That said, if you find the name actively confusing, I'll do the rename — it's mechanical (provider methods + tests + ARCHITECTURE.md). Let me know.

Now back to fixing PR 1228 — Matter's `async_setup` duplicates what the base now does:

> AGENT

Now the conftest imports the real constant.\n\n**How to apply:** when adding a new provider or credential type, the work is provider-specific only. Capability mapping (provider's `async_get_capabilities`) is the only place provider-specific logic lives. Everything else (type guards, name truncation, user-record gate, setup validation) inherits.\n\n**Naming convention** ([[feedback_base_helper_verb_consistency]]): base lifecycle helpers use the same verbs as primitives — `_set_credential`/`_delete_credential`, not `_put_credential`/`_drop_credential`.\n\n**Related**: [[project_pr1227_sync_state_design]] for the broader sync direction; [[project_zwave_credential_cc_abstraction]] for why this works transparently across User Credential CC and User Code CC; [[project_password_credential_expansion]] for what the type guards prepare for.\n"
}

## PR #1227 Summary

**Title:** feat(zwave_js): migrate to unified access_control credential API

**What it does:** This PR migrates the Z-Wave JS lock provider to Home Assistant's unified credential management system introduced in PR #1225. It drops legacy User Code Command Class operations and reads PIN values directly from `node.access_control`, enabling the sync loop to detect when lock state matches desired state and avoid re-writing slots on restart. The provider now transparently supports both User Credential CC (newer 700/800-series locks) and User Code CC (500-series) without regression. Capability-driven decisions—type checking, name truncation, user-record gating—are hoisted into `BaseLock` so future credential types and providers are additive.

**File scope:**
- Domain credentials type (new `max_user_name_length` field)
- Base orchestration (`BaseLock`: caching, validation, truncation, type projection)
- Z-Wave provider (reads from `access_control`, drops legacy CC operations, uses `lock_helpers`)
- Seam tests (unified API mocking)
- Z-Wave unit tests (rewritten onto `access_control` API; 1042 passing)

**Net LOC delta:** +2215 / −1510 = **+705 lines** (domain/base adds exceed provider reduction due to new capability hoists and expanded test coverage)

> DEVELOPER

how will a User Code CC lock behave immediately after this update. Consider PINs that are already in the correct state and ones that aren't

> AGENT

Let me trace this end-to-end for a User Code CC (500-series) lock.

## Setup path (both scenarios)

1. **Capability probe** — base `async_setup_internal` calls `_get_cached_capabilities()` → `async_get_capabilities()` → `lock_helpers.async_get_credential_capabilities(node)`. The driver's unified `accessControl` API works on UC; lock_helpers returns `supports_user_management=True` (hardcoded) and `credential_types={CredentialType.PIN: ...}` (driver advertises PIN-only with the lock's actual slot count + min/max length). `max_user_name_length=0` (UC has no names).
2. Base validation passes (`supports_user_management` ✓, PIN in credential_types ✓). Provider's `async_setup` registers listeners. Push subscription wires the three credential events (`added` / `modified` / `deleted`).
3. **Coordinator first refresh** calls `async_get_usercodes` → `_project_users_to_slots(PIN)` → `async_get_users()`. The driver's UC backend has historically held the PIN values readably (User Code CC value-reports include the data), so `node.access_control.get_users_cached()` + `get_all_credentials_cached()` return synthetic users (slot N ↔ user_id N) with PIN credentials carrying the actual values.

## Scenario A: PINs already in correct state

- `_project_users_to_slots(PIN)` returns the same dict the coordinator would build from config — `{slot N: SlotCredential.known("1234")}` for occupied slots, `SlotCredential.empty()` for managed-but-empty slots.
- Sync compares desired vs actual, sees match per slot, **issues no writes**. Lock stays silent.
- This is the key win over LCM 1.x — the readable PIN gives the sync a fixed point, so existing codes carry over with zero churn on upgrade.

## Scenario B: PIN mismatch (config changed, or out-of-band edit)

Per-slot, sync calls `async_set_usercode(slot, pin, name)`:

1. Seam builds `credential_from_slot(slot, SlotCredential.known(pin))` and `user_from_slot(slot, ...)`.
2. `supports_native_users=True` → routes to base `_set_credential`.
3. `_assert_credential_type_supported(credential)` → PIN is supported, passes.
4. **`_supports_user_records()` returns False** on UC (`max_user_name_length == 0`). So the base **skips `async_set_user`** entirely, addresses the credential by `user.user_id` (which equals the slot), and goes straight to `async_set_credential`.
5. Provider calls `lock_helpers.async_set_credential(node, user_id=slot, PIN_CODE, pin, credential_slot=slot)`. Inside the driver's `accessControl` API, this dispatches to the legacy UC `set_usercode` (the same primitive LCM 1.x used). Lock accepts the PIN.
6. Driver fires `"credential added"` or `"credential modified"` from inside the API call. Push handler picks it up, `args.data` is the actual PIN, `_push_credential_update(slot, SlotCredential.known(pin))` lands on the coordinator. Sync now sees match, stops writing.

For a clear (`async_clear_usercode(slot)`):

1. Resolves the owner from `async_get_users` (synthetic UC user at slot).
2. Calls base `_delete_credential(owner, ref)` → `_assert_credential_ref_supported` passes → `async_delete_credential(ref)`.
3. Driver's UC backend clears the code and **fires BOTH `"credential deleted"` AND `"user deleted"`** in the same call (UC ties them: the user IS the code).
4. Base sees `was_only_credential=True` and calls `async_delete_user(owner.user_id)` to finish the lifecycle.
5. UC has already implicitly deleted the user when the credential cleared; the driver's `deleteUser` for UC returns `Error_Unknown` because the cache shows `existed=False`. `lock_helpers.async_delete_user` raises HomeAssistantError; provider maps to `LockOperationFailed`; base's `_delete_credential` catches in its existing best-effort handler and **logs a warning** ("cleared the credential at slot N but failed to remove the now-empty user"). The clear itself succeeds; coordinator gets the empty push.

## Edge cases / things to know

- **No regression for the most common case** (PINs already match) — zero writes, lock undisturbed.
- **Names are silently dropped** on UC because `_supports_user_records()` is False, so the base never calls `async_set_user`. LCM 1.x behaved the same; nothing to lose here.
- **The "user already deleted" warning on every clear** is the one real piece of noise. It's harmless (the user is supposed to be gone, the slot is cleared, the coordinator is updated correctly), but every clear on a UC lock will log one WARNING. Worth either suppressing on UC specifically or downgrading the level for the implicit-user case.
- **Fresh lock (no existing codes)**: `async_get_users` returns `[]`, projection produces all-empty for managed slots, sync writes each configured PIN — same as scenario B per slot.
- **The driver's `_pin_state(data)` for UC events**: UC's credential-changed events carry the actual `data`, so push handlers always land with `SlotCredential.known(value)`. No "0000" disambiguation needed — UC events only fire for actual mutations (driver doesn't synthesize spurious events on read).

Net: **scenario A is silent and clean; scenario B works correctly with one warning-level log line per clear**. The only fast-follow worth considering before merge is suppressing/demoting the "couldn't delete user" warning on implicit-user locks, since it's expected behavior, not an anomaly.

> DEVELOPER

we shouldn't have that warning if there's nothing to set

> AGENT

Right — symmetry with `_set_credential` (which skips `async_set_user` when `_supports_user_records()` is False, the credential write creates the user implicitly). On the delete side, the credential delete already removed the user implicitly, so there's nothing to delete and the cleanup call is bogus. Gate it the same way.

Mirrors ``_set_credential``'s\n    ``_supports_user_records()`` gate on the set side.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    class _ImplicitUserStubLock(_NativeStubLock):\n        async def async_get_capabilities(self) -> LockCapabilities:\n            # supports_user_management True (hardcoded by the driver for\n            # all Z-Wave locks), max_user_name_length 0 (UC has no\n            # names) -- the implicit-user signal.\n            return LockCapabilities(\n                supports_user_management=True,\n                max_users=30,\n                credential_types={\n                    CredentialType.PIN: CredentialTypeCapability(\n                        num_slots=30,\n                        min_length=4,\n                        max_length=8,\n                        supports_learn=False,\n                    ),\n                },\n                max_user_name_length=0,\n            )\n\n    lock = _make_lock(hass, _ImplicitUserStubLock, \"seam_clear_implicit_user\")\n    # Seed the lock with a credential at slot 3 via the seam (set path\n    # also skips async_set_user, exercising the symmetric gate).\n    await lock.async_set_usercode(3, \"9999\")\n    # Seed an implicit user so the owner-resolution path finds something\n    # to delete; on a real UC lock the user is created by the credential\n    # write inside the driver.\n    lock._users[3] = User(\n        user_id=3,\n        credentials=[credential_from_slot(3, SlotCredential.known(\"9999\"))],\n    )\n    lock.calls.clear()\n\n    changed = await lock.async_clear_usercode(3)\n\n    assert changed is True\n    # delete_credential ran; delete_user did NOT.\n    assert lock.calls == [(\"delete_credential\", 3, 3)]"
}

> AGENT

Pushed `d9de57dd` to PR 1227.

`_delete_credential` now mirrors `_set_credential`'s `_supports_user_records()` gate — on implicit-user locks (UC, and any future provider where the user is implicit in the credential), the cleanup `async_delete_user` call is skipped entirely. No more spurious warning per clear on 500-series Z-Wave locks. Native-user path (Matter, U3C) is unchanged.

Test added: `test_clear_usercode_implicit_user_skips_delete_user` — synthetic provider with `max_user_name_length=0` confirms `delete_credential` ran and `delete_user` did NOT.

Full suite: 1043 passing, pre-commit clean.

Transport-level failures\n        (``LockDisconnected``/``LockOperationFailed``) during the\n        capability probe OR the provider's own ``async_setup`` are logged\n        and the coordinator is created anyway so the integration retries\n        once the lock comes online.\n        \"\"\"\n        self._lcm_config_entry = config_entry\n        try:\n            if self.supports_native_users:\n                caps = await self._get_cached_capabilities()\n                if not caps.supports_user_management:\n                    raise LockCodeManagerProviderError(\n                        f\"{self.lock.entity_id}: lock does not support user management\"\n                    )\n                if CredentialType.PIN not in caps.credential_types:\n                    raise LockCodeManagerProviderError(\n                        f\"{self.lock.entity_id}: lock does not advertise PIN credential support\"\n                    )\n            await self.async_setup(config_entry)\n        except (LockDisconnected, LockOperationFailed) as err:\n            LOGGER.warning(\n                \"Provider setup failed for %s: %s. 	/**
	 * Deletes the given credential.
	 * This communicates with the node.
	 */
	public async deleteCredential(
		userId: number,
		type: UserCredentialType,
		slot: number,
	): Promise<SetCredentialResult> {
		if (this.#usesUserCredentialCC) {
			this.#assertValidSlot(type, slot);

			const api = this.#u3cAPI();
			const raw = await api.setCredential({
				operationType: UserCredentialOperationType.Delete,
				userId,
				credentialType: type,
				credentialSlot: slot,
			});
			if (raw) await this.endpoint.tryGetNode()?.handleCommand(raw);
			return u3cCredentialReportTypeToSetCredentialResult(
				raw?.reportType,
			);
		} else {
			// User Code CC stores exactly one credential per user slot. Ignore the
			// caller-provided unified slot and write back to the owning user's slot
			// so events and cached state stay internally consistent.
			this.#assertValidSlot(type, userId);
			const existed = this.#getCredentialCached_UC(
				type,
				userId,
			) != undefined;
			const api = this.#ucAPI();
			const result = await api.clear(userId);
			let succeeded: boolean;
			if (result == undefined) {
				const verified = await api.get(userId);
				succeeded = existed
					&& verified?.userIdStatus === UserIDStatus.Available;
			} else {
				succeeded = supervisedCommandSucceeded(result) && existed;
			}
			if (succeeded) {
				const node = this.endpoint.tryGetNode();
				if (node) {
					node.emit("credential deleted", this.endpoint as any, {
						userId,
						credentialType: type,
						credentialSlot: userId,
					});
					node.emit("user deleted", this.endpoint as any, { userId });
				}
			}
			return succeeded
				? SetCredentialResult.OK
				: SetCredentialResult.Error_Unknown;
		}
	}

export class UserCodeCCExtendedUserCodeSet extends UserCodeCC {
	public constructor(
		options: WithAddress<UserCodeCCExtendedUserCodeSetOptions>,

	public static from(
		raw: CCRaw,
		ctx: CCParsingContext,
	): UserCodeCCExtendedUserCodeSet {
		validatePayload(raw.payload.length >= 1);
		const numCodes = raw.payload[0];
		let offset = 1;
		const userCodes: UserCodeCCSetOptions[] = [];

		// Parse each user code
		for (let i = 0; i < numCodes; i++) {
			validatePayload(raw.payload.length >= offset + 4);
			const userId = raw.payload.readUInt16BE(offset);
			const userIdStatus: UserIDStatus = raw.payload[offset + 2];
			const codeLength = raw.payload[offset + 3];
			validatePayload(raw.payload.length >= offset + 4 + codeLength);

			if (userIdStatus === UserIDStatus.Available) {
				userCodes.push({
					userId,
					userIdStatus,
				});
			} else {
				const userCodeBuffer = raw.payload.subarray(
					offset + 4,
					offset + 4 + codeLength,

				const userCodeString = userCodeBuffer.toString("utf8");
				const userCode = isPrintableASCII(userCodeString)

				userCodes.push({
					userId,
					userIdStatus,
					userCode,
				} as UserCodeCCSetOptions);
			}

			offset += 4 + codeLength;
		}

> AGENT

Got it. Traced root cause: it's in **node-zwave-js**, specifically the `accessControl.deleteCredential` UC path. Here's the diff:

**Legacy LCM path (User Code CC value-set):**
- `clear_usercode` calls `node.async_set_value(LOCK_USERCODE_STATUS_PROPERTY, AVAILABLE)` — sets the `userIdStatus` value property directly.
- The driver's value-DB layer treats this as a paired update: setting `userIdStatus = Available` also normalizes the paired `userCode` value to the sentinel `"0000"`.
- zwave-js-ui reads the value DB and sees `userCode = "0000"`, `userIdStatus = Available` → slot renders as "Available 0000".

**New LCM path (unified accessControl):**
- `lock_helpers.async_delete_credential` calls `node.access_control.deleteCredential(...)` → driver's `AccessControlAPI.deleteCredential` UC branch → `api.clear(userId)`.
- `api.clear` sends `UserCodeCCExtendedUserCodeSet` (V2+) or `UserCodeCCSet` (V1) with `userIdStatus = Available` and **no `userCode` field**.
- The Extended-Set serialization (packages/cc/src/cc/UserCodeCC.ts) explicitly writes `code-length = 0` and zero-length code bytes for `Available` status (`userCode?.length ?? 0`).
- The driver fires `"credential deleted"` and `"user deleted"` events directly — it does NOT round-trip through the value-DB update that the legacy property-set path triggered.
- Result: `userCode` value stays whatever it was (often `undefined`), `userIdStatus = Available`. zwave-js-ui sees no value and hides the slot.

LCM doesn't cause this — same `accessControl.deleteCredential` call from any client produces the same result. It's an asymmetry between two driver code paths in node-zwave-js: the legacy property-set path normalizes paired values, the new event-emitting `accessControl` path does not.

**Where to file:** node-zwave-js. The fix is likely in `AccessControlAPI.deleteCredential`'s UC branch — after `api.clear(userId)` succeeds, also clear the paired `userCode` value in the value DB (or have the UC clear unconditionally set it to `"00000000"` to match legacy behavior, since that's what zwave-js-ui and other downstream consumers expect for an Available slot).

A minimal repro for the upstream issue:
```js
// On a UC lock with a code at slot 1:
await node.access_control.deleteCredential(1, UserCredentialType.PIN_CODE, 1);
// vs the legacy path:
const value = { commandClass: CommandClasses["User Code"], property: "userIdStatus", propertyKey: 1 };
await node.setValue(value, UserIDStatus.Available);
// Compare value DB state for the paired userCode property after each.
```

Both succeed at the lock level; only the legacy path leaves the value DB in the shape zwave-js-ui expects.

If you want, I can write that up as a node-zwave-js issue with the trace I just did. The fix is one-sided (upstream), so there's nothing for LCM to do beyond noting it in release notes if a meaningful share of users will hit this.

Causes zwave-js-ui to hide slots after LCM 2.x credential delete on User Code CC locks.\nmetadata:\n  type: project\n---\n\nUser-observed bug, traced 2026-06-10 while testing PR #1227 on a User Code CC (500-series) lock. **The bug is upstream in node-zwave-js, not in LCM.**\n\n**Observation:** After LCM 2.x triggers a credential delete on a UC lock, the affected slot disappears from the zwave-js-ui interface. The freshly-deleted slot shows `userCode = undefined`.\n\n**Root cause** (traced through node-zwave-js v15.23.4):\n\nThe two code paths produce different value-DB state after clearing a UC slot:\n\n1. **Legacy path (LCM 1.x and zwave-js-ui's own \"clear\" button)** — `zwave_js_server/util/lock.py:clear_usercode` calls `node.async_set_value(userIdStatus, AVAILABLE)`. This goes through the driver's value-DB property setter, which has special-cased paired-update logic: setting `userIdStatus = Available` also writes the paired `userCode` value to the `\"0000\"` sentinel.\n\n2. **New unified path (LCM 2.x via PR #1227)** — `lock_helpers.async_delete_credential` calls `node.access_control.deleteCredential(...)` → driver's `AccessControlAPI.deleteCredential` UC branch → `api.clear(userId)`. `api.clear` sends `UserCodeCCExtendedUserCodeSet` (V2+) or `UserCodeCCSet` (V1) with `userIdStatus = Available` and **no `userCode` field**. The serializer writes `code-length = 0` and zero-length code bytes (`code.userCode?.length ?? 0`). The driver fires `\"credential deleted\"` and `\"user deleted\"` events directly — it does NOT update the paired `userCode` value DB entry, so it remains `undefined`.\n\n**File and line refs in node-zwave-js (v15.23.4):**\n- `packages/zwave-js/src/lib/node/feature-apis/AccessControl.ts` — `AccessControlAPI.deleteCredential` UC branch (around L953-1010).\n- `packages/cc/src/cc/UserCodeCC.ts` — `UserCodeCCAPI.clear` (V2+ branch uses `setMany` with no `userCode`) and `UserCodeCCExtendedUserCodeSet.serialize` (writes length=0 and empty bytes when `userCode` is undefined).\n\n**Upstream fix direction:** in `AccessControlAPI.deleteCredential`'s UC branch, after `api.clear(userId)` succeeds, also clear the paired `userCode` value DB entry (or have UC clear unconditionally set it to `\"00000000\"` to match the legacy path's observable state).\n\n**Workaround in LCM:** none reasonable. # Instructions for GitHub Copilot

> **Note for AI assistants:** `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` are symlinks pointing to this file (`.github/copilot-instructions.md`). Always edit this file directly, never the symlinks, or they will be replaced with regular files and break.

This repository holds the Z-Wave JS driver library, a TypeScript implementation of a Z-Wave controller software stack and supporting tools.

## Project structure

- The `packages/` directory contains all of the packages in this monorepo.
  - `packages/zwave-js`: The main driver library (name: `zwave-js`)
  - `packages/shared`: Internal utilities shared between packages (name: `@zwave-js/shared`)
  - `packages/core`: Core definitions, utilities and types used by other packages and applications (name: `@zwave-js/core`)
  - `packages/cc`: Command Class definitions and implementations (name: `@zwave-js/cc`)
  - `packages/config`: Functionality related to device configuration and all configuration files (name: `@zwave-js/config`)
  - `packages/eslint-plugin`: A custom ESLint plugin, used internally throughout the project (name: `@zwave-js/eslint-plugin`)
  - `packages/flash`: Command-line based Z-Wave firmware flashing tool (name: `@zwave-js/flash`)
  - `packages/host`: Host abstractions layer for integration tests (name: `@zwave-js/host`)
  - `packages/nvmedit`: Utilities and a command-line tool for editing the contents of Z-Wave controller memory/NVM (name: `@zwave-js/nvmedit`)
  - `packages/serial`: Serial port abstraction and Serial API message implementation (name: `@zwave-js/serial`)
  - `packages/testing`: Utilities for testing (name: `@zwave-js/testing`)
  - `packages/transformers`: Plugins for the TypeScript compiler used to auto-generate code at build time (name: `@zwave-js/transformers`)
- Device configuration files are located in `packages/config/config/devices` and have a `.json` extension.

## Tools and Tasks

- Build the entire project: `yarn build`
- Build a specific package: `yarn build <package-name>`, e.g. `yarn build zwave-js` or `yarn build @zwave-js/cc`
- Run tests: `yarn test:ts`
- Run tests for a specific file: `yarn test:ts <file>`
- Format all code: `yarn fmt`
- Check configuration files for semantic errors: `yarn lint:zwave`
- Detect and fix linting issues in TypeScript code: `yarn lint:ts:fix`
- Prefer built-in tools for finding files (e.g. `Grep`) over shell commands like `find`, `ls`, `grep`, `xargs`, to ensure cross-platform compatibility.

## Common Guidelines

- All code and comments and other text are written in American English
- Follow existing code style patterns as much as possible
- Prefer `async`/`await` over callbacks and Promises wherever possible
- After making code changes, always run `yarn fmt` to fix the formatting

## Common Guidelines

- All code and comments and other text are written in American English
- Follow existing code style patterns as much as possible
- Prefer `async`/`await` over callbacks and Promises wherever possible
- After making code changes, always run `yarn fmt` to fix the formatting
- Do not preserve backwards compatibility (e.g., keeping unused methods, re-exporting removed types, renaming to `_unused`) unless explicitly asked. When refactoring or iterating on new features, remove unused code completely.
- In comments, never mention things you replaced or removed

## Commenting Style

Comments should explain the WHY, not the WHAT. The code itself shows what happens; comments should explain why that approach was chosen or what it achieves in context.

**When to write comments:**

- Non-obvious algorithmic decisions or workarounds
- Protocol-specific behavior or constraints (e.g., "These fields are only available for Z-Wave LR")
- References to specifications (e.g., "Implementation based on SDS13782")
- Edge cases, gotchas, or assumptions that aren't evident from code
- Complex conditional logic where the reasoning matters

**When NOT to write comments:**

- Self-explanatory code (prefer clear naming over comments)
- Describing what the next line does
--
## Testing

- Use `vitest` for testing.
- Unit tests must be located next to the code they test, but with a `.test.ts` extension instead of `.ts`.
- Do not create tests for functionality that interacts with (mock) devices, unless specifically instructed to do so.
- Do not create tests when you are assigned a Github issue to fix, unless specifically instructed to do so.

function persistUserCode(
	this: UserCodeCC,
	ctx: GetValueDB & GetSupportedCCVersion,
	userId: number,
	userIdStatus: UserIDStatus,
	userCode: string | Bytes,
) {
	const statusValue = UserCodeCCValues.userIdStatus(userId);
	const codeValue = UserCodeCCValues.userCode(userId);

	// Check if this code is supported
	if (userIdStatus === UserIDStatus.StatusNotAvailable) {
		// It is not, remove all values if any exist
		this.removeValue(ctx, statusValue);
		this.removeValue(ctx, codeValue);
		this.removeMetadata(ctx, statusValue);
		this.removeMetadata(ctx, codeValue);
	} else {
		// Always create metadata in case it does not exist
		setUserCodeMetadata.call(this, ctx, userId, userCode);
		this.setValue(ctx, statusValue, userIdStatus);
		this.setValue(ctx, codeValue, userCode);
	}

	return true;
}

1501		public static from(raw: CCRaw, ctx: CCParsingContext): UserCodeCCReport {
1502			validatePayload(raw.payload.length >= 2);
1503			const userId = raw.payload[0];
1504			const userIdStatus: UserIDStatus = raw.payload[1];
1505			let userCode: string | Bytes;
1506	
1507			if (
1508				raw.payload.length === 2
1509				&& (userIdStatus === UserIDStatus.Available
1510					|| userIdStatus === UserIDStatus.StatusNotAvailable)
1511			) {
1512				// The user code is not set or not available and this report contains no user code
1513				userCode = "";
1514			} else {
1515				// The specs require the user code to be at least 4 digits
1516				validatePayload(raw.payload.length >= 6);
1517	
1518				let userCodeBuffer = raw.payload.subarray(2);
1519				// Specs say infer user code from payload length, manufacturers send zero-padded strings
1520				while (userCodeBuffer.at(-1) === 0) {
1521					userCodeBuffer = userCodeBuffer.subarray(0, -1);
1522				}
1523				// Specs say ASCII 0-9, manufacturers don't care :)
1524				// Thus we check if the code is printable using ASCII, if not keep it as a Buffer
1525				const userCodeString = userCodeBuffer.toString("utf8");
1526				if (isPrintableASCII(userCodeString)) {
1527					userCode = userCodeString;
1528				} else if (isPrintableASCIIWithWhitespace(userCodeString)) {
1529					// Ignore leading and trailing whitespace in V1 reports if the rest is ASCII
1530					userCode = userCodeString.trim();
1531				} else {
1532					userCode = userCodeBuffer;
1533				}
1534			}
1535	
1536			return new this({
1537				nodeId: ctx.sourceNodeId,
1538				userId,
1539				userIdStatus,

1541			});

> AGENT

Found the real bug. The UC branch's `#purgeCachedUserCodes(targetUserId)` at line 1198 **removes** both userIdStatus and userCode values from the value DB. That's the asymmetry — the legacy `setValue` path uses `verifyChanges` → `schedulePoll` → Get → Report → `persistUserCode` which **rewrites** them with `Available`/`""`. zwave-js-ui renders slot rows from value-DB entries, so removed entries = disappeared row.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- For UC locks (User Code CC), slots are permanently reserved 1..N — clearing means "Available", not "gone". The new accessControl unified API treats credentials as ephemeral objects (UC3 model) and the purge reflects that, but it semantically mismatches UC where the slot persists.
- The setCredential UC branch (line 1075+) also doesn't write to the value DB on success — it just emits an event. So the value DB on UC locks is increasingly driven by Reports rather than Sets in the new API, but `deleteCredential` actively *removes* entries, which is the only "destructive" value-DB action on the success path.
- The fix is to stop purging in the UC branch and instead persist the cleared state (`Available`/`""`), which is what `persistUserCode` would write if we let the Report come back.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Before writing the fix, a design question worth surfacing to you:

**Two fix options:**

| Option | Change | Trade-off |
|---|---|---|
| **A** — Remove purge from UC branch, rely on existing `api.get()` + Report to persist | Smaller diff; still requires post-clear Get even on supervised success | Adds a Get round-trip when supervision succeeded |
| **B** — Remove purge from UC branch, directly write `Available`/`""` to value DB on success (no extra Get) | Matches what `persistUserCode` writes; no extra network traffic | More direct value-DB manipulation outside the CC code |

# Changelog
[Older changelog entries (v1...v12)](CHANGELOG_v12.md)

<!--
	Add placeholder for next release with `wip` snippet
-->
## 15.24.2 (2026-06-01)
### Bugfixes
* Verify new state after Protection CC Set (#8831)
* Add the missing possibility of adding users and credentials together in one call through the unified credential management API on devices using User Code CC (#8837)
* Fixed an issue where bulk deletion of users and credentials would purge the cache after issuing the deletion event, causing applications to read stale data (#8829)
* Work around an issue with some controllers that could not enter inclusion mode because the SUC was missing from the network (#8842)

### Config file changes
* Add lifeline association and remove Binary Switch CC for iBlinds v2 (#8830)
* Add new fingerprint for Honeywell TH6320ZW2007 (#8841)

### Changes under the hood
* Speed up typed documentation generation process (#8843)

## 15.24.0 (2026-05-12)
### Features
* Implement bulk-delete APIs for credentials (#8793)

### Config file changes
* Map Basic Set to Binary Sensor for Fibaro FGMS001 (#8765)

## 15.23.5 (2026-04-27)
### Bugfixes
* Fixed an issue where the response after setting a duplicate PIN would not be properly matched to the controlling command, causing a timeout (#8761)

### Config file changes
* Update parameters for Zooz ZSE44 firmware 2.40 (#8759)

## 15.23.4 (2026-04-22)
Changed the names of result-type enums on the `endpoint.accessControl` API from `...Status` to `...Result`

## 15.23.3 (2026-04-22)
This release continues to iterate on the new `endpoint.accessControl` API:
* Credential slots are considered global per device, not user specific.
* Set-type credential management methods return specific error types that give more information about what failed.

### Bugfixes
* Fixed an issue where connection to encrypted ESPHome Z-Wave proxies would fail when unrelated commands were received during the handshake (#8721)
* Interviewed Notification CC capabilities are no longer overwritten when applying alarm mappings (#8755)

### Config file changes
* Add Philio PAC03 Mitsubishi IT adapter (#8748)

## 15.23.2 (2026-04-15)

    fix: persist cleared User Code CC slot in value DB after deleteCredential

    userIdStatus and userCode value DB entries on success, removing the
    slot entirely. User Code CC reserves a permanent slot per user
    identifier, so the post-clear state is a slot in the Available state
    with an empty code, not a missing slot. Persist that state explicitly
    so downstream consumers (e.g. UIs that render slots from the value
    DB) keep showing the cleared slot rather than dropping the row.

{
  "command": "cd /Users/raman/projects/node-zwave-js && gh pr create --repo zwave-js/node-zwave-js --base master --head raman325:fix/uc-delete-credential-value-db --title \"fix: persist cleared User Code CC slot in value DB after deleteCredential\" --body \"$(cat <<'EOF'\n### What\n\nOn a successful clear via \\`endpoint.accessControl.deleteCredential(...)\\` against a User Code CC node, the UC branch calls \\`#purgeCachedUserCodes(targetUserId)\\`, which removes both the \\`userIdStatus\\` and \\`userCode\\` value DB entries for that slot.\n\n[\\`AccessControl.ts\\`#L1197-L1199](https://github.com/zwave-js/node-zwave-js/blob/b06736492a5cf7e7f8a4ed18d188e0f17fee9527/packages/zwave-js/src/lib/node/feature-apis/AccessControl.ts#L1197-L1199):\n\n```ts\nif (succeeded) {\n    this.#purgeCachedUserCodes(targetUserId);\n}\n```\n\n\\`#purgeCachedUserCodes\\` calls \\`valueDB.removeValue(vid)\\` for both the status and code values.\n\n### Why this is wrong\n\nUser Code CC reserves a fixed number of slots (1..N), one per user identifier. Clearing a slot doesn't make the slot go away — it moves the slot to the \\`Available\\` state with an empty code. The slot is still there and can be filled again later.\n\nThe legacy property-set path (\\`UserCodeCCAPI[SET_VALUE]\\` for \\`userIdStatus = Available\\`) ultimately ends up with the slot persisted as \\`userIdStatus = Available\\` and \\`userCode = \"\"\\` in the value DB, because of the \\`verifyChanges\\` hook in \\`UserCodeCCAPI[SET_VALUE_HOOKS]\\` that schedules a poll → Get → Report → \\`persistUserCode\\` writes both values.\n\nThe new \\`accessControl.deleteCredential\\` path skips that and actively *removes* the entries instead. The effect is observable to value-DB consumers: zwave-js-ui renders slots from value-DB entries, so after a delete via this API, the slot row disappears from its UI entirely (rather than showing as Available like every other cleared slot).\n\nThe neighboring \\`setCredential\\` UC branch does not purge or rewrite value-DB entries on success — it just emits an event. Only the \\`deleteCredential\\` UC branch performs this destructive value-DB action, and it's the source of the asymmetry.\n\n### The fix\n\nStop purging in the UC branch. After a successful clear, write the post-clear state explicitly into the value DB:\n\n* \\`userIdStatus(targetUserId)\\` → \\`UserIDStatus.Available\\`\n* \\`userCode(targetUserId)\\` → \\`\"\"\\`\n\nThis mirrors what \\`persistUserCode\\` would write if a Report came back via Get, but without forcing an extra Get round-trip on supervised success.\n\n### How this was found\n\nEncountered while testing [\\`lock_code_manager\\`](https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager) 2.x against a 500-series UC lock + zwave-js-ui. LCM 2.x routes credential deletes through \\`accessControl.deleteCredential\\` (instead of the legacy property-set path used by LCM 1.x), and the affected slot disappears from zwave-js-ui after each delete. Other cleared slots remain visible.\n\n### Verification\n\n* \\`yarn test:ts -- accessControl.UserCode.test.ts\\` → 28/28 pass\n* \\`yarn test:ts -- accessControl.UserCredential.test.ts\\` → 30/30 pass (U3C path untouched)\n* \\`oxlint --type-aware\\` clean\n* \\`dprint check\\` clean\n* The first commit is just \\`yarn run sync-references\\` output (\\`packages/cc/tsconfig.build.json\\`); the actual fix is in the second commit.\nEOF\n)\" 2>&1 | tail -3",

}

> AGENT

PR opened: **[zwave-js/zwave-js#8866](https://github.com/zwave-js/zwave-js/pull/8866)** — "fix: persist cleared User Code CC slot in value DB after deleteCredential"

Summary of what changed:

- **The bug**: `accessControl.deleteCredential` UC branch called `#purgeCachedUserCodes(targetUserId)` on success, which `valueDB.removeValue`s both `userIdStatus` and `userCode` entries — making the slot disappear from any UI that renders slots from value-DB entries (zwave-js-ui).
- **The fix** ([AccessControl.ts:1197-1232](https://github.com/zwave-js/zwave-js/pull/8866/files)): replace the purge with explicit writes of `userIdStatus = Available` and `userCode = ""`, mirroring what `persistUserCode` would write if a Get/Report came back. No extra network round-trip on supervised success.
- **PR structure**: 2 commits — `chore: sync project references` (forced by pre-commit hook because `packages/cc/tsconfig.build.json` was missing the `transformers` reference on upstream/master) and the actual fix commit.
- **Verification**: 28/28 UC tests pass, 30/30 U3C tests pass (untouched), oxlint + dprint clean.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- Value-DB writes are not just internal driver state — they're the wire protocol between zwave-js and every downstream consumer (zwave-js-ui, zwave-js-server). Removing vs setting entries is a meaningfully different API contract, so UC's "permanent slot" semantics had to be encoded in how we leave the value DB after a clear.
- The maintainer may push back and argue the purge was deliberate ("credentials are objects, slots are an implementation detail of UC"). If so, the cleanest counter is that `setCredential` UC branch doesn't purge either, so the destructive asymmetry only exists on delete — making it look like an oversight in the UC branch rather than a design statement.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

980	    async def _project_users_to_slots(
981	        self, credential_type: CredentialType
982	    ) -> dict[int, SlotCredential]:
983	        """
984	        Project the lock's users to a slot -> ``SlotCredential`` map.
985	
986	        Every managed slot is present even when empty: the projection
987	        starts from ``managed_slots`` mapped to ``SlotCredential.empty()``
988	        and then overlays the credentials of ``credential_type`` read via
989	        ``async_get_users``. This preserves the slot-keyed contract the
990	        coordinator, sync manager, and slot entities depend on -- a
991	        managed slot missing from the map is treated as unavailable, not
992	        empty, so the empty placeholders are load-bearing. Occupied slots
993	        the lock reports that are not managed are surfaced too.
994	        Credentials of other types are dropped here -- the seam keeps
995	        everything below it slot-shaped and single-type this round.
996	
997	        This is the chokepoint for "the base class filters per credential
998	        type before passing to the coordinator/entities" (Option A in the
999	        design discussion). Adding a second supported type means calling
1000	        this helper from a second projection method -- providers store
1001	        every type they can map, so no provider changes are required.
1002	
1003	        TODO(option-b): when the integration adds a second supported
1004	        credential type (Z-Wave User Credential CC also exposes
1005	        ``PASSWORD``), revisit whether the coordinator/entities should
1006	        instead be type-scoped from the top -- one set of slot entities
1007	        per credential type -- rather than threading the type through a
1008	        single projection. The provider-side model is already ready for
1009	        that move; the open question is configuration / user experience
1010	        (do users configure "PIN slots 1-10" and "password slots 1-5"
1011	        separately, or is each slot polymorphic?).
1012	        """
1013	        codes = {slot: SlotCredential.empty() for slot in self.managed_slots}
1014	        codes.update(
1015	            {
1016	                credential.slot: credential.state
1017	                for user in await self.async_get_users()
1018	                for credential in user.credentials_of_type(credential_type)
1019	            }

1159	        """

1161

1163	        deletes the credential. On locks with separate user records

1165	        that was its last credential -- the invariant being that a user
1166	        exists if and only if it owns at least one credential. On
1167	        implicit-user locks (e.g. Z-Wave User Code CC) the credential
1168	        delete already removed the user, so the cleanup call is skipped.
1169	        The count is read from ``owner``, a pre-deletion snapshot, so
1170	        the decision does not depend on whether the provider mutates the
1171	        user during the delete. Returns True if changed.
1172	
1173	        The credential delete is the operation that clears the slot, so a
1174	        failure of the follow-up user delete is logged rather than raised: the
1175	        slot is already cleared, and raising would only churn retries that
1176	        re-resolve to no owner. The leftover empty user is surfaced in the log.
1177	        """

1179	        was_only_credential = len(owner.credentials) <= 1
1180	        changed = await self.async_delete_credential(ref)
1181	        if changed and was_only_credential and await self._supports_user_records():
1182	            try:

1184	            except Exception as err:

1187	                    "remove the now-empty user %s: %s",
1188	                    self.lock.entity_id,
1189	                    ref.slot,
1190	                    owner.user_id,
1191	                    err,
1192	                )

265	def credential_from_slot(slot: int, state: SlotCredential) -> Credential:
266	    """
267	    Build the Personal Identification Number credential for a managed slot.
268	
269	    The new model relates to the coordinator's ``SlotCredential`` by a
270	    one-to-one projection: a managed slot index becomes a PIN ``Credential``
271	    at the same index, reusing the ``SlotCredential`` verbatim as its state.
272	    """
273	    return Credential(type=CredentialType.PIN, slot=slot, state=state)
274	
275	
276	def slot_credential_of(credential: Credential) -> SlotCredential:
277	    """
278	    Project a Personal Identification Number credential back to a SlotCredential.
279	
280	    This is the inverse of ``credential_from_slot`` and is identity on the
281	    state, so the coordinator can keep consuming ``SlotCredential`` unchanged.
282	    It rejects non-PIN credentials because only PIN projects one-to-one onto a
283	    managed slot today.
284	    """
285	    if credential.type is not CredentialType.PIN:
286	        raise ValueError(
287	            f"Only PIN credentials project to a slot, got {credential.type}"
288	        )
289	    return credential.state
290	
291	
292	def user_from_slot(slot: int, state: SlotCredential, name: str | None = None) -> User:
293	    """
294	    Build the single-credential user for a managed slot.
295	
296	    Realizes today's one-managed-slot to one-user to one-PIN-credential
297	    projection: the user identifier shares the slot index, the user owns
298	    exactly one PIN credential at that index, and the user is active exactly
299	    when the slot holds a code. A future multi-credential world only appends
300	    to ``credentials`` -- no field changes here.
301	    """
302	    return User(
303	        user_id=slot,
304	        name=name,
305	        active=state.is_present,
306	        credentials=[credential_from_slot(slot, state)],
307	    )

    async def async_set_user(self, user: User) -> SetUserResult:
        """
        Create or update a lock user, returning whether it was newly created.

        The user.user_id here is the slot (credential_index). Matter allocates
        user_index independently: you cannot create a user at a chosen index —
        set_lock_user raises UserSlotEmptyError when user_index is given for an
        empty slot. So the flow is:

        1. Check the credential slot's current owner via get_lock_credential_status.
        2. If the slot is occupied (UPDATE): call set_lock_user with the existing
           user_index from the status response.
        3. If the slot is empty (CREATE): call set_lock_user with user_index=None
           so Matter auto-allocates a free user slot and returns the new index.

        The returned SetUserResult carries the real Matter user_index, which the
        base orchestration passes into async_set_credential as the user_id.
        """
        client, node = self._require_client_and_node()
        try:
            status = await get_lock_credential_status(
                client,
                node,
                credential_type="pin",
                credential_index=user.user_id,
            )
        except ServiceValidationError as err:
            raise LockOperationFailed(
                f"Matter get_lock_credential_status rejected input for "
                f"{self.lock.entity_id}: {err}"
            ) from err
        except HomeAssistantError as err:
            raise LockDisconnected(
                f"Matter get_lock_credential_status failed for "
                f"{self.lock.entity_id}: {err}"
            ) from err

        credential_exists = status.get("credential_exists", False)
        existing_user_index = status.get("user_index")

        if credential_exists and existing_user_index is None:
            # The credential is reportedly occupied but the lock did not
            # surface its owner. Falling through to CREATE would orphan
            # the original user (it would still exist with zero credentials)
            # and break the user-per-credential invariant, so refuse the
            # write and let the caller decide how to recover.
            raise LockOperationFailed(
                f"Matter lock {self.lock.entity_id} slot {user.user_id} reports "
                "credential_exists=True but no user_index"
            )

        if credential_exists and existing_user_index is not None:
            # UPDATE: the slot is occupied — modify the existing user record.
            # set_lock_user here is a metadata-only name update. The historical
            # Matter contract (PR #1077) tolerated name-set failures so a
            # transient 500 or a name the lock rejects does not block the
            # subsequent credential write; the user still exists at the
            # known index, the only thing lost is the name update. Log a
            # warning and fall through.
            try:
                await set_lock_user(
                    client,
                    node,
                    user_index=existing_user_index,
                    user_name=user.name,
                )
            except HomeAssistantError as err:
                LOGGER.warning(
                    "Lock %s: failed to update user name on slot %s "
                    "(user_index=%s); continuing without name update: %s",
                    self.lock.entity_id,
                    user.user_id,
                    existing_user_index,
                    err,
                )
            return SetUserResult(user_id=existing_user_index, created=False)

        # CREATE: the slot is empty — let Matter auto-allocate a user_index.
        try:
            result = await set_lock_user(
                client,
                node,
                user_index=None,
                user_name=user.name,
            )
        except ServiceValidationError as err:
            raise LockOperationFailed(
                f"Matter set_lock_user rejected input for {self.lock.entity_id}: {err}"
            ) from err
        except HomeAssistantError as err:
            raise LockDisconnected(
                f"Matter set_lock_user failed for {self.lock.entity_id}: {err}"
            ) from err
        return SetUserResult(user_id=result["user_index"], created=True)

Here's what I traced. Direct answer first, then the safety guarantee you asked about.

## How LCM users map to lock users today

**They don't, in any nominal sense.** The mapping is purely positional: each managed slot has its own LCM-side user with `user_id = slot`, and each provider creates a brand-new lock-side user per slot. There's no "find the existing user named X" or "attach PIN to the user whose fingerprint is enrolled" — every LCM-managed PIN ends up on its own dedicated user record on the lock.

- **Matter today (on `main`)** — `matter.py:363-369` calls `set_lock_credential(credential_type="pin", credential_index=slot)` with **no** `user_index`. Per the Matter spec, that auto-allocates a fresh user_index and attaches the PIN to that new user (see `lock_helpers.py:702-729`).
- **Matter after PR #1228** — explicit two-step: `set_lock_user(user_index=None)` → auto-allocated index → `set_lock_credential(user_index=<that index>)`. Same outcome, just made explicit at the seam.
- **Z-Wave (PR #1227, merged)** — `zwave_js.py:248-254` uses `user.user_id == slot` directly. Slot==user_id is invariant. PIN goes onto its own user.

So if you have a fingerprint and an NFC tag enrolled on user_index=1, and LCM manages slot 5 with a PIN, you end up with **two users on the lock**: user 1 (fingerprint + NFC) and user 42 or whatever Matter allocated (PIN only). They are unrelated as far as the lock cares.

## Safety: will clearing the PIN wipe the fingerprint/NFC user?

**No.** Three layers of protection:

1. **Today (matter on `main`)** — `async_clear_usercode` (`matter.py:606`) only calls `clear_lock_credential` (ClearCredential). It never touches the user record. Even if the PIN somehow ended up on the same user as your fingerprint, the clear leaves the user alone.
2. **After PR #1228** — `_delete_credential` in `_base.py:1158-1193` runs the cleanup `async_delete_user` **only** if `was_only_credential = len(owner.credentials) <= 1`. `owner.credentials` is the pre-deletion snapshot of every credential the user owns — across all types. If the user owns fingerprint + NFC + PIN, the count is 3, the cleanup is skipped, and only the PIN is cleared.
3. **owner resolution** — `async_clear_usercode` finds owner by "user with a PIN at this slot" (`_base.py:943-951`). If the PIN was attached to a separate auto-allocated user (the realistic case today), that throwaway user is the owner, not your fingerprint user.

So the destructive case ("PIN lives on the fingerprint user AND that's the user's only credential") is the only way an `async_delete_user` would fire, and it cannot occur today because LCM never puts PINs on existing users.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The `was_only_credential` invariant is load-bearing — it's why the user→credential refactor's "implicit user cascade" model (Z-Wave UC clears the user when the credential goes away) and "explicit cascade" model (Matter ClearUser cascades all credentials) can coexist behind the same seam without one accidentally torching the other's user. Trace it in `_base.py:1179`.
- The Matter spec uses `userIndex=null` on SetCredential to mean "auto-allocate a user." That's a quiet but consequential default — it ensures LCM never accidentally rides over a user with other credentials, but it also means there's no path today to *intentionally* unify a PIN with an existing fingerprint user without a new code path.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

## What the user-unification feature would look like

If you want "PIN attaches to the same user as my fingerprint+NFC," the seam already supports it cleanly — Matter's `async_set_credential` writes `user_index=user_id` (`matter-credential-migration:391`). The missing piece is the LCM-side decision of *which existing user_index* to use for a given slot. That needs one of:

- **Manual mapping** — a per-slot config option ("Attach to existing Matter user #1"). Trivial to wire; UX-ugly.
- **Name-based discovery** — `async_set_user` first scans `async_get_users()` for a user whose name matches `user.name`; if found, returns its index (UPDATE path) instead of allocating. Cheap, but only works if you name your LCM slot to match the existing Matter user's name.
- **First-class "Person" identity** — surface lock users in LCM's UI, let users assign slots to existing persons. Big UX lift, but it's the model Matter's DoorLock cluster actually exposes and the memory file [project_matter_data_model.md](/Users/raman/.claude/projects/-Users-raman-projects-lock-code-manager/memory/project_matter_data_model.md) flags this as the long-term direction.

Want me to sketch any of these as a follow-up, or is this just the verification you needed before continuing?

> AGENT

Exactly right — and the answer is that LCM currently has **no ownership marker at all**. The slot is the only namespace mechanism. `async_get_users` (both `_base.py:1280` and `zwave_js.py:159`) returns *every* user on the lock without filtering. There's no "LCM owns user 5" tag, no name prefix convention, no namespace gate. Conflict avoidance today is purely positional: don't put your `managed_slots` range over user_ids/credential_indices that anything else uses.

## Concrete conflict cases this opens

| Path | What happens to an externally-managed user at the same slot |
|---|---|
| Z-Wave `async_set_user(5)` when user 5 exists externally with name "Alice" | Silently renames to LCM's `user.name`. `set_user` is unconditional. |
| Z-Wave `_delete_credential` when external user 5 had only the PIN (e.g. lock factory default) | `was_only_credential=True` → `async_delete_user(5)` fires → external user lost. |
| Z-Wave `_delete_credential` when external user 5 had PIN + RFID | `was_only_credential=False` → user kept; PIN replaced earlier. RFID safe. |
| Matter UPDATE path when `credential_index=5` already has a PIN attached to a fingerprint user | `set_lock_user(user_index=<existing>, user_name=<LCM>)` renames the fingerprint user. PIN value gets overwritten. |
| Matter clear when LCM-owned user has only a PIN | Standard cascade — user deleted. Fine if LCM created it; quiet damage if it was a pre-existing PIN-only user that LCM "adopted." |

The fingerprint+NFC case you raised is the *safe* one because `was_only_credential` protects it. The dangerous ones are externally-created users whose only credential happens to be a PIN sitting at an LCM-managed slot.

## The three feasible models to fix this

| Model | Idea | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| **A — Tag ownership in `user.name`** (Recommended) | Write LCM-created users with a name prefix or sentinel (e.g. `"LCM:Alice"` or `"\u200blcm Alice"`). `async_set_user` UPDATE-path refuses to overwrite a non-LCM user; `_delete_credential` cleanup refuses to delete a non-LCM user. | Cheap to add. One field convention. Has the downside that the name is user-visible on the lock — Z-Wave already requires it for sync, so this would be exposed. |
| **B — Detect-and-warn at config flow** | At slot configuration, read the lock's users. If the slot index collides with a non-LCM user, surface a warning and require the user to confirm "yes, take over this slot." | Catches the conflict at the right moment (before silent damage). Doesn't help with users created on the lock *after* LCM is configured. |
| **C — Managed-slot range above a threshold** | Per-lock setting: "LCM manages user_ids ≥ N." Default N=10 or 20. Manufacturer apps and physical-keypad programming typically use 1..N. | Coarse but effective. Doesn't solve Matter (because Matter user_indices are auto-allocated, not slot-pinned) — only helps Z-Wave where `user_id = slot`. |

**My recommendation: A as the primary, B as the safety net on top.** A is the only one that survives lifecycle events (lock factory reset, external user added later, two LCM installations on the same lock). B catches the initial-configuration foot-gun without code surgery beyond the config flow. C is too provider-specific to be the spine.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The user.name field is the only writable, free-text per-user storage the cluster/CC exposes. Both Z-Wave UC and Matter DoorLock have it; neither has an "application_data" or "owner" field. So tagging there is the *only* in-band ownership marker — out-of-band would mean a `.storage` file mapping `(lock_id, user_id) → managed?`, which has a known sync-drift problem if the lock is reset.
- The seam was deliberately built without an ownership concept (see `_base.py:1280` comment — "Read every user and all of their credentials from the lock"), which means adding A is non-invasive: a small `user.name` decorator on writes + a "is_lcm_managed(user)" predicate, both at the base layer, and every provider inherits it.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
