> AGENT

That framing — slot↔user as a permanent binding — has an important consequence that's worth surfacing explicitly: **the user lifecycle has to be tied to the slot's lifecycle, not the credential's lifecycle.** That's the bigger pivot than the ownership tag.

## What idempotency forces

Today, `_delete_credential` calls `async_delete_user(owner.user_id)` when `was_only_credential` is true (`_base.py:1181-1183`). For 1:1 slot↔user to hold across a temporary "clear PIN, set new PIN" cycle, that deletion has to **not happen** when the slot is still configured in LCM. The lock-side user is the anchor for the slot; PINs come and go through it.

Concretely:
- **Slot configured in LCM** → corresponding lock user exists.
- **PIN set/cleared/replaced** → only the credential changes. The user stays.
- **Slot un-configured in LCM** → only then do we tear the user down.

That moves the cleanup from `_delete_credential` (per-PIN) to slot teardown (per-slot config change). The `was_only_credential` check stops being load-bearing for cleanup and becomes a defensive check that something hasn't drifted.

## What that costs per-provider

**Z-Wave (UC + U3C)** — Already idempotent by the `user_id = slot` invariant. The only change is removing the `async_delete_user` cleanup from the PIN-clear path and moving it to slot teardown. Easy.

**Matter** — The API doesn't let you pin `user_index` on CREATE (Matter auto-allocates), so the binding has to be **discoverable from lock state** or **persisted by LCM**. Two ways:

| Approach | How slot 5 finds "its" user on every operation | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| **Tag in `user_name`** (Recommended) | Format `user_name` with slot encoded — e.g. `f"\u200blcm:{slot}:{display}"`. On any operation: scan `async_get_users()`, find the one whose name parses as slot-5. No LCM-side state. | Burns part of the name field's bytes for the tag; the prefix is visible on the lock UI unless you use ZWS/invisible chars. |
| **LCM `.storage` mapping** | `(lock_entity_id, slot) → user_index`. On first CREATE, allocate & store. Always read the mapping. | New persistence layer with its own sync-drift risk (lock factory reset, mapping points at a deleted user). Need rebuild-on-startup logic anyway. |

Tag-in-name is cheaper because the lock itself is the source of truth: no LCM-side state to drift, no migration on factory reset (the tagged users are gone, LCM re-creates them on next operation). The slot-encoded prefix doubles as the ownership marker from the previous turn — one mechanism solves both problems.

## The collision case becomes easy

Under this model: when LCM is about to write slot 5 and finds an existing non-tagged user at user_index=42 with a PIN at credential_index=5, the decision is unambiguous — that user is **not LCM's**, so LCM allocates a fresh user for itself rather than UPDATE'ing user 42. The PIN write goes to LCM's own user at a different credential_index... 

Actually wait — that breaks because credential_index is also slot-pinned. If credential_index=5 is occupied externally, LCM either has to refuse the slot (matter doesn't let two credentials share an index), or overwrite. **So slot=credential_index is still a collision point on Matter even with idempotency.** That's a config-flow-level concern, not solvable by tagging alone. The tag fixes user-record collisions; credential-index collisions need either refusal at config or a separate credential_index allocation strategy.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- This shift mirrors a common pattern in resource-management systems: separating the **handle** lifecycle (user_index, slot binding) from the **payload** lifecycle (credential value). It's the same reason a database keeps a primary key stable across UPDATEs to other columns — without that, every join becomes ambiguous. Right now LCM's "primary key" (slot → lock_user) gets recycled on every PIN cycle.
- The `was_only_credential` check in `_base.py:1179` was written under the assumption "user exists iff it owns at least one credential" — that's the invariant from the [project_credential_mgmt_refactor.md](/Users/raman/.claude/projects/-Users-raman-projects-lock-code-manager/memory/project_credential_mgmt_refactor.md) design doc. Idempotency-as-priority flips that to "user exists iff its slot is LCM-configured." Both are coherent; they just optimize for different things.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

So the open design questions for you to direct:
1. Tag-in-name vs LCM-side persistence for Matter's mapping recovery
2. Whether to refuse a slot at config time if `credential_index` is externally occupied (Matter only)
3. Whether to migrate the cleanup point from `_delete_credential` to slot-teardown — and if so, what code path "owns" slot teardown today (config-flow remove? options-flow slot drop?)

> AGENT

Yes, exactly right — and that turns out to be the cleaner design because it lets the tag do double duty (ownership marker AND idempotency anchor) and frees LCM from ever having to reason about existing users.

**Aside on the syntax bug I flagged** — turns out I was wrong. Python 3.14 brought back `except A, B:` as sugar for `except (A, B):`; verified it catches both. Sorry for the misdirect.

## What "always create our own" forces

| Invariant | Today | Under new rule | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| Z-Wave UC `user_id = slot = credential_id` | Slot IS the user | Unchanged — no user records to tag, so no LCM concept to manage. Coexistence is by slot-range. | Free. The UC path is entirely outside this conversation. |
| Z-Wave U3C `user_id = slot` | LCM writes user 5 for slot 5 | Drop the invariant. Allocate user_id at runtime, write the `lcm:{slot}:` tag, rediscover by tag on every op. | Loses the elegant equality; gains coexistence. |
| Matter `credential_index = slot` | LCM writes PIN at credential_index=5 for slot 5 | Drop the invariant. Pass `credential_index=None` so Matter auto-allocates, find the PIN by walking the tagged user's credentials. | Same shape as user_id — runtime-discovered, not slot-pinned. |
| Matter `user_index` auto-allocated | Today happens to be runtime | Unchanged; tag rule formalizes it. | Free. |

So the unified provider contract becomes: **slot is an LCM concept that maps to a lock user via the tag, and credentials are properties of that user.** No protocol-level identifier is slot-pinned anymore. The base seam stays the same shape, but `async_set_user` switches from "write user with user_id=slot" to "find-or-create the user tagged `lcm:{slot}:`."

## Coexistence properties you get

- Other controller's users with non-`lcm:` names are invisible to LCM's write paths. `async_set_user` only finds-or-creates LCM-tagged users; `_delete_credential` cleanup only acts on LCM-tagged owners.
- External user gets a PIN at credential_index=5? Doesn't affect LCM's slot 5 — LCM's PIN goes to its own user at whatever credential_index Matter allocates.
- External controller renames or reorganizes users? Doesn't affect LCM — discovery is by tag, not by index.
- Factory reset + re-pair? LCM's tagged users vanish; on next operation LCM recreates them. Slot config in LCM is the source of truth for "should this slot exist."

## Open questions before I save this as a memory

1. **Slot teardown trigger** — when does LCM delete its tagged user? Slot removed from config flow? Lock unmanaged? My read: slot removed from LCM config is the cleanest trigger; PIN-clear no longer deletes the user (the lifecycle decoupling we discussed last turn).
2. **Migration for pre-tag installs** — existing LCM users have plain names like `"Alice"`. On first post-upgrade read, do we: (a) auto-rename to `lcm:{slot}:Alice` (adopt-and-tag), (b) leave them and treat them as legacy un-managed (defensive — never modify), or (c) require user to re-key during upgrade? Option (a) is the most ergonomic but mutates existing locks on upgrade.
3. **Tag format final** — `lcm:{slot}:{display}` with slot in decimal. Want me to lock that exactly, or use a separator like `|` or a zero-width prefix? Decimal slot can go up to 3 digits, so worst-case overhead is 9 chars (`lcm:255:`). On a 10-char-limit lock that leaves 1 char of display — degenerate but functional.

Pick directions for those three and I'll save the consolidated decision as a project memory, then we can scope the implementation as a separate move.

Saved. The consolidated decision is now in [project_user_tag_idempotency.md](/Users/raman/.claude/projects/-Users-raman-projects-lock-code-manager/memory/project_user_tag_idempotency.md) and indexed in MEMORY.md.

## Summary of what's locked in

- **Tag format**: `lcm:{slot}:{display}` with decimal slot, no zero padding.
- **Rule**: LCM always creates its own users; never adopts or modifies non-tagged users.
- **Invariants dropped**: Z-Wave U3C `user_id = slot`, Matter `credential_index = slot`. Both become runtime-allocated; discovery is by tag scan.
- **Z-Wave UC unchanged** — implicit-user model has no name field, coexistence is by slot-range.
- **Lifecycle**: user existence ties to slot configuration, not credential presence. PIN cycles never delete the user.
- **Slot teardown**: hooks on slot removed from LCM config flow.
- **Matter-only migration**: on first startup post-upgrade, if state matches LCM's last-known snapshot, auto-rename existing LCM-managed users to the tag format.

## Remaining implementation surface (not yet sequenced)

1. PR #1228 and #1229 should land first on the current design, then this work goes on top.
2. `_truncate_user_name` redesign — preserve prefix, truncate only display.
3. Slot-teardown hook location in the config flow.
4. Migration-gate fingerprint persistence in `.storage`.
5. `_delete_credential`'s `was_only_credential` cleanup removal (`_base.py:1179-1183`).

Nothing to do right now — say the word when you want to pick this up after #1228/#1229 merge, or if you want me to draft a phased PR sequence as a follow-up.

function ensureAccessControl(endpoint: Endpoint): AccessControlAPI {
  const api = endpoint.accessControl;
  if (api === undefined) {
    throw new InvalidParamsPassedToCommandError(
      "This endpoint does not support access control methods",
    );
  }
  return api;
}

## PR #1227 Summary

**Title:** feat(zwave_js): migrate to unified access_control credential API

**What it does:** This PR migrates the Z-Wave JS lock provider to Home Assistant's unified credential management system introduced in PR #1225. It drops legacy User Code Command Class operations and reads PIN values directly from `node.access_control`, enabling the sync loop to detect when lock state matches desired state and avoid re-writing slots on restart. The provider now transparently supports both User Credential CC (newer 700/800-series locks) and User Code CC (500-series) without regression. Capability-driven decisions—type checking, name truncation, user-record gating—are hoisted into `BaseLock` so future credential types and providers are additive.

**File scope:**
- Domain credentials type (new `max_user_name_length` field)
- Base orchestration (`BaseLock`: caching, validation, truncation, type projection)
- Z-Wave provider (reads from `access_control`, drops legacy CC operations, uses `lock_helpers`)
- Seam tests (unified API mocking)
- Z-Wave unit tests (rewritten onto `access_control` API; 1042 passing)

**Net LOC delta:** +2215 / −1510 = **+705 lines** (domain/base adds exceed provider reduction due to new capability hoists and expanded test coverage)

Two parts:

## #1229 functional changes — none

Pure refactor. The migration is mechanical:
- `async_set_usercode` → `async_set_credential` (new signature, body unchanged)
- `async_clear_usercode` → `async_delete_credential` (new signature, body unchanged)
- `async_get_usercodes` overrides **deleted** — the base now derives the slot map from `async_get_users` (the projection that #1225 introduced).
- Tests updated to call the new APIs.

I checked virtual (tiny), zigbee2mqtt (largest), and skimmed akuvox/schlage/zha. The MQTT pub semantics, OSError-vs-HomeAssistantError mapping, optimistic-push behavior, and pending-future cleanup are all identical to main. No behavior diffs; just shape and types.

## akuvox/schlage tag convergence — agreed, but later

You're right that there's a duplicate tag convention now:

| Today | Where | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `[LCM:5] Alice` | `_util.py:make_tagged_name` (used by akuvox + schlage) | bracketed-with-space |
| `lcm:5:Alice` | Just-decided design for matter & U3C | colon-delimited |

Same purpose (encode slot in a discoverable string); same mechanism (parse on read, prepend on write); two formats. Converging on one is correct.

**Recommendation: do it as a follow-up PR, not in #1229.** Reasons:

1. **#1229's scope is the seam migration, full stop.** Adding a format change broadens the diff and weakens the "pure refactor" framing for review. Easier to merge as-is.
2. **The matter side of the new format doesn't exist yet.** Changing akuvox/schlage's format now leaves them ahead of matter; review reviewers can't see the consistency payoff until the matter migration lands too.
3. **There's a migration concern on existing installs** — anyone already using akuvox or schlage with LCM has `[LCM:5] Alice` written to their lock today. A format change needs a read-time compat shim (parse both formats), then eventual sunset. That's its own change with its own tests.

Better sequence:
1. Land #1229 as-is (signature migration only).
2. Build the matter tag work on the unified `lcm:{slot}:{display}` format.
3. Migrate akuvox/schlage onto the same `_util.py` helpers + format, with a read-time compat shim for the old bracketed format.

Memory updated. The migration model is now explicitly:

1. **Parser** accepts both `[LCM:5] Alice` and `lcm:5:Alice`. On match, returns `(slot, display, needs_rewrite)`.
2. **Rewrite trigger** — when `needs_rewrite=True`, the next operation that already needs to touch that user's name (or a passive sync pass) writes the new format. No extra lock command if we're already writing.
3. **Display preserved verbatim** — `[LCM:5] Alice` → `lcm:5:Alice`, never `[LCM:5] Alice` → `lcm:5:Code Slot 5`.
4. **No gate needed** — the presence of the old `[LCM:` prefix is itself proof of LCM ownership. (Contrast with matter's untagged migration which needs the state-unchanged gate.)
5. **Sunset path** — once the parser stops seeing old-format matches in real-world telemetry (or after a stated deprecation window), drop the old branch from the parser.

Does that match what you had in mind, or do you want the rewrite eager (on read) instead of opportunistic (next write)?

## Suggested PR sequence for the tag work

Three PRs, each focused and testable. Flagging up front that none are trivially small.

**PR A — shared tag helper + tolerant parser (no behavior change)**
- Promote/extend `_util.py` with `make_tagged_name(slot, display)` emitting `lcm:{slot}:{display}` and a tolerant `parse_tag(name)` returning `(slot, display, needs_rewrite)`.
- Acceptance: old `[LCM:5] Alice` parses with `needs_rewrite=True`; new `lcm:5:Alice` parses with `needs_rewrite=False`; non-LCM names return `(None, name, False)`.
- akuvox and schlage switch to the new helper but **keep writing the old format for now** (write-path stays `[LCM:5] Alice`). This isolates the parser change from any rewrite behavior so a rollback is safe.
- Tests: parser round-trips for both formats, mixed-format lock state, name-with-no-tag, display containing colons.

**PR B — matter tag adoption + `_truncate_user_name` redesign**
- `_truncate_user_name` becomes `_build_tagged_user_name(slot, display)`: builds `lcm:{slot}:{display}`, truncates only `display` so the total fits `max_user_name_length`.
- Matter's `async_set_user` switches to find-or-create-by-tag (scan `async_get_users()` for `lcm:{slot}:` prefix), drops the `credential_index=slot` invariant (pass `credential_index=None`, discover via owner's credentials).
- Drop the `was_only_credential` cleanup in `_delete_credential` (`_base.py:1179-1183`). User lifecycle ties to slot config, not credentials.
- New slot-teardown hook in the config flow that calls `async_delete_user` for the LCM-owned user.
- Matter-only startup migration: on first connect post-upgrade, if state matches LCM's last-known snapshot, rewrite each LCM-managed slot's user to the tag format. Snapshot fingerprint persisted in `.storage`.
- Tests: tag discovery, fresh slot (CREATE), repeated slot (UPDATE same user_index), coexistence with a non-tagged external user at the same `credential_index`, startup migration with state-matched and state-drifted cases.

**PR C — Z-Wave U3C tag adoption + akuvox/schlage format rewrite**
- Z-Wave U3C `async_set_user` switches to find-or-create-by-tag; drops `user_id = slot` invariant; allocates `user_id` at runtime by finding the first free index. (Z-Wave UC stays untouched — implicit-user gate already short-circuits.)
- akuvox and schlage write paths switch to the new format. Read paths use the tolerant parser from PR A and rewrite opportunistically on the next operation that already needs to write a name (so no extra command per read).
- Tests: U3C tag discovery and free-index allocation, akuvox/schlage round-trip + old-format rewrite on next write.

## Why this split

- Each PR is independently revertable. PR A is purely additive — easy to drop in early so reviewers can grok the parser/format separately.
- PR B is the meaty architectural change (lifecycle pivot, drop-the-invariant, migration). Reviewers can focus on it without also seeing format-helper churn.
- PR C is the broadest in file count but smallest in conceptual surface — each provider gets the same treatment, and PR B's review has already validated the seam-level reasoning.

The alternative — one big PR with all of it — would be unreviewable. The alternative on the other extreme — splitting PR B's migration from PR B's lifecycle pivot — leaves an awkward intermediate state where matter has tags but still deletes users on PIN clear, which would break user assumptions mid-sequence.

Want me to start drafting PR A, or pause for you to digest the sequence first?

  "old_string": "\"\"\"\nShared helpers for provider implementations.\n\nProvider-internal utilities that don't belong in the integration-wide\n``util.py``. Currently: slot-tagging used by providers whose lock APIs\nidentify codes by user-name rather than by slot number (Schlage, Akuvox).\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\n\n# Format: ``[LCM:<slot>] <friendly name>`` — providers prepend this tag\n# so we can recover which slot a code belongs to from the lock's stored\n# user name.\n_SLOT_TAG_RE = re.compile(r\"^\\[LCM:(\\d+)\\]\\s*(.*)\")\n\n\ndef make_tagged_name(slot_num: int, name: str | None = None) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return a code name tagged with the Lock Code Manager slot number.\"\"\"\n    base = name or f\"Code Slot {slot_num}\"\n    return f\"[LCM:{slot_num}] {base}\"\n\n\ndef parse_tag(name: str) -> tuple[int | None, str]:\n    \"\"\"\n    Parse a Lock Code Manager slot tag from a code name.\n\n    Returns ``(slot_num, friendly_name)`` when a tag is present, or\n    ``(None, original_name)`` when no tag is found.\n    \"\"\"\n    match = _SLOT_TAG_RE.match(name)\n    if match:\n        return int(match.group(1)), match.group(2)\n    return None, name",
  "new_string": "\"\"\"\nShared helpers for provider implementations.\n\nProvider-internal utilities that don't belong in the integration-wide\n``util.py``. Currently: slot-tagging used by providers whose lock APIs\nidentify codes by user-name rather than by slot number (Schlage, Akuvox,\nand -- once the unified-user migration lands -- Matter and Z-Wave User\nCredential CC).\n\nTwo tag formats coexist during the migration window:\n\n* Legacy ``[LCM:<slot>] <name>`` -- written by Schlage/Akuvox today.\n* New ``lcm<slot>:<name>`` -- the consolidated format the rest of the\n  integration will move to. One character shorter, matters on locks with\n  small ``max_user_name_length``.\n\n``parse_tag_with_rewrite`` accepts both and signals when the matched name\nis in the legacy format so callers can rewrite it in place at the next\nwrite opportunity.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\n\n_LEGACY_SLOT_TAG_RE = re.compile(r\"^\\[LCM:(\\d+)\\]\\s*(.*)\")\n_NEW_SLOT_TAG_RE = re.compile(r\"^lcm(\\d+):(.*)\")\n\n\ndef make_tagged_name(slot_num: int, name: str | None = None) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return a code name in the legacy ``[LCM:<slot>]`` format.\"\"\"\n    base = name or f\"Code Slot {slot_num}\"\n    return f\"[LCM:{slot_num}] {base}\"\n\n\ndef make_new_tagged_name(slot_num: int, name: str | None = None) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return a code name in the new ``lcm<slot>:`` format.\"\"\"\n    base = name or f\"Code Slot {slot_num}\"\n    return f\"lcm{slot_num}:{base}\"\n\n\ndef parse_tag(name: str) -> tuple[int | None, str]:\n    \"\"\"\n    Parse a Lock Code Manager slot tag, tolerant of both formats.\n\n    Returns ``(slot_num, friendly_name)`` when either format matches, or\n    ``(None, original_name)`` otherwise. Callers that care about\n    rewriting legacy tags in place should use ``parse_tag_with_rewrite``\n    instead.\n    \"\"\"\n    slot, friendly, _ = parse_tag_with_rewrite(name)\n    return slot, friendly\n\n\ndef parse_tag_with_rewrite(name: str) -> tuple[int | None, str, bool]:\n    \"\"\"\n    Parse a slot tag and signal whether it needs format migration.\n\n    Returns ``(slot_num, friendly_name, needs_rewrite)``. ``needs_rewrite``\n    is True only when the legacy ``[LCM:<slot>]`` format matched; the\n    caller can re-emit via ``make_new_tagged_name`` on the next write to\n    migrate the lock-stored name in place. The new format and untagged\n    names both return ``needs_rewrite=False``.\n    \"\"\"\n    match = _NEW_SLOT_TAG_RE.match(name)\n    if match:\n        return int(match.group(1)), match.group(2), False\n    match = _LEGACY_SLOT_TAG_RE.match(name)\n    if match:\n        return int(match.group(1)), match.group(2), True\n    return None, name, False"
}

author: Copilot

author: Copilot

> AGENT

Got it — the model is `async_setup_internal` (base, wraps with cap probe + error handling) → `async_setup` (provider, surgical). Providers never `super().async_setup_internal()`; they just implement the surgical leaf.

Applied to credentials, the existing seam already has that shape:

```
async_internal_set_usercode  (base — rate-limit, refresh, etc.)
  → async_set_usercode       (base — builds Credential, dispatches)
    → async_set_credential   (provider — surgical write)
```

So the PIN guard should live in `async_set_usercode` (or right between, depending on where credential validation belongs). The provider's `async_set_credential` receives a credential whose PIN-readability is already guaranteed by the seam — no per-provider defense, no `super()`.

This means I should reverse what I just did:
- **Remove** the `self._require_readable_pin(credential)` call from virtual.py and zha.py (already on my branch).
- **Add** the guard at the seam level once.
- **Remove** the existing inline guards from zwave_js.py and matter.py (they become redundant duplicates of the seam guard).
- Net result: every provider's `async_set_credential` is shorter.

One design question before I rewire: the seam-passes-string approach.

337	        """
338	        Set a Personal Identification Number credential on a slot.
339	
340	        If a user already exists for the given slot, the Personal
341	        Identification Number (and optionally the name) is updated via
342	        ``modify_user``. Otherwise a new user is created via ``add_user``.
343	
344	        Returns True unconditionally because the Akuvox API does not
345	        indicate whether the value actually changed. The list/modify
346	        (or list/add) sequence runs under the sequence lock so concurrent
347	        callers cannot interleave their own multi-step writes against the
348	        same slot. Ignores ``user_id``; slot-only providers address the
349	        credential by slot.
350	        """
351	        code_slot = credential.slot
352	        usercode = credential.readable_pin or ""
353	        async with self._serialize_sequence():
354	            users = await self._async_list_users()
355	
356	            existing_device_id: str | None = None
357	            existing_friendly_name: str | None = None
358	            for user in users:
359	                if not _is_local_user(user):
360	                    continue
361	                user_name = user.get("name", "")
362	                parsed_slot, friendly = _parse_tag(user_name)
363	                if parsed_slot == code_slot:
364	                    existing_device_id = str(user.get("id", ""))
365	                    existing_friendly_name = friendly
366	                    break
367	
368	            effective_name = name or existing_friendly_name
369	            tagged_name = _make_tagged_name(code_slot, effective_name)
370	
371	            if existing_device_id:
372	                await self._async_modify_user(
373	                    existing_device_id, name=tagged_name, pin=usercode
374	                )
375	            else:
376	                await self._async_add_user(tagged_name, usercode)
377	
378	        LOGGER.debug(
379	            "Lock %s: set Personal Identification Number credential on slot %s",
380	            self.lock.entity_id,
381	            code_slot,
382	        )
383	        return True

Emit up to and including the open paren\n        out.append(src[i:j+len(target)])\n        # Walk to closing paren, tracking depth, brackets, strings.\n        k = j + len(target)\n        depth = 1\n        in_str = None  # quote char if inside string\n        positions = []  # comma positions at our depth (depth==1)\n        escape = False\n        while k < n:\n            c = src[k]\n            if in_str is not None:\n                if escape:\n                    escape = False\n                elif c == \"\\\\\":\n                    escape = True\n                elif c == in_str:\n                    in_str = None\n                k += 1\n                continue\n            if c in (\"\\\"\", \"'\"):\n                in_str = c\n                k += 1\n                continue\n            if c == \"(\" or c == \"[\" or c == \"{\":\n                depth += 1\n            elif c == \")\" or c == \"]\" or c == \"}\":\n                depth -= 1\n                if depth == 0:\n                    break\n            elif c == \",\" and depth == 1:\n                positions.append(k)\n            k += 1\n        # positions[0] = comma between arg1 (uid) and arg2 (credential)\n        # We need the comma AFTER arg2 (credential): positions[1]\n        if len(positions) >= 2:\n            comma2 = positions[1]\n            # body content of arg2 (credential) goes from positions[0]+1 to comma2\n            arg2 = src[positions[0]+1:comma2].strip()\n            # Skip transform if 'credential' isn't actually the second positional.\n            # Heuristic: it should be something that has .readable_pin-able semantics.\n            # We look for whether the call already includes 3+ positional args (pin already added).\n            # Detect that by checking if positions[2] exists and the 3rd arg is a string-literal/expr.\n            # For simplicity: if the 3rd arg looks like a kwarg (contains '='), inject.\n            need_inject = True\n            if len(positions) >= 3:\n                arg3 = src[positions[1]+1:positions[2]].strip()\n                if \"=\" not in arg3:\n                    # third positional already present\n                    need_inject = False\n            else:\n                # only 2 positionals total before close; check last segment\n                last = src[positions[1]+1:k].strip()\n                if \"=\" not in last:\n                    need_inject = False\n            if need_inject:\n                # Inject \", <expr>\" right after comma2's leading commas. Actually\n                # we want to insert AFTER positions[1] which is the comma2 itself,\n                # then before the next char (typically whitespace/newline then arg3).\n                # Strategy: emit src[j+len(target) .. positions[1]+1], then injection,\n                # then src[positions[1]+1 .. k].\n                head = src[j+len(target):positions[1]+1]\n                tail = src[positions[1]+1:k]\n                # The pin expression. Use credential variable name from arg2 if simple identifier,\n                # otherwise wrap.\n                if re.fullmatch(r\"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\", arg2):\n                    pin_expr = f' {arg2}.readable_pin or \"\",'\n                else:\n                    # Complex expression — pass the credential's readable_pin via the same expression\n                    pin_expr = f' ({arg2}).readable_pin or \"\",'\n                out[-1] = src[i:j+len(target)]  # already pushed; replace head emission\n                out.append(head + pin_expr + tail + src[k])\n                i = k + 1\n                continue\n        # Default: emit balance to and including the closing paren.\n        out.append(src[j+len(target):k+1])\n        i = k + 1\n    return \"\".join(out)\n\nchanged_count = 0\nfor f in files:\n    p = Path(f)\n    orig = p.read_text()\n    new = transform(orig)\n    if new != orig:\n        p.write_text(new)\n        # Count number of injected lines\n        injs = new.count(\"readable_pin or \\\"\\\"\") - orig.count(\"readable_pin or \\\"\\\"\")\n        print(f\"{f}: +{injs} injections\")\n        changed_count += injs\nprint(f\"total: {changed_count} injections\")\nEOF\n",
  "description": "Bulk inject pin argument into test call-sites",

{
  "command": "gh pr create --base main --title \"refactor(providers): hoist PIN-readability guard to base seam\" --body \"$(cat <<'EOF'\n## Proposed change\n\nAddress PR #1229 review feedback (Copilot flagged silent empty-PIN fallback in slot-only providers) by **hoisting** the PIN-readability guard from per-provider to the base seam, rather than duplicating it across every provider.\n\n### Before\n- \\`zwave_js\\` and \\`matter\\` each had an inline \\`if credential.readable_pin is None: raise CodeRejectedError(...)\\` guard at the top of \\`async_set_credential\\`.\n- Slot-only providers (virtual, zha, akuvox, schlage, zigbee2mqtt) used \\`credential.readable_pin or \\\"\\\"\\` — coercing to empty string and silently writing a blank PIN if the credential was unreadable.\n\n### After\n- New \\`BaseLock._require_readable_pin(credential)\\` helper expresses the contract once.\n- The seam (\\`async_set_usercode\\`) validates and threads the resolved \\`pin: str\\` through \\`_set_credential\\` → \\`async_set_credential\\`.\n- Every provider's \\`async_set_credential\\` now takes \\`pin: str\\` as a guaranteed non-None argument. No per-provider guard. Saves one character per name vs. the legacy bracketed format, which matters on locks with small \\`max_user_name_length\\` (some advertise 10).\n- Make \\`parse_tag\\` tolerant: it now matches either format (strict superset of prior behavior). Existing call-sites continue to work without change.\n- Add \\`parse_tag_with_rewrite\\` returning \\`(slot, friendly, needs_rewrite)\\`. The \\`needs_rewrite\\` flag is True only when the legacy format matched, signalling that the caller can opportunistically rewrite the lock-stored name to the new format on the next write.\n\n### What this PR does NOT do\n\n- **Schlage and Akuvox continue to write the legacy format.** Their \\`async_set_credential\\` paths are untouched.   "new_string": "## Open implementation surface\n\nResolved during the 2026-06-10 deep-research pass:\n\n* **Slot-teardown hook point**: `__init__.py:946-995` already computes `diff.pairs_removed` (frozenset of (lock_entity_id, slot)). Inside the existing `if slots_to_remove:` block, after entity removal and coordinator stop. Wrap in try/except `LockDisconnected`/`LockOperationFailed` because slot teardown can't block on lock connectivity.\n* **`_truncate_user_name` redesign**: rename to `_build_tagged_user_name(slot: int, display: str | None) -> str | None`. Builds `f\"lcm{slot}:{display or ''}\"`, truncates the display portion to fit `max_user_name_length - len(prefix)`. Degenerate cases: `max == 0` → None (implicit-user gate already short-circuits), prefix alone exceeds max → truncate prefix to `max` (extremely small locks, mostly hypothetical).\n* **`_set_credential` signature**: drop the `User.user_id == slot` invariant. Thread `slot: int` as a separate parameter alongside `user`. The base orchestration uses `slot` to build the tagged name; the provider returns the allocated `user_id` from `async_set_user(SetUserResult)`.\n* **Matter startup migration gate**: persist a fingerprint of the last-known user list (set of `(user_index, user_name)` pairs) in LCM's `.storage`. On startup, read current lock users — if the set matches the stored fingerprint, run the auto-rename pass; if it drifted, skip and log so the user can resolve manually. After a successful pass (rename or skip), update the fingerprint to the new state.\n\nActive-PRs status:\n* **PR #1237** (PIN-guard hoist) — open, in review. Modifies `_base.py` extensively. 1	"""
2	Shared helpers for provider implementations.
3	
4	Provider-internal utilities that don't belong in the integration-wide
5	``util.py``. Currently: slot-tagging used by providers whose lock APIs
6	identify codes by user-name rather than by slot number (Schlage, Akuvox,
7	and -- once the unified-user migration lands -- Matter and Z-Wave User
8	Credential CC).
9	
10	Two tag formats coexist during the migration window:
11	
12	* Legacy ``[LCM:<slot>] <name>`` -- written by Schlage/Akuvox today.
13	* New ``lcm<slot>:<name>`` -- the consolidated format the rest of the
14	  integration will move to. One character shorter, matters on locks with
15	  small ``max_user_name_length``.
16	
17	``parse_tag_with_rewrite`` accepts both and signals when the matched name
18	is in the legacy format so callers can rewrite it in place at the next
19	write opportunity.
20	"""
21	
22	from __future__ import annotations
23	
24	import re
25	
26	_LEGACY_SLOT_TAG_RE = re.compile(r"^\[LCM:(\d+)\]\s*(.*)")
27	_NEW_SLOT_TAG_RE = re.compile(r"^lcm(\d+):(.*)")
28	
29	
30	def make_tagged_name(slot_num: int, name: str | None = None) -> str:
31	    """Return a code name in the legacy ``[LCM:<slot>]`` format."""
32	    base = name or f"Code Slot {slot_num}"
33	    return f"[LCM:{slot_num}] {base}"
34	
35	
36	def make_new_tagged_name(slot_num: int, name: str | None = None) -> str:
37	    """Return a code name in the new ``lcm<slot>:`` format."""
38	    base = name or f"Code Slot {slot_num}"
39	    return f"lcm{slot_num}:{base}"
40	
41	
42	def parse_tag(name: str) -> tuple[int | None, str]:
43	    """
44	    Parse a Lock Code Manager slot tag, tolerant of both formats.
45	
46	    Returns ``(slot_num, friendly_name)`` when either format matches, or
47	    ``(None, original_name)`` otherwise. Callers that care about
48	    rewriting legacy tags in place should use ``parse_tag_with_rewrite``
49	    instead.
50	    """
51	    slot, friendly, _ = parse_tag_with_rewrite(name)
52	    return slot, friendly
53	
54	
55	def parse_tag_with_rewrite(name: str) -> tuple[int | None, str, bool]:
56	    """
57	    Parse a slot tag and signal whether it needs format migration.
58	
59	    Returns ``(slot_num, friendly_name, needs_rewrite)``. ``needs_rewrite``
60	    is True only when the legacy ``[LCM:<slot>]`` format matched; the
61	    caller can re-emit via ``make_new_tagged_name`` on the next write to
62	    migrate the lock-stored name in place. The new format and untagged
63	    names both return ``needs_rewrite=False``.
64	    """
65	    match = _NEW_SLOT_TAG_RE.match(name)
66	    if match:
67	        return int(match.group(1)), match.group(2), False
68	    match = _LEGACY_SLOT_TAG_RE.match(name)
69	    if match:
70	        return int(match.group(1)), match.group(2), True
71	    return None, name, False
72	
73	
74	def parse_slot_num(value: object) -> int | None:
75	    """
76	    Convert a slot identifier to an int, or return None if not convertible.
77	
78	    Mirrors ``int(value)`` while collapsing the ``TypeError``/``ValueError``
79	    that providers otherwise catch when a lock reports a non-numeric slot key.
80	    Call sites remain responsible for their own logging and skip/return flow.
81	    """
82	    try:
83	        return int(value)  # type: ignore[call-overload]
84	    except TypeError, ValueError:
85	        return None
86

20:Worst-case prefix overhead is 7 characters (`lcm255:`). On a 10-character-limit lock, that leaves 3 characters of display — tight but functional. The leading colon was dropped vs. the original sketch (`lcm:{slot}:`) to claw back one character.
72:**Backwards-compat as detect-and-rewrite:** on read, parse with a tolerant parser that accepts both `[LCM:5] Alice` and `lcm5:Alice`. When the old format is detected, rewrite the lock-stored user name to the new format via the lock's rename API as a side effect of the read or the next sync pass. The display portion is preserved verbatim. Once every existing install has rewritten, the old-format branch in the parser can be removed.
```

  "new_string": "    def _require_readable_pin(self, credential: Credential) -> str:\n        \"\"\"\n        Return the credential's readable PIN, or raise ``CodeRejectedError``.\n\n        Called by the seam (``async_set_usercode`` and ``_set_credential``)\n        before dispatching to the provider's ``async_set_credential``\n        override; the resolved ``pin: str`` is threaded through as a\n        positional argument so the provider receives a guaranteed string\n        and does not need its own defensive check.\n\n        The seam already builds credentials from a string usercode so\n        ``readable_pin`` is non-None by construction along that path -- the\n        guard catches future regressions (a credential constructed outside\n        the seam, a refactor that loses the invariant) and never the\n        normal flow. Providers MUST NOT re-add their own readable-pin\n        check; doing so duplicates the contract and re-introduces the\n        ``or \"\"`` silent coercion pattern this helper exists to eliminate.\n        \"\"\""

name = self._make_credential(slot=N, pin=\"literal\")\n    re.compile(\n        r'^\\s*(?P<n>[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\\s*=\\s*self\\._make_credential\\([^)]*pin\\s*=\\s*\"(?P<p>[^\"]+)\"'\n    ),\n    # name = credential_from_slot(slot, SlotCredential.known(\"literal\"))\n    re.compile(\n        r'^\\s*(?P<n>[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\\s*=\\s*credential_from_slot\\(\\s*\\d+\\s*,\\s*SlotCredential\\.known\\(\\s*\"(?P<p>[^\"]+)\"'\n    ),\n    # name = Credential(...SlotCredential.known(\"literal\")...)\n    re.compile(\n        r'^\\s*(?P<n>[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\\s*=\\s*Credential\\([^)]*SlotCredential\\.known\\(\\s*\"(?P<p>[^\"]+)\"'\n    ),\n]\n\n\ndef find_recent_pin_assignment(lines, line_idx, name):\n    \"\"\"Walk backward from line_idx to find an assignment to `name` that captures a PIN literal.\"\"\"\n    for i in range(line_idx, -1, -1):\n        line = lines[i]\n        for pat in assignment_pin_patterns:\n            m = pat.search(line)\n            if m and m.group(\"n\") == name:\n                return m.group(\"p\")\n    return None\n\n\ntotal_fixed = 0\nunresolved = []\nfor f in files:\n    p = Path(f)\n    text = p.read_text()\n    lines = text.split(\"\\n\")\n    # 1	"""
2	Shared helpers for provider implementations.
3	
4	Provider-internal utilities that don't belong in the integration-wide
5	``util.py``. Currently: slot-tagging used by providers whose lock APIs
6	identify codes by user-name rather than by slot number (Schlage, Akuvox,
7	and -- once the unified-user migration lands -- Matter and Z-Wave User
8	Credential CC).
9	
10	Two tag formats coexist during the migration window:
11	
12	* Canonical ``lcm:<slot>:<name>`` -- the consolidated format every new
13	  write uses. Two colons delimit the slot field clearly for visual
14	  parseability on the lock UI.
15	* Legacy ``[LCM:<slot>] <name>`` -- written by Schlage/Akuvox today.
16	  Still emitted by ``make_legacy_tagged_name`` while those providers
17	  migrate; their reads tolerate it via ``parse_tag_with_rewrite``, which
18	  signals a legacy match so the caller can rewrite the lock-stored name
19	  in place at the next write opportunity. The legacy emitter is the
20	  deprecation marker -- ``_legacy_`` in the name is intentional so
21	  reviewers see at the call site that the writer hasn't migrated yet.
22	"""
23	
24	from __future__ import annotations
25	
26	import re
27	
28	_LEGACY_SLOT_TAG_RE = re.compile(r"^\[LCM:(\d+)\]\s*(.*)")
29	_TAG_RE = re.compile(r"^lcm:(\d+):(.*)")
30	
31	
32	def make_tagged_name(slot_num: int, name: str | None = None) -> str:
33	    """Return a code name in the canonical ``lcm:<slot>:`` format."""
34	    base = name or f"Code Slot {slot_num}"
35	    return f"lcm:{slot_num}:{base}"
36	
37	
38	def make_legacy_tagged_name(slot_num: int, name: str | None = None) -> str:
39	    """
40	    Return a code name in the legacy ``[LCM:<slot>]`` format.
41	
42	    Deprecated: kept for Schlage/Akuvox until they migrate to the
43	    canonical format with read-time detect-and-rewrite. New call sites
44	    should use ``make_tagged_name``.
45	    """
46	    base = name or f"Code Slot {slot_num}"
47	    return f"[LCM:{slot_num}] {base}"
48	
49	
50	def parse_tag(name: str) -> tuple[int | None, str]:
51	    """
52	    Parse a Lock Code Manager slot tag, tolerant of both formats.
53	
54	    Returns ``(slot_num, friendly_name)`` when either format matches, or
55	    ``(None, original_name)`` otherwise. Callers that care about
56	    rewriting legacy tags in place should use ``parse_tag_with_rewrite``
57	    instead.
58	    """
59	    slot, friendly, _ = parse_tag_with_rewrite(name)
60	    return slot, friendly
61	
62	
63	def parse_tag_with_rewrite(name: str) -> tuple[int | None, str, bool]:
64	    """
65	    Parse a slot tag and signal whether it needs format migration.
66	
67	    Returns ``(slot_num, friendly_name, needs_rewrite)``. ``needs_rewrite``
68	    is True only when the legacy ``[LCM:<slot>]`` format matched; the
69	    caller can re-emit via ``make_tagged_name`` on the next write to
70	    migrate the lock-stored name in place. The canonical ``lcm:<slot>:``
71	    format and untagged names both return ``needs_rewrite=False``.
72	    """
73	    match = _TAG_RE.match(name)
74	    if match:
75	        return int(match.group(1)), match.group(2), False
76	    match = _LEGACY_SLOT_TAG_RE.match(name)
77	    if match:
78	        return int(match.group(1)), match.group(2), True
79	    return None, name, False
80	
81	
82	def parse_slot_num(value: object) -> int | None:
83	    """
84	    Convert a slot identifier to an int, or return None if not convertible.
85	
86	    Mirrors ``int(value)`` while collapsing the ``TypeError``/``ValueError``
87	    that providers otherwise catch when a lock reports a non-numeric slot key.
88	    Call sites remain responsible for their own logging and skip/return flow.
89	    """
90	    try:
91	        return int(value)  # type: ignore[call-overload]
92	    except TypeError, ValueError:
93	        return None
94

## Status

**[#1237](https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/pull/1237)** — PIN-guard hoist, addressed all 11 review comments:
- `_require_readable_pin` docstring rewritten to reflect new contract (seam calls it, providers must NOT re-add it)

- Canonical regex now consumes optional whitespace after the second colon (`lcm:5: Alice` → `(5, "Alice")`), matching legacy regex behavior
- Precedence test renamed and rewritten — both regexes are anchored so they can't both match the same input; the test is about display-text content, not ambiguity
- Added 2 new test cases for whitespace tolerance
- 1113/1113 tests pass (35 in `test_util.py`, up from 33)

Both ready for re-review.

## Where we stand and what's next

The credential refactor + tag-helper groundwork is done. The remaining tag-idempotency work per the memory is **PR B**:

- Matter `async_set_user` switches to find-or-create-by-tag (drops `credential_index = slot`).
- `_truncate_user_name` → `_build_tagged_user_name(slot, display)` that preserves the `lcm:<slot>:` prefix and only truncates display.
- Drop `was_only_credential` cleanup from `_delete_credential` — user lifecycle decoupled from credential lifecycle.
- New `async_release_managed_slot` base no-op + Matter override; wire into `__init__.py`'s `pairs_removed` (currently unconsumed).
- Matter-only startup migration: `.storage` fingerprint gate, auto-rename untagged LCM-created users to `lcm:<slot>:`.

This is the meaty 200-300 line PR I scoped earlier. Before I start writing, two checkpoints:

1. **One PR or split?** PR B is cohesive ("Matter adopts tag, lifecycle decouples") but it touches four concerns: helper redesign, seam lifecycle change, Matter migration, startup-migration mechanism. I lean toward one PR since the seam changes don't make sense without the Matter consumer and vice versa. But if you want B1 (seam + helper + lifecycle) and B2 (Matter adoption + migration) split, I can do that.

2. **Should I start now or wait?** You may want to actually use the merged code (sync a slot, see the new contract in flight) before I pile more architectural change on top.

What's your preference?

  PR B — matter tag adoption + _truncate_user_name redesign
  - _truncate_user_name becomes _build_tagged_user_name(slot, display): builds lcm:{slot}:{display}, truncates only display so the total fits max_user_name_length.
  - Matter's async_set_user switches to find-or-create-by-tag (scan async_get_users() for lcm:{slot}: prefix), drops the credential_index=slot invariant (pass credential_index=None, discover via owner's credentials).

  - Matter-only startup migration: on first connect post-upgrade, if state matches LCM's last-known snapshot, rewrite each LCM-managed slot's user to the tag format. Snapshot fingerprint persisted in .storage.

  PR C — Z-Wave U3C tag adoption + akuvox/schlage format rewrite
  - Z-Wave U3C async_set_user switches to find-or-create-by-tag; drops user_id = slot invariant; allocates user_id at runtime by finding the first free index. (Z-Wave UC stays untouched — implicit-user gate already short-circuits.)

Internal API changes, signature refactors, and code-only behavior shifts ship freely as part of major releases.\"\nmetadata:\n  type: feedback\n---\n\nLCM's back-compat policy is scoped narrowly: **only user-facing features get back-compat treatment.** Internal seams, helper signatures, and provider contracts are free to evolve in major releases without compatibility shims or deprecation cycles.\n\n**Why:** during the 2026-06-10 PR B (matter user-tag adoption + lifecycle decoupling) work, the user noted that this is a major release. Adding `_ = owner` dead-param discards or kept-for-backward-compat keyword arguments would only pollute the internal API for no real benefit. Internal callers in the same repo get updated atomically with the signature change.\n\n**How to apply:** when refactoring internal helpers (anything not exported through a documented user surface), drop dead parameters, rename methods, change signatures freely. Update all in-repo callers in the same PR. Do not add `# kept for compat` cruft on internal seams.\n\n**The three known user-facing back-compat concerns** the user has flagged (as of 2026-06-10):\n\n1. **Tag format migration** — old `[LCM:<slot>]` user-name tag → new `lcm:{slot}:{display}` canonical tag. Tolerant parser accepts both formats indefinitely; opportunistic rewrite on next write. See [[project_user_tag_idempotency]].\n2. **Dropping `number_of_uses` from configs** — separate work, not currently active. Users with `number_of_uses` set in their slot config need a graceful drop, presumably during a config-flow migration.\n3. **Switching from calendar entity to entity key** — separate work, not currently active. Users with the older calendar-based schedule config need migration to the new entity-key shape.\n\nThese three are the ONLY surfaces where existing-user configurations must survive an upgrade. Everything else can refactor cleanly.\n\n## Related\n* [[project_user_tag_idempotency]] — design for the tag format migration (active in PR B/C work).\n* [[feedback_no_amend_after_pr]] — never amend after PR creation; the back-compat policy says we can drop internal-API cruft cleanly, the amend policy says we still keep commits forward-only.\n"
}

> AGENT

Still part of PR B. PR B's original scope covered both the seam-level work (helper + lifecycle + wiring) AND the Matter-specific find-or-create-by-tag + startup migration. The commit I just made is the first logical chunk; the Matter changes will be subsequent commits on the same branch, all going to one PR.

That said — the base-only state is actually a clean standalone landing point. Tagged user names get written, but Matter and Z-Wave U3C still use their existing `credential_index = slot` / `user_id = slot` lookup paths. No half-broken state, no regression. So you could split:

| Option | What ships first |
|---|---|
| **One PR B as planned** (Recommended) | Base + Matter find-or-create + startup migration in one cohesive review. Matter's identity model fully migrates atomically. |
| **PR B1 then PR B2** | B1 = the commit I just made (helper + lifecycle + wiring). B2 = Matter adoption + startup migration. Smaller reviews, B1 bakes briefly before Matter's read-path flips. |

The split's main appeal is review surface — B1 is ~190 lines diff and conceptually self-contained ("we now write tagged names and have a slot-teardown hook, no provider yet uses the teardown"). B2 would be the Matter consumer (~150-200 lines).

167	        """
168	        Read every user and their Personal Identification Number credentials from the lock.
169	
170	        Matter PINs are write-only: each occupied credential slot is projected to
171	        SlotCredential.unreadable(). Non-PIN credentials (for example RFID) are
172	        filtered out because the coordinator and sync manager only manage PIN slots.
173	        """

177	        except ServiceValidationError as err:
178	            raise LockOperationFailed(
179	                f"Matter get_lock_users rejected input for {self.lock.entity_id}: {err}"
180	            ) from err
181	        except HomeAssistantError as err:
182	            raise LockDisconnected(
183	                f"Matter get_lock_users failed for {self.lock.entity_id}: {err}"
184	            ) from err
185	
186	        # A for-loop (not a comprehension) so the int-or-None user_index and
187	        # credential index are narrowed by explicit guards before use: the
188	        # Matter helper types both as ``int | None``.
189	        users: list[User] = []
190	        for raw_user in lock_data.get("users", []):
191	            user_index = raw_user.get("user_index")
192	            if user_index is None:
193	                continue
194	            pin_credentials: list[Credential] = []
195	            for cred in raw_user.get("credentials", []):
196	                slot = cred.get("index")
197	                if cred.get("type") != "pin" or slot is None:
198	                    continue
199	                pin_credentials.append(
200	                    Credential(
201	                        type=CredentialType.PIN,
202	                        slot=slot,
203	                        state=SlotCredential.unreadable(),
204	                    )
205	                )
206	            users.append(
207	                User(
208	                    user_id=user_index,
209	                    name=raw_user.get("user_name"),
210	                    active=True,
211	                    credentials=pin_credentials,
212	                )
213	            )
214	        return users

> AGENT

That's an important concern — and you're right, the current implementation would leave orphan PINs on every upgrade. The cleanest fix is **inline migration on the set path**: when no `lcm:`-tagged user is found, fall back to the legacy `credential_index = slot` lookup and adopt that user (rename it to the tagged form, reuse its credential index). No orphan ever gets created.

Updating `_find_user_index_for_slot` to do both lookups in priority order.

{

  "old_string": "    async def _find_user_index_for_slot(self, slot: int) -> int | None:\n        \"\"\"Return the ``user_index`` of the user LCM owns for ``slot``, if any.\n\n        Walks the lock's current user list and matches by canonical or\n        legacy tag. Returns ``None`` when no LCM-owned user exists for\n        the slot.\n        \"\"\"\n        for existing in await self.async_get_users():\n            if existing.name is None:\n                continue\n            parsed_slot, _ = parse_tag(existing.name)\n            if parsed_slot == slot:\n                return existing.user_id\n        return None",
  "new_string": "    async def _find_user_index_for_slot(self, slot: int) -> int | None:\n        \"\"\"Return the ``user_index`` of the user LCM owns for ``slot``, if any.\n\n        Two lookups, in priority order:\n\n        1. **Canonical** -- a user whose name carries the\n           ``lcm:<slot>:`` tag. This is the post-PR-B identity rule.\n        2. **Legacy adoption** -- a user owning a PIN credential at\n           ``credential_index == slot``. Pre-PR-B Matter LCM pinned\n           ``credential_index`` to the LCM slot, so an untagged user\n           owning a PIN at that index is almost certainly the LCM 2.0\n           user for this slot. Adopting it (the subsequent\n           ``set_lock_user`` rewrites the name to the tagged form, and\n           ``set_lock_credential`` MODIFY'es the existing credential\n           index in place) preserves a single, identifiable user per\n           slot across the upgrade. Without this fallback the new model\n           would CREATE a second user every time, silently leaving the\n           pre-upgrade PIN active on the lock.\n\n        Returns ``None`` when neither lookup matches.\n        \"\"\"\n        users = await self.async_get_users()\n        for existing in users:\n            if existing.name is None:\n                continue\n            parsed_slot, _ = parse_tag(existing.name)\n            if parsed_slot == slot:\n                return existing.user_id\n        for existing in users:\n            for cred in existing.pin_credentials:\n                if cred.slot == slot:\n                    return existing.user_id\n        return None"
}

> AGENT

Pausing on task 21 (startup migration) — I want to flag the design implication. The inline migration in `_find_user_index_for_slot` (the legacy adoption fallback I just added) covers the orphan concern for any slot that gets written to after upgrade. The startup migration was originally about renaming **dormant** legacy users — slots LCM manages but the user never touches. Without it, those slots stay with untagged names indefinitely, but they're still correctly resolved on every operation via the legacy fallback.

1465	        proceeds to write the credential.
1466	
1467	        This preserves the historical contract from PR #1077 — the
1468	        DoorLock SetUser command on an existing user is a metadata-only
1469	        update (the user already exists), and a transient 500 or a name
1470	        the lock rejects should not block the subsequent credential
1471	        write. Regression guard against treating that failure as
1472	        LockDisconnected and aborting _put_credential.
1473	        """
1474	        mock_get_status = AsyncMock(
1475	            return_value={"credential_exists": True, "user_index": 7}
1476	        )

1480	            patch.object(
1481	                matter_lock_simple, "_get_matter_client", return_value=MagicMock()
1482	            ),

1484	                matter_lock_simple, "_get_matter_node", return_value=MagicMock()
1485	            ),
1486	            patch(f"{_PROVIDER_MODULE}.get_lock_credential_status", mock_get_status),
1487	            patch(f"{_PROVIDER_MODULE}.set_lock_user", mock_set_user),
1488	        ):
1489	            result = await matter_lock_simple.async_set_user(user)

{
  "command": "git add -A\ngit diff --cached --stat\necho \"===\"\ngit commit -m \"$(cat <<'EOF'\nfeat(matter): adopt user-tag identity model with legacy adoption fallback\n\nMatter's async_set_user, async_set_credential, async_delete_credential,\nand a new async_release_managed_slot override now use the canonical\nuser-tag identity model described in the user-tag-idempotency design.\n\nUser identity (async_set_user):\n\n* Find-or-create by tag. Walks async_get_users() looking for a user\n  whose user_name parses to the requested LCM slot (canonical lcm:<slot>:\n  prefix). If found, UPDATE that user_index. If not, allocate a fresh\n  user_index via set_lock_user(user_index=None) and let Matter pick.\n* Legacy adoption fallback. Before allocating fresh, fall back to \"user\n  owning a PIN at credential_index == slot\" -- pre-PR-B Matter LCM\n  pinned credential_index to the LCM slot, so an untagged user owning\n  a PIN at that index is almost certainly the LCM 2.0 user for this\n  slot. Adopting it (rename in place, MODIFY the credential index)\n  preserves a single user per slot across the upgrade. Without this\n  fallback the new model would CREATE a second user every time,\n  silently leaving the pre-upgrade PIN active on the lock as an orphan.\n\nCredential identity (async_set_credential, async_delete_credential):\n\n* credential_index = slot is dropped. The Matter credential index is\n  rediscovered per call by walking the owning user's credentials.\n* Set uses MODIFY (existing index) when the user already owns a PIN\n  and CREATE (credential_index=None, Matter auto-allocates) otherwise.\n* Delete looks up the user's PIN credential and clears it at the\n  rediscovered index. No-op return when LCM has no PIN for the user.\n* Sync-duplicate retry only fires when LCM actually owns a PIN to\n  clear (existing_credential_index is not None). When the duplicate is\n  external (no LCM-owned credential for this user), DuplicateCodeError\n  surfaces immediately -- clearing it would step on another\n  controller's credential.\n\nSlot teardown (async_release_managed_slot):\n\n* New override. Finds the LCM-owned user for the slot via the same\n  find-or-adopt logic the set path uses, then calls\n  async_delete_user(user_index). Matter's ClearUser cascade removes\n  the PIN credential. No-op when no LCM-owned user exists for the slot.\n\nTest changes:\n\n* TestSetUser, TestSetCredential, TestDeleteCredential, TestReleaseManagedSlot,\n  and the e2e patch lists are rewritten for the new flow.\n* Autouse fixtures default get_lock_users to empty (TestSetCredential)\n  or to a user owning a PIN at credential_index=user_index (TestDeleteCredential)\n  so the most common scenarios are concise; tests that need different\n  lock state patch get_lock_users locally.\n* New tests pin the orphan-prevention contract (legacy adoption) and\n  the external-duplicate surface behaviour.\nEOF\n)\" 2>&1 | tail -5",

## PR #1239 Summary

**Headline:** Matter provider adopts user-tag identity model, decoupling user lifecycle from credential operations.

### Files Modified

| File | Changes |
|------|---------|
| `custom_components/lock_code_manager/__init__.py` | +26 / -0 (slot teardown wiring) |
| `custom_components/lock_code_manager/providers/_base.py` | +75 / -55 (seam lifecycle changes) |
| `custom_components/lock_code_manager/providers/matter.py` | +178 / -72 (find-or-create-by-tag logic) |
| `tests/providers/matter/conftest.py` | +0 / -9 (cleanup) |
| `tests/providers/matter/test_e2e.py` | +5 / -5 (minor adjustments) |
| `tests/providers/matter/test_provider.py` | +377 / -102 (new tag-based test coverage) |
| `tests/providers/test_seam.py` | +73 / -113 (seam test refactor) |
| `tests/providers/zwave_js/test_provider.py` | +19 / -13 (minor test updates) |

### Key Behavioral Changes

1. **User-tag identity**: Lock-side user names now follow canonical `lcm:<slot>:<display>` format; the `lcm:` prefix makes the user binding idempotent across restarts.

2. **Persistent user lifecycle**: Users are created when a slot is first written and persist through PIN clear-and-rewrite cycles. Users are only deleted when the slot is removed from LCM config (new `async_release_managed_slot` method).

3. **Find-or-create-by-tag in Matter**: `async_set_user` searches existing users for the LCM tag; if found, reuses that `user_index`; if not, allocates a new one. A legacy-adoption fallback adopts untagged pre-2.0 users to prevent orphan PINs on upgrade.

4. **Credential index rediscovery**: Matter no longer pins `credential_index == slot`. Set and delete operations discover the index by walking the owning user's credentials, allowing Matter to auto-allocate indices.

5. **External duplicate detection**: Sync-duplicate retry only fires for LCM-owned duplicates. External duplicates surface immediately as `DuplicateCodeError` to avoid stepping on other controllers' credentials.

### Unchanged Providers

Z-Wave User Code CC, Z-Wave User Credential CC (coming PR C), Schlage, Akuvox, and slot-only providers are not modified in this PR. PR C will extend the tagging model to Z-Wave UC and update Schlage/Akuvox name-tag formats.

**Test status**: Full suite passes (1115/1115).

## What landed in the comment (5 issues)

| # | Issue | Severity |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `async_clear_usercode` owner lookup broken — `credential.slot` is now the Matter-auto-allocated index, not the LCM slot; loop silently no-ops | **Critical bug** |
| 2 | `_find_user_index_for_slot` legacy-adoption pass doesn't filter out users already canonically tagged for a different slot → cross-slot user contamination | **Critical bug** |
| 3 | `_find_user_index_for_slot` uses `for/early-return` instead of `next()` (CLAUDE.md idiomatic-Python rule) | Style |
| 4 | Same pattern in `_find_pin_credential_index_for_user` | Style |
| 5 | `_set_credential` docstring still says "truncates user.name" and `async_delete_user` still describes the retired lifecycle invariant | Docstring drift |

## What you should look at first

Issues **#1 and #2** are the meaty ones — they're real bugs that the test suite missed because the conftest fixtures and unit tests still use `credential_index == LCM slot` (the old invariant). The bug surfaces the moment a real Matter lock auto-allocates a credential index different from the LCM slot, or when an existing tagged user's Matter index collides with a different LCM slot number.

## Copilot's review on #1239

| # | Path | Finding | Matches my issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `_base.py:961` | `credential.slot == code_slot` lookup breaks for native-user providers that no longer pin `credential.slot` to LCM slot — proposed fix: resolve owner by parsing the `lcm:` tag from `user.name` first, fall back to credential-index lookup | **Same as my #1** |
| 2 | `matter.py:373` | Legacy-adoption fallback can mis-adopt a tagged user who happens to own a PIN at the auto-allocated index matching another slot | **Same as my #2** |
| 3 | `_base.py:1077` | `_build_tagged_user_name` docstring contradicts itself on prefix-truncation behavior | Matches my issue N (scored 50, filtered out) |

Top-level: Codecov reports 90.9% patch coverage (6 lines uncovered) — separate concern, not blocking.

## Bottom line

Two independent review systems (Claude multi-agent and Copilot) flagged the same two critical bugs — high confidence they're real. The fix shape is similar:

1. **For issue #1**: change `async_clear_usercode` owner resolution to prefer the LCM tag in `user.name` before the credential-index fallback (matches Copilot's exact suggestion).
2. **For issue #2**: in `_find_user_index_for_slot`'s legacy pass, skip any user whose `user.name` already parses to ANY LCM slot via `parse_tag`.

Both bugs will be exercised the moment a real Matter lock auto-allocates a credential index that's different from the LCM slot — the unit tests masked it because the conftest fixtures use the old `credential_index == LCM slot` invariant.

Want me to fix both and push a forward commit on the branch?

This is the post-PR-B identity rule.\n        2. **Legacy adoption** -- a user owning a PIN credential at\n           ``credential_index == slot``. Pre-PR-B Matter LCM pinned\n           ``credential_index`` to the LCM slot, so an untagged user\n           owning a PIN at that index is almost certainly the LCM 2.0\n           user for this slot. Adopting it (the subsequent\n           ``set_lock_user`` rewrites the name to the tagged form, and\n           ``set_lock_credential`` MODIFY'es the existing credential\n           index in place) preserves a single, identifiable user per\n           slot across the upgrade. Without this fallback the new model\n           would CREATE a second user every time, silently leaving the\n           pre-upgrade PIN active on the lock.\n\n        Returns ``None`` when neither lookup matches.\n        \"\"\"\n        users = await self.async_get_users()\n        for existing in users:\n            if existing.name is None:\n                continue\n            parsed_slot, _ = parse_tag(existing.name)\n            if parsed_slot == slot:\n                return existing.user_id\n        for existing in users:\n            for cred in existing.pin_credentials:\n                if cred.slot == slot:\n                    return existing.user_id\n        return None",
  "new_string": "    async def _find_user_index_for_slot(self, slot: int) -> int | None:\n        \"\"\"\n        Return the ``user_index`` of the user LCM owns for ``slot``, if any.\n\n        Two lookups, in priority order:\n\n        1. **Canonical** -- a user whose name carries the\n           ``lcm:<slot>:`` tag. This is the post-PR-B identity rule.\n        2. **Legacy adoption** -- an *untagged* user owning a PIN\n           credential at ``credential_index == slot``. Pre-PR-B Matter\n           LCM pinned ``credential_index`` to the LCM slot, so an\n           untagged user owning a PIN at that index is almost certainly\n           the LCM 2.0 user for this slot. Adopting it (the subsequent\n           ``set_lock_user`` rewrites the name to the tagged form, and\n           ``set_lock_credential`` MODIFY'es the existing credential\n           index in place) preserves a single, identifiable user per\n           slot across the upgrade. Without this fallback the new model\n           would CREATE a second user every time, silently leaving the\n           pre-upgrade PIN active on the lock.\n\n           The legacy pass MUST skip users whose names already parse to\n           ANY LCM slot. Under the new model the Matter credential index\n           is auto-allocated, so a user tagged ``lcm:<A>:`` can own a\n           PIN at index ``B``; matching on ``cred.slot == slot`` alone\n           would mis-adopt slot-A's user as slot-B's anchor.\n\n        Returns ``None`` when neither lookup matches.\n        \"\"\"\n        users = await self.async_get_users()\n        canonical = next(\n            (\n                existing.user_id\n                for existing in users\n                if existing.name and parse_tag(existing.name)[0] == slot\n            ),\n            None,\n        )\n        if canonical is not None:\n            return canonical\n        return next(\n            (\n                existing.user_id\n                for existing in users\n                if parse_tag(existing.name or \"\")[0] is None\n                for cred in existing.pin_credentials\n                if cred.slot == slot\n            ),\n            None,\n        )"
}

```
The provider now allows `credential_index=None` (Matter auto-allocation) and treats `code_slot` as the LCM slot only, but the rest of the integration (notably `BaseLock.async_get_usercodes()` / `_project_users_to_slots` and the push event handlers) still keys slot occupancy by the lock-reported credential index. If Matter allocates a different credential index than `code_slot`, LCM will start showing/updating the wrong slot numbers on refresh/events (e.g., slot 1 configured but slot 7 becomes occupied), and managed-slot state will drift. Either keep `credential_index` pinned to the LCM slot until the read/projection path is updated to translate by the `lcm:<slot>:` tag, or introduce a persisted mapping layer so coordinator/push updates can translate between LCM slot and Matter credential index.
```

> AGENT

Copilot found a critical bug I missed. The credential-index decoupling for Matter has ripple effects:

## The bug

Two paths in matter.py still treat the Matter credential index as the LCM slot:
1. **`async_get_users`** sets `Credential.slot = cred.get("index")` (Matter credential index)
2. **`_handle_user_change_event`** (push handler at `matter.py:790`) takes `dataIndex` from LockUserChange and pushes it as the LCM slot

After auto-allocation, these no longer match. The base seam's `_project_users_to_slots` keys by `credential.slot`, and the push handler updates the wrong LCM slot.

Existing tests didn't catch it because the fixtures still seed users with `credential_index == LCM slot`.

## Fix options

Copilot offers two:

| Option | Change | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| **A — Revert credential_index decoupling** | Set `credential_index = code_slot` in `set_lock_credential` (pre-PR-B behavior). Coexistence at user level still works (tagged users), but if external systems claim credential_index N, LCM would MODIFY that credential when it manages slot N. Smaller patch. | ~15 lines. Defers the "Matter auto-allocates indices" goal. |
| **B — Translate Matter credential index → LCM slot in the projection + push paths** | `async_get_users` parses the owning user's `lcm:<slot>:` tag to derive `Credential.slot = LCM slot`. New `_raw_lock_users()` helper for internal Matter-index lookups. Push handler resolves the LCM slot via the event's `userIndex` and the user's tag. | ~80-100 lines + tests. Completes the original PR B design. |

Option B is the proper fix but it's bigger. Option A is a quick rollback that leaves PR B's coexistence behavior at the user level intact (the main motivation) while sidestepping the projection issue.

Which path do you want?

> DEVELOPER

B

This helper deliberately walks the **raw** lock-side\n        user data (not ``async_get_users``) so the returned value is the\n        Matter credential index Matter expects for\n        ``set_lock_credential`` / ``clear_lock_credential`` -- not the\n        LCM-projected slot that ``async_get_users`` exposes upward.\n        \"\"\"\n        return next(\n            (\n                cred.get(\"index\")\n                for raw_user in await self._raw_lock_users()\n                if raw_user.get(\"user_index\") == user_id\n                for cred in raw_user.get(\"credentials\", [])\n                if cred.get(\"type\") == \"pin\" and cred.get(\"index\") is not None\n            ),\n            None,\n        )"

Untagged users (legacy LCM 2.0\n  that hasn't migrated yet) keep the old credential_index = slot\n  invariant for their projection so continuity is preserved. | New `_raw_lock_users()` helper | `matter.py` | Returns unprojected lock-side data; Matter-internal lookups consume this |
| `async_get_users` projection | `matter.py` | `Credential.slot = LCM slot from owning user's lcm:<slot>: tag`; untagged users keep the legacy `credential_index = slot` invariant |

| Existing `TestLockUserChangeEvent` tests | `test_provider.py` | Rewritten to be async, seed `lcm:<slot>:` tagged users via `get_lock_users` mock, assert the push targets the LCM slot rather than the Matter index |

| New `test_get_users_untagged_user_falls_back_to_credential_index` | `test_provider.py` | Pins the legacy compat for untagged users |
| New `test_pin_event_for_untagged_user_ignored` | `test_provider.py` | Pins the "non-LCM events get filtered" contract |

1	"""
2	Shared helpers for provider implementations.
3	
4	Provider-internal utilities that don't belong in the integration-wide
5	``util.py``. Currently: slot-tagging used by providers whose lock APIs
6	identify codes by user-name rather than by slot number (Schlage, Akuvox,
7	and -- once the unified-user migration lands -- Matter and Z-Wave User
8	Credential CC).
9	
10	Two tag formats coexist during the migration window:
11	
12	* Canonical ``lcm:<slot>:<name>`` -- the consolidated format every new
13	  write uses. Two colons delimit the slot field clearly for visual
14	  parseability on the lock UI.
15	* Legacy ``[LCM:<slot>] <name>`` -- written by Schlage/Akuvox today.
16	  Still emitted by ``make_legacy_tagged_name`` while those providers
17	  migrate; their reads tolerate it via ``parse_tag_with_rewrite``, which
18	  signals a legacy match so the caller can rewrite the lock-stored name
19	  in place at the next write opportunity. The legacy emitter is the
20	  deprecation marker -- ``_legacy_`` in the name is intentional so
21	  reviewers see at the call site that the writer hasn't migrated yet.
22	"""
23	
24	from __future__ import annotations
25	
26	import re
27	
28	_LEGACY_SLOT_TAG_RE = re.compile(r"^\[LCM:(\d+)\]\s*(.*)")
29	_TAG_RE = re.compile(r"^lcm:(\d+):\s*(.*)")
30	
31	
32	def make_tagged_name(slot_num: int, name: str | None = None) -> str:
33	    """Return a code name in the canonical ``lcm:<slot>:`` format."""
34	    base = name or f"Code Slot {slot_num}"
35	    return f"lcm:{slot_num}:{base}"
36	
37	
38	def make_legacy_tagged_name(slot_num: int, name: str | None = None) -> str:
39	    """
40	    Return a code name in the legacy ``[LCM:<slot>]`` format.
41	
42	    Deprecated: kept for Schlage/Akuvox until they migrate to the
43	    canonical format with read-time detect-and-rewrite. New call sites
44	    should use ``make_tagged_name``.
45	    """
46	    base = name or f"Code Slot {slot_num}"
47	    return f"[LCM:{slot_num}] {base}"
48	
49	
50	def parse_tag(name: str) -> tuple[int | None, str]:
51	    """
52	    Parse a Lock Code Manager slot tag, tolerant of both formats.
53	
54	    Returns ``(slot_num, friendly_name)`` when either format matches, or
55	    ``(None, original_name)`` otherwise. Callers that care about
56	    rewriting legacy tags in place should use ``parse_tag_with_rewrite``
57	    instead.
58	    """
59	    slot, friendly, _ = parse_tag_with_rewrite(name)
60	    return slot, friendly
61	
62	
63	def parse_tag_with_rewrite(name: str) -> tuple[int | None, str, bool]:
64	    """
65	    Parse a slot tag and signal whether it needs format migration.
66	
67	    Returns ``(slot_num, friendly_name, needs_rewrite)``. ``needs_rewrite``
68	    is True only when the legacy ``[LCM:<slot>]`` format matched; the
69	    caller can re-emit via ``make_tagged_name`` on the next write to
70	    migrate the lock-stored name in place. The canonical ``lcm:<slot>:``
71	    format and untagged names both return ``needs_rewrite=False``.
72	    """
73	    match = _TAG_RE.match(name)
74	    if match:
75	        return int(match.group(1)), match.group(2), False
76	    match = _LEGACY_SLOT_TAG_RE.match(name)
77	    if match:
78	        return int(match.group(1)), match.group(2), True
79	    return None, name, False
80	
81	
82	def parse_slot_num(value: object) -> int | None:
83	    """
84	    Convert a slot identifier to an int, or return None if not convertible.
85	
86	    Mirrors ``int(value)`` while collapsing the ``TypeError``/``ValueError``
87	    that providers otherwise catch when a lock reports a non-numeric slot key.
88	    Call sites remain responsible for their own logging and skip/return flow.
89	    """
90	    try:
91	        return int(value)  # type: ignore[call-overload]
92	    except TypeError, ValueError:
93	        return None

> AGENT

Pushed (`377b302f` on PR #1239).

## Behavior summary

| `max_user_name_length` | Slot | Display | Result | Notes |
|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| 16 | 5 | "alice" | `lcm:5:alice` | Canonical fits |
| 10 | 5 | "alexandra" | `lcm:5:alex` | Display truncated to 4 chars |
| 8 | 255 | "alice" | `lcm:255:` | Exactly fits the prefix, display dropped |
| 6 | 1 | "alice" | `lcm:1:` | Exactly fits the prefix |
| 5 | 1 | "alice" | `1` | Prefix overflows → slot-only fallback |
| 3 | 255 | "alice" | `255` | Slot-only fallback |
| 0 | any | any | `None` | No name field — handled by seam gate |

## Parser changes

`parse_tag` now matches three formats in priority order:
1. Canonical `lcm:<slot>:<display>`
2. Legacy `[LCM:<slot>] <display>` (flagged for rewrite)
3. **New:** Slot-only digit-only names (e.g. `"5"`, `"255"`)

The slot-only branch is ambiguous with external users whose names happen to be digit-only — a tradeoff we accept because:
- It's only reached on locks with absurdly small name limits (rare)
- The alternative (sliced canonical prefix like `"lcm"`) loses the slot binding entirely

Suite: 1125/1125 pass (+4 from the earlier 1121: two `_build_tagged_user_name` tests rewritten, two new `parse_tag` slot-only cases).

12	## The rule
13	
14	LCM-managed lock users always have a name of the form `lcm:{slot}:{display}` where:
15	
16	* `lcm` is a fixed sentinel
17	* `{slot}` is the decimal LCM slot number (no zero padding)
18	* `{display}` is the user-facing name from the LCM slot config
19	
20	Worst-case prefix overhead is 8 characters (`lcm:255:`). On a 10-character-limit lock, that leaves 2 characters of display — tight but functional. A colon-free variant (`lcm{slot}:`) was briefly considered for the one-character savings but rejected on aesthetics: the colon-delimited form is visually parseable on the lock UI.
21	
22	## Why
23	
24	* **Idempotency** — the same LCM slot resolves to the same lock user every time, across PIN cycles, restarts, and provider reloads. Discovery is by tag scan on every operation, so no LCM-side persistence is required.
25	* **Coexistence with other controllers** — users whose names don't match the `lcm<digits>:` pattern are invisible to LCM's write paths. LCM's `async_set_user` finds-or-creates only LCM-tagged users; `_delete_credential` cleanup only acts on LCM-tagged owners. Other controllers can manage their own users in the same lock without LCM trampling them.
26	* **One mechanism, two problems** — the tag is both the ownership marker (prevents collisions) and the discovery key (provides idempotency). No duplicate state to drift.
```

A colon-free variant (`lcm{slot}:`) was briefly considered for the one-character savings but rejected on aesthetics: the colon-delimited form is visually parseable on the lock UI.\n\n### Slot-only fallback for length-constrained locks\n\nWhen `len(f\"lcm:{slot}:\") > max_user_name_length` (rare — would need a lock with a name field of ≤7 chars for a 3-digit slot), `_build_tagged_user_name` falls back to writing just `str(slot)` as the user name. `parse_tag` has a third match arm that recognizes digit-only names as the slot binding (with empty display). The fallback's ambiguity with external users whose names happen to be digit-only is the cost of preserving the slot binding on length-constrained locks — better than slicing the canonical prefix to `\"lcm\"` and losing the slot recoverably. Resolved 2026-06-10 in PR #1239's fourth fix commit (`377b302f`)."
