# Lock Code Manager Architecture

## Overview

Lock Code Manager (LCM) manages user codes across locks via providers. Each lock
gets a coordinator that holds the full slot-to-code mapping (managed AND unmanaged).

## Data Flow

```text
Config Entry (desired state)
    |
Binary Sensor (sync decision)
    | set/clear
Provider (async_set_usercode / async_clear_usercode)
    | Z-Wave service call
Lock (firmware)
    | push notification / poll response
Coordinator (actual state: ALL slots)
    | listener notification
Binary Sensor (re-evaluate sync)
```

## Coordinator

Stores `dict[int, int | str]` mapping slot number to code for ALL slots on the
lock. Does not distinguish managed vs unmanaged — that distinction lives in the
config entries.

- Push-based providers (Z-Wave JS) set `update_interval = None`
- Poll-based providers use periodic refresh via `_async_update_data()`

## Push vs Poll vs Hard Refresh

- **Push**: Z-Wave value update events → provider filters → `coordinator.push_update()`
- **Poll**: Coordinator's `_async_update_data()` → provider's `async_get_usercodes()` on interval
- **Hard refresh**: `async_hard_refresh_codes()` → refreshes Z-Wave CC values cache from device,
  then reads all slots. Triggered via the `hard_refresh_usercodes` service.

## Managed vs Unmanaged Slots

This tutorial walks through adding support for a new lock integration to Lock Code Manager.
We'll create a provider for a hypothetical "SmartLock" integration.

## Prerequisites

Before starting, ensure:

1. The lock integration exists in Home Assistant and creates `lock.*` entities
2. The integration provides a way to read and write usercodes
3. You understand the integration's data model and API

Create a new file in `custom_components/lock_code_manager/providers/`:

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from homeassistant.core import callback

# Provider State Management

This guide explains how Lock Code Manager providers manage usercode state, including update
modes, the coordinator lifecycle, and best practices.

## Overview

The `LockUsercodeUpdateCoordinator` manages usercode state through three update modes:

| Mode | Mechanism | When to Use |
| ---- | --------- | ----------- |
| **Poll for updates** | Periodic `get_usercodes()` | Default for most integrations |
| **Push for updates** | Real-time subscription | Integrations with event support |
| **Poll for drift** | Periodic `hard_refresh_codes()` | Detect out-of-band changes |

All modes include an initial poll to populate coordinator data.

> **Important:** Even with push mode enabled, you must implement `get_usercodes()`.
> The coordinator always calls it for the initial data load and any manual refresh requests.

## Architecture

```text
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    LockUsercodeUpdateCoordinator                │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  data: dict[int, str | None]         # slot -> usercode        │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  async_get_usercodes()               # poll method             │
│  push_update(updates)                # push entry point        │

  "new_string": "## How It Works\n\nZ-Wave locks store PIN codes in numbered user code slots. Lock Code Manager reads, sets, and clears these codes via the Z-Wave JS driver. Most Z-Wave locks support push updates — when a code is used or changed, the lock notifies Home Assistant immediately.\n\nSome Z-Wave locks mask PIN codes (returning `****` instead of the actual value). Lock Code Manager handles this transparently — masked codes are treated as \"occupied but unreadable\" and the configured PIN is shown in the sensor display.\n\n### User Credential CC vs User Code CC\n\nZ-Wave locks expose codes through one of two command classes:\n\n- **User Code CC (UC)** — the older slot-only model: a slot holds a PIN with no user concept. LCM addresses these by slot number directly. No on-lock identity tag is needed (there is no name field).\n- **User Credential CC (U3C)** — the newer Z-Wave Plus v2 model: each PIN belongs to a named user. As of LCM 4.0.0, LCM tags its own U3C users with `lcm:<slot>:<friendly name>` in the user-name field — so a slot-3 user named \"Alice\" appears on the lock as `lcm:3:Alice`. This lets LCM coexist with other controllers managing their own users on the same lock.\n\nFor U3C locks, two consequences worth knowing:\n\n- **Lock-side `user_id` is no longer pinned to the LCM slot**. Previously LCM created users at `user_id == slot`; now Z-Wave auto-allocates a free `user_id` and LCM discovers the user by walking the lock's user list for the tag. You may see the on-lock user_id differ from the LCM slot, which is expected.\n- **Existing installs migrate seamlessly**. On the first write to a slot after upgrade, LCM scans for an untagged user at the old `user_id == slot` position; if found, it adopts that user (preserving its credentials) and rewrites its name to the new tagged form. No PIN re-entry needed.\n\nUC locks are unchanged by this — they have no user name field to tag.\n\nLCM uses the Z-Wave JS unified `access_control` API (introduced in node-zwave-js 15.23.4+) for both command classes; the same Python code path serves UC and U3C locks."
}

```
1	# Lock Code Manager Architecture
2	
3	## Overview
4	
5	Lock Code Manager (LCM) manages user codes across locks via providers. Each lock
6	gets a coordinator that holds the full slot-to-code mapping (managed AND unmanaged).
7	
8	## Data Flow
9	
10	```text
11	Config Entry (desired state)
12	    |
13	Binary Sensor (sync decision)
14	    | set/clear
15	Provider (async_set_usercode / async_clear_usercode)
16	    | Z-Wave service call
17	Lock (firmware)
18	    | push notification / poll response
19	Coordinator (actual state: ALL slots)
20	    | listener notification
21	Binary Sensor (re-evaluate sync)
22	```
23	
24	## Coordinator
25	
26	Stores `dict[int, int | str]` mapping slot number to code for ALL slots on the
27	lock. Does not distinguish managed vs unmanaged — that distinction lives in the
28	config entries.
29	
30	- Push-based providers (Z-Wave JS) set `update_interval = None`
31	- Poll-based providers use periodic refresh via `_async_update_data()`
32	
33	## Push vs Poll vs Hard Refresh
34	
35	- **Push**: Z-Wave value update events → provider filters → `coordinator.push_update()`
36	- **Poll**: Coordinator's `_async_update_data()` → provider's `async_get_usercodes()` on interval
37	- **Hard refresh**: `async_hard_refresh_codes()` → refreshes Z-Wave CC values cache from device,
38	  then reads all slots. Triggered via the `hard_refresh_usercodes` service.
39	
40	## Managed vs Unmanaged Slots
41	
42	A slot is **managed** if it exists in any LCM config entry's `CONF_SLOTS` for this
43	lock AND the corresponding LCM entities exist.
44	
45	Detection: `_get_slot_entity_states()` returns `None` for unmanaged slots.
46	
47	Coordinator stores both managed and unmanaged; sync only operates on managed slots;
48	the UI displays both.
49	
50	## Sync Decision
51	
52	The in-sync binary sensor compares **desired state** (PIN from text entity, active
53	state from condition) against **actual state** (coordinator data):
54	
55	- If active + PIN differs from coordinator → set
56	- If inactive + code present in coordinator → clear
57	- If states match → in sync (no operation)
58	
59	## PIN Clearing Auto-Disables Slots
60	
61	When a user clears the PIN text entity on an enabled slot, the text entity
62	automatically disables the slot (turns off the enabled switch) before clearing
63	the PIN value. This ensures the sync logic will clear the code on the lock rather
64	than leaving a stale code active.
65	
66	## Masked PINs
67	
68	Some locks return `****` instead of actual codes. LCM handles this:
69	
70	- **Managed slots**: Resolved via the text entity's expected PIN — if the expected
71	  PIN is set and the coordinator shows `****`, the binary sensor treats it as in-sync
72	  (the lock has *a* code, and we set it, so we trust it matches).
73	- **Unmanaged slots**: Kept as-is — `****` just indicates "slot in use."
74	
75	## Duplicate Code Detection
76	
77	Two layers of defense against duplicate PINs causing infinite sync loops:
78	
79	1. **Pre-flight check** (`_check_duplicate_code()` in `BaseLock`): Scans coordinator
80	   data for matching PINs before sending to the lock. Raises `DuplicateCodeError`.
81	   Skips masked values (`****`) since they can't be compared.
82	
83	2. **Event 15 handler** (Z-Wave JS only, `_async_handle_duplicate_code()`): Reactive
84	   safety net for cases where the pre-flight check can't detect the duplicate (e.g.,
85	   masked codes from unmanaged slots).
86	
87	Both paths disable the slot and create a persistent notification.
88	
89	## Sync Attempt Tracking
90	
91	The sync mechanism tracks consecutive successful SET attempts (provider call did
92	not raise) that fail to resolve the out-of-sync state. If `MAX_SYNC_ATTEMPTS`
93	are reached within `SYNC_ATTEMPT_WINDOW`, the lock is assumed to be rejecting
94	the PIN. The slot is disabled and the user is notified.
95	
96	Only SET operations are tracked — clears always proceed and are not counted.
97	`LockDisconnected` exceptions are transient and use the separate retry mechanism
98	with `RETRY_DELAY`. The tracker resets when the slot is disabled or when the
99	code is successfully synced.
100	
101	## Exception Hierarchy for Code Rejection
102	
103	- `CodeRejectedError` — base: the lock won't accept this PIN (any reason)
104	- `DuplicateCodeError(CodeRejectedError)` — specific: PIN duplicates another slot
105	
106	The pre-flight duplicate check raises `DuplicateCodeError`. The sync path catches
107	the parent `CodeRejectedError` so any rejection reason results in disable + notify.
108	
109	## Base Provider (`BaseLock`)
110	
111	The `@final` methods `async_internal_set_usercode` and `async_internal_clear_usercode`
112	are the single entry point for all lock operations. They enforce cross-cutting concerns
113	in this order:
114	
115	1. **Integration connectivity check** — verify integration is connected
116	2. **Device availability check** — verify physical device is responsive
117	3. **Acquire operation lock** — serialize operations via `asyncio.Lock`
118	4. **Pre-execute hook** (set only) — duplicate code check runs inside the lock
119	5. **Rate limit delay** — minimum delay between operations
120	6. **Provider call** — delegate to subclass `async_set_usercode` / `async_clear_usercode`
121	7. **Coordinator refresh** — update state (skipped for push-based providers)
122	
123	Helper methods available to all providers:
124	
125	- `is_masked_or_empty(code)` — detect `****` masked or empty codes
126	- `is_slot_managed(code_slot)` — check if any LCM config entry manages this slot
127	
128	The `source` parameter (`"sync"` or `"direct"`) indicates whether the call came from
129	the sync path (binary sensor) or a user action (websocket). Currently informational;
130	future use for differentiated error handling policies.
131	
132	## Rate Limiting
133	
134	All lock operations are serialized via `asyncio.Lock` per provider instance, with
135	a 2-second minimum delay between operations. This prevents overwhelming the lock's
136	radio and Z-Wave mesh.
137	
138	## WebSocket Subscriptions
139	
140	WebSocket subscriptions for slot card data re-resolve entity IDs dynamically on
141	each update. This handles entities that are created after the subscription is
142	established (for example, during initial config setup). The resolution uses
143	lightweight entity registry lookups.
144	
145	## Lovelace Dashboard Updates
146	
147	When structural config changes occur (slots or locks added/removed), LCM fires
148	`lovelace_updated` events for each registered dashboard. This triggers the
149	"Configuration changed" toast in the Home Assistant frontend, prompting users to
150	refresh so the strategy re-generates cards.
151	
152	## Frontend
153	
154	The frontend is built with TypeScript 6.0 and provides Lovelace strategies
155	(dashboard, view, and section level) and custom cards (`lcm-slot`,
156	`lcm-lock-codes`) for managing PINs.
157	
```

1	# Provider State Management
2	
3	This guide explains how Lock Code Manager providers manage usercode state, including update
4	modes, the coordinator lifecycle, and best practices.
5	
6	## Overview
7	
8	The `LockUsercodeUpdateCoordinator` manages usercode state through three update modes:
9	
10	| Mode | Mechanism | When to Use |
11	| ---- | --------- | ----------- |
12	| **Poll for updates** | Periodic `get_usercodes()` | Default for most integrations |
13	| **Push for updates** | Real-time subscription | Integrations with event support |
14	| **Poll for drift** | Periodic `hard_refresh_codes()` | Detect out-of-band changes |
15	
16	All modes include an initial poll to populate coordinator data.
17	
18	> **Important:** Even with push mode enabled, you must implement `get_usercodes()`.
19	> The coordinator always calls it for the initial data load and any manual refresh requests.
20	
21	## Architecture
22	
23	```text
24	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
25	│                    LockUsercodeUpdateCoordinator                │
26	├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
27	│  data: dict[int, str | None]         # slot -> usercode        │
28	├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
29	│  async_get_usercodes()               # poll method             │
30	│  push_update(updates)                # push entry point        │
31	│  _async_drift_check()                # hard refresh timer      │
32	│  _async_connection_check()           # connection poll timer   │
33	└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
34	                              │
35	                              │ calls
36	                              ▼
37	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
38	│                         BaseLock                                │
39	├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
40	│  Properties:                                                    │
41	│    supports_push: bool              # opt-in for push mode      │
42	│    usercode_scan_interval: timedelta   # polling interval       │
43	│    hard_refresh_interval: timedelta    # drift detection        │
44	│    connection_check_interval: timedelta  # connection polling   │
45	├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
46	│  Required Methods:                                              │
47	│    get_usercodes()                  # return current codes      │
48	│    set_usercode()                   # set a code on lock        │
49	│    clear_usercode()                 # clear a code from lock    │
50	│    is_integration_connected()       # check integration state    │
51	├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
52	│  Optional Methods:                                              │
53	│    hard_refresh_codes()             # re-fetch from device      │
54	│    subscribe_push_updates()         # set up event listeners    │
55	│    unsubscribe_push_updates()       # clean up listeners        │
56	└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
57	                              │
58	                              │ implements
59	                              ▼
60	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
61	│                      YourLockProvider                           │
62	└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
63	```
64	
65	## Update Modes
66	
67	### Poll Mode (Default)
68	
69	The coordinator periodically calls `get_usercodes()` at the interval specified by `usercode_scan_interval`.
70	
71	**Flow:**
72	
73	1. Timer fires at `usercode_scan_interval`
74	2. Coordinator calls `async_internal_get_usercodes()`
75	3. Base class applies rate limiting, then calls `async_get_usercodes()`
76	4. Provider returns current usercode state
77	5. Coordinator updates `data` and notifies listening entities
78	
79	**When to use:**
80	
81	- Integrations without real-time event support
82	- Simple implementations where polling is sufficient
83	
84	**Example configuration:**
85	
86	```python
87	class MyLock(BaseLock):
88	    @property
89	    def usercode_scan_interval(self) -> timedelta:
90	        return timedelta(minutes=1)  # Poll every minute
91	
92	    @property
93	    def hard_refresh_interval(self) -> timedelta | None:
94	        return None  # No drift detection needed
95	```
96	
97	### Push Mode
98	
99	For integrations that support real-time events (e.g., Z-Wave JS value updates), push mode
100	provides immediate updates without polling overhead.
101	
102	**Flow:**
103	
104	1. Provider subscribes to device events in `subscribe_push_updates()`
105	2. Device event fires (e.g., code changed)
106	3. Provider's event handler calls `coordinator.push_update({slot: value})`
107	4. Coordinator merges update into `data`
108	5. Coordinator notifies listening entities immediately
109	
110	**When to use:**
111	
112	- Integrations with real-time event support
113	- When you want immediate UI updates after code changes
114	
115	**Example configuration:**
116	
117	```python
118	class MyLock(BaseLock):
119	    @property
120	    def supports_push(self) -> bool:
121	        return True  # Disable polling, use push instead
122	
123	    @property
124	    def hard_refresh_interval(self) -> timedelta | None:
125	        return timedelta(hours=1)  # Still check for drift
126	```
127	
128	### Drift Detection
129	
130	Drift detection catches out-of-band changes (e.g., codes changed at the lock's keypad, or via another integration).
131	
132	**Flow:**
133	
134	1. Timer fires at `hard_refresh_interval`
135	2. Coordinator calls `async_internal_hard_refresh_codes()`
136	3. Provider queries the device directly, bypassing cache
137	4. If data differs from current state, coordinator updates and notifies entities
138	
139	**When to use:**
140	
141	- Codes can be changed outside Home Assistant
142	- Integration caches data that may become stale
143	- You want to catch sync issues even with push mode
144	
145	## Interval Properties
146	
147	| Property | Default | Purpose |
148	| -------- | ------- | ------- |
149	| `usercode_scan_interval` | 1 minute | How often to poll for usercode updates (ignored if `supports_push=True`) |
150	| `hard_refresh_interval` | `None` | How often to hard refresh for drift detection (`None` = disabled) |
151	| `connection_check_interval` | 30 seconds | How often to check connection state (`None` = disabled) |
152	
153	## Configuration Examples
154	
155	### Poll-Only (Simple Implementation)
156	
157	```python
158	class MyLock(BaseLock):
159	    @property
160	    def usercode_scan_interval(self) -> timedelta:
161	        return timedelta(minutes=1)
162	
163	    @property
164	    def hard_refresh_interval(self) -> timedelta | None:
165	        return None  # No drift detection
166	```
167	
168	### Push with Drift Detection (Recommended for Z-Wave)
169	
170	```python
171	class MyLock(BaseLock):
172	    @property
173	    def supports_push(self) -> bool:
174	        return True
175	
176	    @property
177	    def hard_refresh_interval(self) -> timedelta | None:
178	        return timedelta(hours=1)  # Periodic drift check
179	
180	    @property
181	    def connection_check_interval(self) -> timedelta | None:
182	        return None  # Z-Wave JS provides config entry state changes
183	```
184	
185	### Poll with Drift Detection
186	
187	```python
188	class MyLock(BaseLock):
189	    @property
190	    def usercode_scan_interval(self) -> timedelta:
191	        return timedelta(minutes=1)
192	
193	    @property
194	    def hard_refresh_interval(self) -> timedelta | None:
195	        return timedelta(hours=1)
196	```
197	
198	## Implementing Required Methods
199	
200	### get_usercodes()
201	
202	Return current usercode state. This may read from a cache or query the device.
203	
204	```python
205	def get_usercodes(self) -> dict[int, str | None]:
206	    """
207	    Return dictionary mapping slot numbers to usercodes.
208	
209	    Raises:
210	        LockDisconnected: If lock cannot be communicated with.
211	
212	    """
213	    return {
214	        1: "1234",   # Slot 1 has code
215	        2: "",       # Slot 2 is empty
216	        3: "5678",   # Slot 3 has code
217	    }
218	```
219	
220	**Important:** The return value format is `dict[int, str | None]`:
221	
222	- **Keys** are slot numbers (integers)
223	- **Values** are usercodes (strings or integers), or empty string `""` for cleared slots
224	
225	### set_usercode()
226	
227	Set a usercode on a specific slot.
228	
229	```python
230	def set_usercode(
231	    self, code_slot: int, usercode: str, name: str | None = None
232	) -> bool:
233	    """Set a usercode on a code slot.
234	
235	    Raises:
236	        LockDisconnected: If the lock cannot be communicated with.
237	
238	    """
239	    # Check if already set to this value (optional optimization)
240	    if self._cache.get(code_slot) == usercode:
241	        return False
242	
243	    # Set the code on the device
244	    self._device.set_code(code_slot, usercode)
245	    return True
246	```
247	
248	### clear_usercode()
249	
250	Clear a usercode from a specific slot.
251	
252	```python
253	def clear_usercode(self, code_slot: int) -> bool:
254	    """
255	    Clear a usercode from a code slot.
256	
257	    Raises:
258	        LockDisconnected: If the lock cannot be communicated with.
259	
260	    """
261	    if code_slot not in self._cache or self._cache[code_slot] == "":
262	        return False
263	
264	    self._device.clear_code(code_slot)
265	    return True
266	```
267	
268	### is_integration_connected()
269	
270	Check if the integration's client/driver/broker is connected.
271	
272	```python
273	def is_integration_connected(self) -> bool:
274	    """Return whether the integration is connected.
275	
276	    This is called periodically (at connection_check_interval) and
277	    before each operation. Return False if the integration is disconnected.
278	    """
279	    return self._device.is_connected()
280	```
281	
282	### hard_refresh_codes()
283	
284	Re-fetch codes directly from the device, bypassing any cache. Required if `hard_refresh_interval` is set.
285	
286	```python
287	def hard_refresh_codes(self) -> dict[int, str | None]:
288	    """
289	    Force refresh from device and return all codes.
290	
291	    This should bypass any caching layer and query the
292	    physical device directly.
293	
294	    Raises:
295	        LockDisconnected: If lock cannot be communicated with.
296	
297	    """
298	    self._cache = self._device.fetch_all_codes()
299	    return self.get_usercodes()
300	```
301	
302	## Implementing Push Updates
303	
304	### 1. Enable Push Mode
305	
306	```python
307	@property
308	def supports_push(self) -> bool:
309	    return True
310	```
311	
312	### 2. Subscribe to Events
313	
314	```python
315	@callback
316	def subscribe_push_updates(self) -> None:
317	    """Subscribe to real-time value updates.
318	
319	    Must be idempotent - no-op if already subscribed.
320	    """
321	    # Skip if already subscribed
322	    if self._unsub is not None:
323	        return
324	
325	    @callback
326	    def on_code_changed(slot: int, usercode: str | None) -> None:
327	        # Convert to coordinator format (empty string for cleared)
328	        value = usercode if usercode else ""
329	
330	        # Push update to coordinator
331	        if self.coordinator:
332	            self.coordinator.push_update({slot: value})
333	
334	    # Store unsubscribe function for cleanup
335	    self._unsub = self.device.subscribe_to_code_events(on_code_changed)
336	```
337	
338	### 3. Clean Up on Unload
339	
340	```python
341	@callback
342	def unsubscribe_push_updates(self) -> None:
343	    """Unsubscribe from value updates.
344	
345	    Must be idempotent - no-op if already unsubscribed.
346	    """
347	    if self._unsub:
348	        self._unsub()
349	        self._unsub = None
350	```
351	
352	## Exception Handling
353	
354	Providers must raise `LockCodeManagerError` subclasses for lock communication failures:
355	
356	```python
357	from ..exceptions import LockDisconnected
358	
359	def get_usercodes(self) -> dict[int, str | None]:
360	    try:
361	        return self._fetch_codes()
362	    except SomeDeviceError as err:
363	        raise LockDisconnected("Cannot communicate with lock") from err
364	```
365	
366	**Available exceptions:**
367	
368	| Exception              | When to Use                                 |
369	| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
370	| `LockDisconnected`     | Lock is unreachable or communication failed |
371	| `LockCodeManagerError` | Base class for other LCM errors             |
372	
373	The coordinator catches `LockCodeManagerError` and handles retry logic. Do NOT raise generic
374	exceptions or `HomeAssistantError` directly.
375	
376	## Rate Limiting
377	
378	The base class provides automatic rate limiting through `_execute_rate_limited()`. Use the
379	`async_internal_*` methods which apply rate limiting:
380	
381	- `async_internal_get_usercodes()` - rate-limited get
382	- `async_internal_set_usercode()` - rate-limited set + refresh
383	- `async_internal_clear_usercode()` - rate-limited clear + refresh
384	- `async_internal_hard_refresh_codes()` - rate-limited hard refresh
385	
386	The default delay between operations is 2 seconds (`MIN_OPERATION_DELAY`).
387	
388	## Connection State Management
389	
390	The base class handles connection state transitions:
391	
392	1. **Reconnection detection**: When `is_integration_connected()` transitions from `False` to `True`:
393	   - Coordinator refresh is triggered
394	   - Push subscriptions are re-established (if `supports_push=True`)
395	
396	2. **Disconnection handling**: When `is_integration_connected()` transitions from `True` to `False`:
397	   - Push subscriptions are cleaned up (if `supports_push=True`)
398	
399	3. **Config entry state changes**: For integrations that expose config entry state (like Z-Wave JS):
400	   - The base class listens for state changes
401	   - Automatically resubscribes when the integration reloads
402	
403	## Best Practices
404	
405	1. **Prefer push mode** when your integration supports events - it's more responsive and
406	   reduces device traffic.
407	
408	2. **Use drift detection** if codes can be changed outside Home Assistant (e.g., at the lock's keypad).
409	
410	3. **Cache appropriately** - `get_usercodes()` can return cached data, but
411	   `hard_refresh_codes()` should always query the device.
412	
413	4. **Handle disconnections gracefully** - raise `LockDisconnected` rather than letting exceptions bubble up.
414	
415	5. **Clean up subscriptions** - always implement `unsubscribe_push_updates()` to prevent
416	   memory leaks.
417	
418	6. **Make subscriptions idempotent** - `subscribe_push_updates()` and
419	   `unsubscribe_push_updates()` may be called multiple times.
420	
421	7. **Return change indicators** - `set_usercode()` and `clear_usercode()` should return
422	   `False` if no change was made to avoid unnecessary refreshes.
423	
424	8. **Use the internal methods** - Call `async_internal_*` methods which provide rate
425	   limiting, connection checks, and automatic coordinator refresh.
426	
```

1	# Adding a New Lock Provider
2	
3	This tutorial walks through adding support for a new lock integration to Lock Code Manager.
4	We'll create a provider for a hypothetical "SmartLock" integration.
5	
6	## Prerequisites
7	
8	Before starting, ensure:
9	
10	1. The lock integration exists in Home Assistant and creates `lock.*` entities
11	2. The integration provides a way to read and write usercodes
12	3. You understand the integration's data model and API

14	## Step 1: Create the Provider File

40	    """Class to represent SmartLock lock."""
41	
42	    # Add any provider-specific fields here
43	    _cache: dict[int, str] = field(default_factory=dict, init=False)
44	
45	    @property
46	    def domain(self) -> str:

93	    """Return whether the integration is connected."""

95	    if self.lock_config_entry:

114	
115	    Raises:
116	        LockDisconnected: If lock cannot be communicated with.
117	
118	    """

140	) -> bool:

268	    """Subscribe to real-time value updates."""

270	    if self._event_unsub is not None:
271	        return

275	        """Handle code change events."""
276	        slot = event_data["slot"]
277	        code = event_data.get("code", "")
278	
279	        # Push to coordinator

354	## Complete Example
355	
356	Here's a complete minimal provider:
357	
358	```python
359	"""Module for SmartLock integration."""
360	
361	from __future__ import annotations
362	
363	from dataclasses import dataclass
364	from datetime import timedelta
365	
366	from homeassistant.config_entries import ConfigEntryState
367	
368	from ..exceptions import LockDisconnected
369	from ._base import BaseLock
370	
371	
372	@dataclass(repr=False, eq=False)
373	class SmartLockLock(BaseLock):
374	    """Class to represent SmartLock lock."""
375	
376	    @property
377	    def domain(self) -> str:
378	        """Return integration domain."""
379	        return "smartlock"
380	
381	    @property
382	    def usercode_scan_interval(self) -> timedelta:
383	        """Return scan interval for usercodes."""
384	        return timedelta(minutes=1)
385	
386	    def is_integration_connected(self) -> bool:
387	        """Return whether connection to lock is up."""
388	        if self.lock_config_entry:
389	            return self.lock_config_entry.state == ConfigEntryState.LOADED
390	        return True
391	
392	    def get_usercodes(self) -> dict[int, str | None]:
393	        """Get dictionary of code slots and usercodes."""
394	        try:
395	            # Replace with your integration's API
396	            codes = self._get_codes_from_device()
397	            return {slot: code or "" for slot, code in codes.items()}
398	        except Exception as err:

434	
435	## Testing Your Provider
436	
437	### Manual Testing
438	
439	1. Add your provider to the registry
440	2. Restart Home Assistant
441	3. Configure Lock Code Manager with a lock using your integration
442	4. Verify:
443	   - Codes can be set and cleared
444	   - Code sensors show correct values
445	   - Sync status updates correctly
446	   - Events fire when codes are used (if applicable)
447	
448	### Automated Testing
449	
450	Create tests in `tests/test_smartlock.py`:
451	
452	```python
453	"""Tests for SmartLock provider."""
454	
455	import pytest
456	from unittest.mock import Mock, patch
457	
458	from custom_components.lock_code_manager.providers.smartlock import SmartLockLock
459	
460	
461	@pytest.fixture
462	def mock_lock():
463	    """Create a mock SmartLock provider."""
464	    # Set up mocks for your integration
465	    ...
466	
467	
468	async def test_get_usercodes(hass, mock_lock):
469	    """Test getting usercodes."""
470	    codes = mock_lock.get_usercodes()
471	    assert isinstance(codes, dict)
472	    assert all(isinstance(k, int) for k in codes.keys())
473	
474	
475	async def test_set_usercode(hass, mock_lock):
476	    """Test setting a usercode."""
477	    result = mock_lock.set_usercode(1, "1234")
478	    assert result is True
479	
480	
481	async def test_clear_usercode(hass, mock_lock):
482	    """Test clearing a usercode."""
483	    result = mock_lock.clear_usercode(1)
484	    assert result is True
485	```
486	
487	## Troubleshooting
488	
489	### Common Issues
490	
491	**"Entity not found" errors:**
492	
493	- Ensure the lock entity exists and is in the entity registry
494	- Check that `domain` returns the correct integration domain
495	
496	**Codes not syncing:**
497	
498	- Verify `get_usercodes()` returns the correct format
499	- Check that `set_usercode()` actually writes to the device
500	- Enable debug logging: `logger.setLevel(logging.DEBUG)`
501	
502	**Push updates not working:**
503	
504	- Ensure `supports_push` returns `True`
505	- Verify `subscribe_push_updates()` is being called
506	- Check that `coordinator.push_update()` is called with correct data
507	
508	**Connection state issues:**
509	
510	- Verify `is_integration_connected()` accurately reflects device state
511	- Check that `lock_config_entry` is set correctly
512	
513	### Debug Logging
514	
515	Add debug logging to your provider:
516	
517	```python
518	import logging
519	
520	_LOGGER = logging.getLogger(__name__)
521	
522	def get_usercodes(self) -> dict[int, str | None]:
523	    _LOGGER.debug("Getting usercodes for %s", self.lock.entity_id)
524	    codes = self._fetch_codes()
525	    _LOGGER.debug("Got codes: %s", {k: "****" for k in codes})
526	    return codes
527	```
528	
529	Enable in `configuration.yaml`:
530	
531	```yaml
532	logger:
533	  default: info
534	  logs:
535	    custom_components.lock_code_manager.providers.smartlock: debug
536	```
537

539	
540	- Review existing providers (`zwave_js.py`, `virtual.py`) for examples
541	- Read [[Provider State Management]] for advanced topics
542	- Submit a PR to add your provider to the main repository
543	
```

{
  "file_path": "/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager.wiki/Architecture.md",
  "content": "# Lock Code Manager Architecture\n\n## Overview\n\nLock Code Manager (LCM) manages PIN codes across locks via providers. Each lock gets a coordinator that holds the full slot-to-credential mapping (managed AND unmanaged). Provider implementations target a small contract on `BaseLock` that splits cleanly along two dimensions: how rich the lock's user model is, and whether the lock can push state changes.\n\n## Data Flow\n\n```text\nConfig Entry (desired state)\n    |\nBinary Sensor (sync decision)\n    | set/clear\nBaseLock seam (async_set_usercode / async_clear_usercode)\n    | for native-user locks: async_set_user -> async_set_credential\n    | for slot-only locks:   async_set_credential\nProvider (per-integration writes)\n    | integration service call / SDK\nLock (firmware)\n    | push notification / poll response\nCoordinator (actual state: dict[int, SlotCredential])\n    | listener notification\nBinary Sensor (re-evaluate sync)\n```\n\n## Domain Model: User → Credential\n\nLCM speaks a platform-neutral language at the seam: users own credentials.\n\n- **`User`** — `user_id`, `name`, `active`, `credentials: list[Credential]`. The lock's identity for a person.\n- **`Credential`** — `type` (`CredentialType.PIN` today; `RFID`, `FINGERPRINT`, etc. reserved), `slot` (LCM slot number), `state` (`SlotCredential`: empty / unreadable / known).\n- **`CredentialRef`** — `(user_id, type, slot)` hashable address used when pointing at a credential without carrying its state.\n- **`SlotCredential`** — frozen value with factories `empty()`, `unreadable()` (write-only locks report this on occupied slots), `known(pin)`.\n- **`LockCapabilities`** — what the lock advertises: `supports_user_management`, `max_users`, `credential_types: dict[CredentialType, CredentialTypeCapability]`, `max_user_name_length`.\n\nProviders expose users and credentials through `async_get_users() -> list[User]`. Slot-only providers (Z-Wave User Code CC, ZHA, Akuvox, Schlage, etc.) synthesize a single-credential user per occupied slot via `user_from_slot(...)`. Native-user providers (Matter, Z-Wave User Credential CC) return the lock's actual user list.\n\n## Coordinator\n\nStores `dict[int, SlotCredential]` mapping LCM slot number to credential state for ALL slots on the lock. Does not distinguish managed vs unmanaged — that distinction lives in the config entries.\n\n- Push-based providers (Z-Wave JS, Matter, ZHA, Zigbee2MQTT) set `update_interval = None`\n- Poll-based providers (Akuvox, Schlage, Virtual) use periodic refresh via `_async_update_data()`\n\n## Push vs Poll vs Hard Refresh\n\n- **Push**: device event → provider filters → `coordinator.push_update({slot: SlotCredential})`\n- **Poll**: coordinator's `_async_update_data()` → provider's `async_get_usercodes()` on interval (default-implemented in BaseLock as a projection over `async_get_users()`; providers may override for efficiency)\n- **Hard refresh**: `async_hard_refresh_codes()` → bypasses any cache and re-reads from the device. Triggered periodically via `hard_refresh_interval` for drift detection, and on demand via the `hard_refresh_usercodes` service.\n\n## Managed vs Unmanaged Slots\n\nA slot is **managed** if it exists in any LCM config entry's `CONF_SLOTS` for this lock AND the corresponding LCM entities exist.\n\nDetection: `_get_slot_entity_states()` returns `None` for unmanaged slots.\n\nCoordinator stores both managed and unmanaged; sync only operates on managed slots; the UI displays both.\n\n## Sync Decision\n\nThe in-sync binary sensor compares **desired state** (PIN from text entity, active state from condition) against **actual state** (coordinator data):\n\n- If active + PIN differs from coordinator → set\n- If inactive + code present in coordinator → clear\n- If states match → in sync (no operation)\n\n`SlotCredential.unreadable()` (write-only locks like Matter) is treated as in-sync against any expected PIN — the lock confirmed occupancy and we already set the value.\n\n## User-Tag Identity Model (4.0.0+)\n\nFor locks with a user-name field (Matter, Z-Wave U3C, Akuvox, Schlage), LCM tags its own users with `lcm:<slot>:<friendly name>` so it can coexist with other controllers and recover the LCM slot identity on every read.\n\nMechanics:\n\n- The base seam builds the tag via `_build_tagged_user_name(slot, display)`, truncating the display portion to fit `max_user_name_length`. For length-constrained locks where the canonical prefix doesn't fit, a slot-only fallback (`str(slot)`) is written.\n- Providers do find-or-create-by-tag in `async_set_user`: scan the lock's user list for a user whose name parses to the target LCM slot; UPDATE that user if found, CREATE a new one if not.\n- A second-pass legacy adoption scoops up pre-PR-1239/1240 users (Matter at `credential_index == slot`, Z-Wave U3C at `user_id == slot`) on the first write to each slot after upgrade, so existing PINs don't get orphaned.\n- The tolerant parser in `_util.py` accepts both the canonical `lcm:<slot>:<name>` form and the legacy `[LCM:<slot>] <name>` form (Akuvox/Schlage); legacy-tagged codes are rewritten to canonical on next write.\n\n## Persistent User Anchor Lifecycle (Native-User Providers)\n\nUnder the user-tag idempotency design, lock-side users are **slot anchors** that persist across PIN clear/replace cycles:\n\n- A clear deletes the credential but leaves the user record. The next set on the same slot finds that user by tag and writes a new credential under it.\n- The user is removed only when the slot itself is removed from LCM config, via `async_release_managed_slot(slot)`.\n- This decouples user lifecycle from credential lifecycle and keeps the find-or-create-by-tag invariant stable across operations.\n\nSlot-only providers don't have this distinction — there's nothing to anchor besides the credential itself.\n\n## PIN Clearing Auto-Disables Slots\n\nWhen a user clears the PIN text entity on an enabled slot, the text entity automatically disables the slot (turns off the enabled switch) before clearing the PIN value. This ensures the sync logic will clear the code on the lock rather than leaving a stale code active.\n\n## Masked / Unreadable PINs\n\nSome locks expose write-only PINs:\n\n- **Cloud-backed (Schlage)**: the API returns `****` for code values. LCM treats the slot as occupied but unreadable.\n- **Spec-level (Matter)**: PINs are write-only per the Matter DoorLock cluster.\n- **Variable (Z-Wave UC on some firmwares)**: some chipsets mask the value, others expose it.\n\nLCM handles this uniformly:\n\n- **Managed slots**: resolved via the text entity's expected PIN — if the expected PIN is set and the coordinator reports the slot occupied (`unreadable`), the binary sensor treats it as in-sync.\n- **Unmanaged slots**: kept as-is — `unreadable` just signals \"slot in use.\"\n\n## Duplicate Code Detection\n\nTwo layers of defense against duplicate PINs causing infinite sync loops:\n\n1. **Pre-flight check** (in `BaseLock`): scans coordinator data for matching readable PINs before sending to the lock. Raises `DuplicateCodeError`. Unreadable values are skipped because they can't be compared.\n2. **Provider-side duplicate signals** (Z-Wave JS event 15, Matter's `DuplicateCode` status, Schlage's \"duplicate code value\" error, etc.): reactive safety net for cases where the pre-flight check can't see the duplicate (e.g., unreadable codes on unmanaged slots, or a race with a keypad-entered code).\n\nBoth paths disable the slot and create a persistent notification.\n\n## Sync Attempt Tracking\n\nThe sync mechanism tracks consecutive successful SET attempts (provider call did not raise) that fail to resolve the out-of-sync state. If `MAX_SYNC_ATTEMPTS` are reached within `SYNC_ATTEMPT_WINDOW`, the lock is assumed to be rejecting the PIN. The slot is disabled and the user is notified.\n\nOnly SET operations are tracked — clears always proceed and are not counted. `LockDisconnected` exceptions are transient and use the separate retry mechanism with `RETRY_DELAY`. The tracker resets when the slot is disabled or when the code is successfully synced.\n\n## Exception Hierarchy\n\n```text\nLockCodeManagerError                       # base: LCM-internal error\n└── LockCodeManagerProviderError           # base: provider-side failure\n    ├── LockDisconnected                   # transient: route to retry\n    ├── LockOperationFailed                # lock reachable but operation didn't take\n    ├── CodeRejectedError                  # lock won't accept the PIN (any reason)\n    │   └── DuplicateCodeError             # PIN duplicates another slot\n    └── ProviderNotImplementedError        # bare BaseLock primitives raise this\n```\n\nProviders raise these subclasses; the seam catches them and routes:\n\n- `LockDisconnected` → retry with backoff\n- `CodeRejectedError` / `DuplicateCodeError` → disable slot, persistent notification\n- `LockOperationFailed` → log + propagate to caller\n\nDo NOT raise bare `Exception` or `HomeAssistantError` from providers — those bypass the routing.\n\n## Base Provider (`BaseLock`)\n\n`@final` seam methods are the single entry point for all lock operations:\n\n- `async_set_usercode(slot, pin, *, name)` — top-level \"ensure this slot has this PIN\"\n- `async_clear_usercode(slot)` — top-level \"clear this slot\"\n- `async_get_usercodes()` — default-implemented projection over `async_get_users()`\n\nThey enforce cross-cutting concerns in this order:\n\n1. **Integration connectivity check** — verify integration is connected\n2. **Device availability check** — verify physical device is responsive\n3. **Acquire operation lock** — serialize operations via `asyncio.Lock`\n4. **Pre-execute hook** (set only) — duplicate code check runs inside the lock\n5. **Rate limit delay** — minimum delay between operations\n6. **Provider primitives** — `_set_credential` / `_delete_credential` orchestration helpers\n7. **Coordinator refresh** — update state (skipped for push-based providers that report `True` from their primitive)\n\n### Orchestration helpers (also `@final`)\n\n- **`_set_credential(user, credential, pin, *, name, source)`** — for native-user providers, builds the tagged user name, calls `async_set_user(user_for_write)`, then `async_set_credential(user_id, credential, pin, ...)`. Rolls back a newly-created user if the credential write fails. For slot-only providers, just calls `async_set_credential`.\n- **`_delete_credential(ref)`** — calls `async_delete_credential(ref)`. Does NOT delete the owning user; the user is a persistent slot anchor (see lifecycle section above) and is removed via `async_release_managed_slot`.\n- **`_build_tagged_user_name(slot, display)`** — produces `lcm:<slot>:<display>`, truncates to fit `max_user_name_length`, falls back to slot-only or returns `None` for length-constrained locks.\n\n### Provider primitives (overridden per integration)\n\nSlot-only providers implement:\n\n- `async_set_credential(user_id, credential, pin, *, name, source) -> bool`\n- `async_delete_credential(ref) -> bool`\n- `async_get_users() -> list[User]` (typically via `user_from_slot`)\n- `is_integration_connected()` and the property/interval surface\n\nNative-user providers additionally implement:\n\n- `async_set_user(user) -> SetUserResult` (with find-or-create-by-tag)\n- `async_delete_user(user_id) -> None`\n- `async_get_capabilities() -> LockCapabilities`\n\nHelper methods available to all providers:\n\n- `is_masked_or_empty(...)` — detect unreadable or empty states\n- `is_slot_managed(code_slot)` — check if any LCM config entry manages this slot\n- `_require_readable_pin(credential)` — defensive guard that returns the readable PIN\n\nThe `source` parameter (`\"sync\"` or `\"direct\"`) indicates whether the call came from the sync path (binary sensor) or a user action (websocket / service). Currently informational; reserved for future differentiated error-handling policies.\n\n## Rate Limiting\n\nAll lock operations are serialized via `asyncio.Lock` per provider instance, with a 2-second minimum delay between operations (`MIN_OPERATION_DELAY`). This prevents overwhelming the lock's radio (Z-Wave mesh, Matter fabric, Zigbee network).\n\nA second outer `_sequence_lock` is available for read-modify-write sequences that span multiple primitive calls (e.g., Akuvox's list-then-modify pattern) without deadlocking on the inner per-call lock.\n\n## WebSocket Subscriptions\n\nWebSocket subscriptions for slot card data re-resolve entity IDs dynamically on each update. This handles entities that are created after the subscription is established (for example, during initial config setup). The resolution uses lightweight entity registry lookups.\n\n## Lovelace Dashboard Updates\n\nWhen structural config changes occur (slots or locks added/removed), LCM fires `lovelace_updated` events for each registered dashboard. This triggers the \"Configuration changed\" toast in the Home Assistant frontend, prompting users to refresh so the strategy re-generates cards.\n\n## Frontend\n\nThe frontend is built with TypeScript 6.0 and provides Lovelace strategies (dashboard, view, and section level) and custom cards (`lcm-slot`, `lcm-lock-codes`) for managing PINs.\n\n## See Also\n\n- [[Provider-State-Management]] — coordinator update modes, push/poll/drift, exception routing\n- [[Adding-a-Provider]] — step-by-step tutorial for implementing a new provider\n- [[Supporting-new-lock-integrations]] — higher-level guide on assessing integration feasibility\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager.wiki/Provider-State-Management.md",
  "content": "# Provider State Management\n\nThis guide explains how Lock Code Manager providers expose user/credential state to the coordinator and the sync seam: the domain model providers speak in, the three update modes (push / poll / drift), and the exception-routing contract.\n\n## Overview\n\nThe `LockUsercodeUpdateCoordinator` manages state through three update modes:\n\n| Mode | Mechanism | When to Use |\n| ---- | --------- | ----------- |\n| **Poll for updates** | Periodic `async_get_usercodes()` | Integrations without real-time events (Akuvox, Schlage, Virtual) |\n| **Push for updates** | Real-time event subscription | Integrations with push (Z-Wave JS, Matter, ZHA, Zigbee2MQTT) |\n| **Poll for drift** | Periodic `async_hard_refresh_codes()` | Catch out-of-band changes (keypad, other controllers) |\n\nAll modes include an initial poll to populate coordinator data.\n\n> **Important**: even with push enabled, you must implement `async_get_users()` (or the legacy `async_get_usercodes()`). The coordinator calls it for the initial load and any manual refresh request.\n\n## Coordinator Data Model\n\nCoordinator data is `dict[int, SlotCredential]`. Each entry maps an LCM slot number to a `SlotCredential`:\n\n- `SlotCredential.empty()` — slot has no credential\n- `SlotCredential.unreadable()` — slot is occupied but the value is masked or write-only\n- `SlotCredential.known(pin)` — slot has this readable PIN value\n\nProviders expose this in two ways:\n\n1. **`async_get_users() -> list[User]`** (the new path, post-4.0.0) — return a list of `User` objects each carrying `credentials: list[Credential]`. The base class's `async_get_usercodes()` projects these to `dict[int, SlotCredential]` via `user.pin_credentials`. Native-user providers map the lock's actual users; slot-only providers synthesize a single-credential user per occupied slot using `user_from_slot(slot, state)`.\n2. **`async_get_usercodes() -> dict[int, SlotCredential]`** (default-implemented) — the projection layer. Override only if you have a faster path to slot data than walking users.\n\n## Provider Architecture\n\n```text\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                LockUsercodeUpdateCoordinator                    │\n├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│  data: dict[int, SlotCredential]       # slot -> credential     │\n├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│  async_get_usercodes()                 # poll method            │\n│  push_update({slot: SlotCredential})   # push entry point       │\n│  _async_drift_check()                  # hard refresh timer     │\n│  _async_connection_check()             # connection poll timer  │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n                              │\n                              │ calls (via BaseLock seam)\n                              ▼\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                         BaseLock                                │\n├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│  Properties:                                                    │\n│    supports_push: bool                  # opt in to push mode   │\n│    supports_native_users: bool          # user lifecycle path   │\n│    usercode_scan_interval: timedelta    # polling interval      │\n│    hard_refresh_interval: timedelta     # drift detection       │\n│    connection_check_interval: timedelta # connection polling    │\n├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│  Always implement:                                              │\n│    async_get_users() -> list[User]                              │\n│    async_set_credential(user_id, credential, pin, ...) -> bool  │\n│    async_delete_credential(ref) -> bool                         │\n│    is_integration_connected() -> bool                           │\n├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│  Native-user providers also implement:                          │\n│    async_set_user(user) -> SetUserResult                        │\n│    async_delete_user(user_id) -> None                           │\n│    async_get_capabilities() -> LockCapabilities                 │\n├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│  Optional:                                                      │\n│    async_hard_refresh_codes()           # re-fetch from device  │\n│    subscribe_push_updates()             # set up listeners      │\n│    unsubscribe_push_updates()           # clean up listeners    │\n│    async_release_managed_slot(slot)     # slot teardown hook    │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n                              │\n                              │ implements\n                              ▼\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                      YourLockProvider                           │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\n## Slot-Only vs Native-User Providers\n\nProviders split into two flavors based on the lock's user model:\n\n- **Slot-only** — the lock indexes credentials by slot directly with no user concept (Z-Wave User Code CC, ZHA, Zigbee2MQTT, Virtual) OR the user is the credential's friendly name (Akuvox, Schlage). Set `supports_native_users = False` (the default). LCM addresses credentials by slot; `user_id` in `async_set_credential` is ignored.\n- **Native-user** — the lock has a real user record that owns one or more credentials (Matter, Z-Wave User Credential CC). Set `supports_native_users = True`. LCM follows a user-first lifecycle: `async_set_user` then `async_set_credential`. Implement `async_get_capabilities()` so the seam can decide whether to write a user record before the credential.\n\nThe seam (`_set_credential` / `_delete_credential` in `BaseLock`) routes the orchestration automatically; you just implement the primitives.\n\n## Update Modes\n\n### Poll Mode (Default)\n\nThe coordinator periodically calls `async_get_usercodes()` at `usercode_scan_interval`.\n\n**Flow**:\n\n1. Timer fires at `usercode_scan_interval`\n2. Coordinator calls `async_internal_get_usercodes()`\n3. Base class applies rate limiting, then calls `async_get_usercodes()` (which by default projects `async_get_users()`)\n4. Provider returns current credential state\n5. Coordinator updates `data` and notifies listening entities\n\n**When to use**: integrations without push event support.\n\n**Example**:\n\n```python\nclass MyLock(BaseLock):\n    @property\n    def usercode_scan_interval(self) -> timedelta:\n        return timedelta(minutes=1)\n\n    @property\n    def hard_refresh_interval(self) -> timedelta | None:\n        return None  # No separate drift check needed\n```\n\n### Push Mode\n\nFor integrations that emit real-time events (Z-Wave value updates, Matter LockUserChange, ZHA programming events, Zigbee2MQTT MQTT messages).\n\n**Flow**:\n\n1. Provider subscribes to integration events in `subscribe_push_updates()`\n2. An event fires\n3. Provider's handler resolves the LCM slot (for native-user providers under the tag identity model, this means walking `userIndex → user.name → lcm:<slot>:` tag) and the `SlotCredential` value\n4. Provider calls `self.coordinator.push_update({slot: SlotCredential})`\n5. Coordinator merges and notifies entities immediately\n\n**When to use**: any integration with push. Cuts polling overhead and gives the UI real-time feedback.\n\n**Example**:\n\n```python\nclass MyLock(BaseLock):\n    @property\n    def supports_push(self) -> bool:\n        return True\n\n    @property\n    def hard_refresh_interval(self) -> timedelta | None:\n        return timedelta(hours=1)  # Still recommended for drift\n```\n\n### Drift Detection\n\nDrift detection re-reads the lock to catch changes the push path missed (keypad-enrolled codes, races, other controllers).\n\n**Flow**:\n\n1. Timer fires at `hard_refresh_interval`\n2. Coordinator calls `async_internal_hard_refresh_codes()`\n3. Provider queries the device directly, bypassing any cache (`async_hard_refresh_codes()`)\n4. Coordinator updates and notifies entities if anything changed\n\n**When to use**:\n\n- Codes can be changed outside Home Assistant\n- The integration caches values that can go stale\n- You want a backstop even with push mode\n\n## Interval Properties\n\n| Property | Default | Purpose |\n| -------- | ------- | ------- |\n| `supports_push` | `False` | Opt-in to push mode (disables polling for updates; polling for drift still applies) |\n| `supports_native_users` | `False` | Opt-in to the user lifecycle path |\n| `usercode_scan_interval` | 1 minute | How often to poll for updates (ignored if `supports_push=True`) |\n| `hard_refresh_interval` | `None` | How often to hard refresh for drift detection (`None` = disabled) |\n| `connection_check_interval` | 30 seconds | How often to check connection state (`None` = disabled, used when the integration emits config-entry state changes) |\n\n## Implementing the Provider Primitives\n\n### `async_get_users()`\n\nReturn the lock's users with their credentials.\n\n```python\nfrom custom_components.lock_code_manager.domain.credentials import (\n    Credential,\n    CredentialType,\n    User,\n    user_from_slot,\n)\nfrom custom_components.lock_code_manager.domain.models import SlotCredential\n\n\n# Slot-only: synthesize one user per occupied slot.\nasync def async_get_users(self) -> list[User]:\n    \"\"\"Read current credential state from the device.\"\"\"\n    try:\n        raw = await self._device.get_all_codes()\n    except SomeDeviceError as err:\n        raise LockDisconnected(f\"get codes failed: {err}\") from err\n\n    return [\n        user_from_slot(\n            slot,\n            SlotCredential.known(pin) if pin else SlotCredential.empty(),\n        )\n        for slot, pin in raw.items()\n    ]\n\n\n# Native-user: return the lock's actual users.\nasync def async_get_users(self) -> list[User]:\n    \"\"\"Read users + credentials from the lock.\"\"\"\n    raw_users = await self._driver.list_users()\n    raw_creds = await self._driver.list_credentials()\n    users_by_id = {\n        u.user_id: User(user_id=u.user_id, name=u.name, active=u.active)\n        for u in raw_users\n    }\n    for cred in raw_creds:\n        owner = users_by_id.get(cred.user_id)\n        if owner is None:\n            continue\n        owner.credentials.append(\n            Credential(\n                type=CredentialType.PIN,\n                slot=cred.slot,\n                state=(\n                    SlotCredential.known(cred.value)\n                    if cred.value\n                    else SlotCredential.unreadable()\n                ),\n            )\n        )\n    return list(users_by_id.values())\n```\n\n### `async_set_credential()`\n\nWrite a single credential. The base seam has already resolved `user_id` (for native-user providers, via the find-or-create-by-tag in `async_set_user`).\n\n```python\nasync def async_set_credential(\n    self,\n    user_id: int,\n    credential: Credential,\n    pin: str,\n    *,\n    name: str | None,\n    source: Literal[\"sync\", \"direct\"],\n) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Write a PIN to a slot; return whether the lock changed.\"\"\"\n    try:\n        await self._driver.set_pin(\n            user_id=user_id,\n            slot=credential.slot,\n            pin=pin,\n        )\n    except DuplicateError as err:\n        raise DuplicateCodeError(\n            code_slot=credential.slot,\n            lock_entity_id=self.lock.entity_id,\n        ) from err\n    except DeviceError as err:\n        # Transient: route to retry, not slot suspension.\n        raise LockDisconnected(\n            f\"set credential slot {credential.slot} failed: {err}\"\n        ) from err\n    return True\n```\n\nReturn `True` if the value changed, `False` if the lock confirmed it was already set. When you can't tell (write-only locks like Matter), return `True` — the seam uses this to drive a coordinator refresh.\n\n### `async_delete_credential()`\n\n```python\nasync def async_delete_credential(self, ref: CredentialRef) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Delete the credential addressed by ref.\"\"\"\n    try:\n        await self._driver.clear_credential(\n            user_id=ref.user_id,\n            slot=ref.slot,\n        )\n    except DeviceError as err:\n        raise LockDisconnected(\n            f\"delete credential slot {ref.slot} failed: {err}\"\n        ) from err\n    return True\n```\n\nNote: the seam does **not** delete the owning user after `async_delete_credential` returns. The user is a persistent slot anchor (see [[Architecture]] for the lifecycle rationale). User deletion happens via `async_release_managed_slot(slot)`.\n\n### `async_set_user()` (Native-User Only)\n\nFind-or-create the lock user for the LCM slot encoded in `user.name`.\n\n```python\nfrom custom_components.lock_code_manager.providers._util import parse_tag\n\n\nasync def async_set_user(self, user: User) -> SetUserResult:\n    \"\"\"Find-or-create the lock user for the LCM slot in user.name.\"\"\"\n    slot = self._slot_from_seam_user(user)\n    existing_user_id = await self._find_user_index_for_slot(slot)\n    try:\n        result = await self._driver.set_user(\n            user_id=existing_user_id,  # None on CREATE\n            user_name=user.name,\n            active=user.active,\n        )\n    except DeviceError as err:\n        raise LockDisconnected(f\"set user for slot {slot} failed: {err}\") from err\n    return SetUserResult(\n        user_id=result[\"user_id\"], created=existing_user_id is None\n    )\n\n\ndef _slot_from_seam_user(self, user: User) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Recover LCM slot from the tagged user name; fall back to user_id.\"\"\"\n    if user.name:\n        slot, _ = parse_tag(user.name)\n        if slot is not None:\n            return slot\n    return user.user_id\n\n\nasync def _find_user_index_for_slot(self, slot: int) -> int | None:\n    \"\"\"Return the lock user_id LCM owns for slot, if any.\n\n    1. Canonical pass: a user whose name parses to this LCM slot.\n    2. Legacy adoption: an untagged user at the pre-PR-C invariant\n       (user_id == slot for U3C; credential_index == slot for Matter)\n       that also owns a PIN at the slot. Skip users already tagged for\n       a different slot so we don't re-bind cross-slot.\n    \"\"\"\n    users = await self.async_get_users()\n    try:\n        return next(\n            u.user_id\n            for u in users\n            if u.name and parse_tag(u.name)[0] == slot\n        )\n    except StopIteration:\n        return next(\n            (\n                u.user_id\n                for u in users\n                if u.user_id == slot\n                and parse_tag(u.name or \"\")[0] is None\n                for cred in u.pin_credentials\n                if cred.slot == slot\n            ),\n            None,\n        )\n```\n\nThe legacy adoption pass is what makes pre-4.0.0 installs upgrade seamlessly without orphaning existing PINs.\n\n### `async_delete_user()` (Native-User Only)\n\n```python\nasync def async_delete_user(self, user_id: int) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Delete a lock user (cascades its credentials per spec).\"\"\"\n    try:\n        await self._driver.delete_user(user_id)\n    except DeviceError as err:\n        raise LockDisconnected(f\"delete user {user_id} failed: {err}\") from err\n```\n\n### `async_get_capabilities()` (Native-User Only)\n\n```python\nasync def async_get_capabilities(self) -> LockCapabilities:\n    \"\"\"Report lock capabilities used by the seam to gate the user path.\"\"\"\n    caps = await self._driver.get_capabilities()\n    return LockCapabilities(\n        supports_user_management=caps[\"supports_user_management\"],\n        max_users=caps[\"max_users\"],\n        credential_types={\n            CredentialType.PIN: CredentialTypeCapability(\n                num_slots=caps[\"pin_num_slots\"],\n                min_length=caps[\"pin_min_length\"],\n                max_length=caps[\"pin_max_length\"],\n                supports_learn=False,\n            )\n        },\n        max_user_name_length=caps.get(\"max_user_name_length\", 0),\n    )\n```\n\nThe seam reads `supports_user_management` and `max_user_name_length` to decide whether the user-lifecycle path applies, and to size the tagged user name.\n\n### `is_integration_connected()`\n\n```python\ndef is_integration_connected(self) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Return whether the integration is connected.\"\"\"\n    return self.lock_config_entry.state == ConfigEntryState.LOADED\n```\n\n## Implementing Push Updates\n\n### 1. Enable push mode\n\n```python\n@property\ndef supports_push(self) -> bool:\n    return True\n```\n\n### 2. Subscribe to events\n\n```python\n@callback\ndef subscribe_push_updates(self) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Subscribe to real-time updates. Must be idempotent.\"\"\"\n    if self._event_unsub is not None:\n        return\n\n    @callback\n    def on_code_changed(event_data) -> None:\n        slot = event_data[\"slot\"]\n        state = (\n            SlotCredential.known(event_data[\"pin\"])\n            if event_data.get(\"pin\")\n            else SlotCredential.empty()\n        )\n        if self.coordinator:\n            self.coordinator.push_update({slot: state})\n\n    self._event_unsub = self._device.subscribe(on_code_changed)\n```\n\n### 3. Tear down on unload\n\n```python\n@callback\ndef unsubscribe_push_updates(self) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Unsubscribe. Must be idempotent.\"\"\"\n    if self._event_unsub:\n        self._event_unsub()\n        self._event_unsub = None\n```\n\n### Push under the tag identity model\n\nFor native-user providers using `lcm:<slot>:` tags, the push handler must resolve the LCM slot via the owning user's tag, not via lock-side indices that may differ from LCM slots. See the Matter provider's `_dispatch_lock_user_change` for the canonical pattern: extract `userIndex` from the event, fetch the raw user list, parse its name's tag, and push to the resolved LCM slot.\n\n## Exception Routing\n\nProviders must raise `LockCodeManagerProviderError` subclasses for lock-side failures. The seam routes each subclass differently:\n\n| Exception | When to raise | Seam behavior |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `LockDisconnected` | Transient communication failure (lock asleep, integration not loaded, network glitch) | Retry with backoff |\n| `LockOperationFailed` | Lock reachable but the operation didn't take (rejected input, response timeout) | Log + propagate |\n| `CodeRejectedError` | Lock will not accept this PIN (any reason) | Disable slot, persistent notification |\n| `DuplicateCodeError` | PIN duplicates another slot's value | Disable slot, persistent notification (subclass of CodeRejectedError) |\n| `ProviderNotImplementedError` | A primitive is missing on a subclass (raised by `BaseLock` defaults) | Programmer error; do not raise from real provider code |\n\n```python\nfrom ..domain.exceptions import (\n    CodeRejectedError,\n    DuplicateCodeError,\n    LockDisconnected,\n    LockOperationFailed,\n)\n\n\nasync def async_set_credential(self, user_id, credential, pin, *, name, source):\n    try:\n        await self._driver.set_pin(user_id, credential.slot, pin)\n    except TransientError as err:\n        raise LockDisconnected(f\"set slot {credential.slot}: {err}\") from err\n    except DuplicatePinError as err:\n        raise DuplicateCodeError(\n            code_slot=credential.slot,\n            lock_entity_id=self.lock.entity_id,\n        ) from err\n    except RejectedError as err:\n        raise CodeRejectedError(\n            code_slot=credential.slot,\n            lock_entity_id=self.lock.entity_id,\n            reason=str(err),\n        ) from err\n    return True\n```\n\nDo **not** raise bare `Exception` or `HomeAssistantError` from providers — those bypass the routing.\n\n## Rate Limiting\n\nThe base class provides automatic rate limiting through `_execute_rate_limited()`. The `@final` `async_internal_*` methods apply it:\n\n- `async_internal_get_usercodes()` — rate-limited get\n- `async_set_usercode()` — rate-limited set + refresh\n- `async_clear_usercode()` — rate-limited clear + refresh\n- `async_internal_hard_refresh_codes()` — rate-limited hard refresh\n\nDefault delay between operations is 2 seconds (`MIN_OPERATION_DELAY`).\n\nFor read-modify-write sequences (e.g., Akuvox's list-then-modify pattern), there is an outer `_sequence_lock` that providers can acquire to make the whole sequence atomic without deadlocking on the inner per-call lock.\n\n## Connection State Management\n\nThe base class handles connection state transitions:\n\n1. **Reconnection detection**: when `is_integration_connected()` transitions from `False` to `True`:\n   - Coordinator refresh is triggered\n   - Push subscriptions are re-established (if `supports_push=True`)\n2. **Disconnection handling**: when it transitions from `True` to `False`:\n   - Push subscriptions are cleaned up\n3. **Config entry state changes**: for integrations that expose config entry state (Z-Wave JS, Matter):\n   - The base class listens for state changes\n   - Automatically re-runs setup when the integration reloads\n\nFor these \"rich-state\" integrations, set `connection_check_interval = None` since the connection event drives the transitions.\n\n## Slot Teardown Hook\n\nWhen a slot is removed from LCM config, the base seam calls `async_release_managed_slot(slot)` on each provider that manages that slot. The default implementation is a no-op. Native-user providers override to remove the persistent user anchor for the slot (and any remaining credentials cascade per spec).\n\n```python\nasync def async_release_managed_slot(self, slot: int) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Remove the lock user that anchors this LCM slot.\"\"\"\n    user_id = await self._find_user_index_for_slot(slot)\n    if user_id is not None:\n        await self.async_delete_user(user_id)\n```\n\nWrap in `try/except LockDisconnected` — slot teardown can't block on lock connectivity.\n\n## Best Practices\n\n1. **Prefer push** when the integration supports events — more responsive, less device traffic, less mesh load.\n2. **Enable drift detection** when codes can change outside Home Assistant; pair it with push.\n3. **Cache appropriately** — `async_get_users()` may return cached data; `async_hard_refresh_codes()` must bypass cache.\n4. **Use the typed exceptions** — `LockDisconnected` for transient, `CodeRejectedError` for permanent rejections, `LockOperationFailed` for everything in between.\n5. **Make subscriptions idempotent** — both subscribe and unsubscribe may be called multiple times.\n6. **Return `True` when uncertain** — for write-only locks, returning `True` from set/delete primitives drives a coordinator refresh; returning `False` skips it.\n7. **Use the orchestration helpers** — call the `@final` seam methods (`async_set_usercode` / `async_clear_usercode`), not the primitives directly. The seam owns rate limiting, connection checks, and coordinator routing.\n8. **Resolve LCM slots, not lock indices, in push handlers** — for native-user providers under the tag identity model, the lock's user_id / credential_index may differ from the LCM slot. Always resolve via the owning user's `lcm:<slot>:` tag.\n"
}

You understand the integration's user/credential model: does it expose users with credentials (Matter, Z-Wave User Credential CC), or just slot-indexed credentials (Z-Wave User Code CC, ZHA, Akuvox, Schlage)?\n\n## Choose Your Provider Flavor\n\nLCM providers split into two flavors based on the lock's user model. custom_components/lock_code_manager/providers/smartlock.py\n\"\"\"Module for SmartLock integration.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom datetime \"\"\"Return interval for connection state checks.\"\"\"\n    return timedelta(seconds=30)\n```\n\nFor push-capable integrations, set `connection_check_interval = None` and rely on config-entry state to True if you'll implement push\n\n@property\ndef supports_native_users(self) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Return True for locks with a real user record (Matter, Z-Wave U3C).\"\"\"\n    return False  # reachable.\"\"\"\n    # Option A: check config entry state\n    if self.lock_config_entry:\n        return self.lock_config_entry.state == ConfigEntryState.LOADED\n\n    # Option B: check the entity When the integration doesn't tell you (write-only locks), return `True` — the seam uses this to drive a coordinator refresh.\n\n### `async_delete_credential`\n\n```python\nasync def async_delete_credential(self, ref: CredentialRef) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Delete the credential addressed by ref.\"\"\"\n    try:\n        await self._device.clear_code(ref.slot)\n    except TransientError as err:\n        raise LockDisconnected(\n            f\"clear slot {ref.slot} failed: {err}\"\n        ) from err\n    except LockApiError as err:\n        raise LockOperationFailed(\n            f\"clear slot {ref.slot} failed: {err}\"\n        ) from err\n    return True\n```\n\nThe seam does **not** delete the owning user after `async_delete_credential` for native-user providers — the user is a persistent slot anchor; see [[Architecture]] for the lifecycle rationale.\n\n## Step 6: Implement Hard Refresh (Recommended)\n\nIf your integration caches data, bypass that cache to detect drift.\n\n```python\nasync def async_hard_refresh_codes(self) -> dict[int, SlotCredential]:\n    \"\"\"Force a fresh read and return the projected slot map.\"\"\"\n    try:\n        await self._device.invalidate_cache()\n    except SomeDeviceError as err:\n        raise LockDisconnected(f\"refresh failed: {err}\") from err\n\n    return await self.async_get_usercodes()\n```\n\n## Step 7: Add Push Support (Optional)\n\nIf the integration emits real-time events:\n\n```python\n@property\ndef supports_push(self) -> bool:\n    return True\n\n@dataclass(repr=False, eq=False)\nclass SmartLockLock(BaseLock):\n    # ...existing fields...\n    _event_unsub: Callable[[], None] | None = field(init=False, default=None)\n\n    @callback\n    def subscribe_push_updates(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Subscribe to real-time updates. slot.\"\"\"\n    user_id = await self._find_user_index_for_slot(slot)\n    if user_id is None:\n        return\n    try:\n        await self.async_delete_user(user_id)\n    except (LockDisconnected, LockOperationFailed) as err:\n        _LOGGER.debug(\n            \"Lock %s: could not release slot %s anchor: %s\",\n            self.lock.entity_id,\n            slot,\n            err,\n        )\n```\n\nWrap in `try/except` so slot teardown doesn't block on lock connectivity.\n\n## Complete Minimal Slot-Only Example\n\n```python\n\"\"\"Module for SmartLock integration.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\nfrom datetime import timedelta\nfrom typing import Literal\n\nfrom homeassistant.config_entries import ConfigEntry, ConfigEntryState\n\nfrom ..domain.credentials import (\n    Credential,\n    CredentialRef,\n    User,\n    user_from_slot,\n)\nfrom ..domain.exceptions import (\n    CodeRejectedError,\n    DuplicateCodeError,\n    LockDisconnected,\n)\nfrom ..domain.models import SlotCredential\nfrom ._base import BaseLock\n\n\n@dataclass(repr=False, eq=False)\nclass SmartLockLock(BaseLock):\n    \"\"\"Class to represent SmartLock lock.\"\"\"\n\n    @property\n    def domain(self) -> str:\n        return \"smartlock\"\n\n    @property\n    def usercode_scan_interval(self) -> timedelta:\n        return timedelta(minutes=2)\n\n    def is_integration_connected(self) -> bool:\n        if self.lock_config_entry:\n            return self.lock_config_entry.state == ConfigEntryState.LOADED\n        return True\n\n    async def async_get_users(self) -> list[User]:\n        try:\n            codes = await self._fetch_codes_from_device()\n        except Exception as err:\n            raise LockDisconnected(str(err)) from err\n        return [\n            user_from_slot(\n                slot,\n                SlotCredential.known(pin) if pin else SlotCredential.empty(),\n            )\n            for slot, pin in codes.items()\n        ]\n\n    async def async_set_credential(\n        self,\n        user_id: int,\n        credential: Credential,\n        pin: str,\n        *,\n        name: str | None,\n        source: Literal[\"sync\", \"direct\"],\n    ) -> bool:\n        try:\n            await self._set_code_on_device(credential.slot, pin)\n        except DuplicatePinError as err:\n            raise DuplicateCodeError(\n                code_slot=credential.slot,\n                lock_entity_id=self.lock.entity_id,\n            ) from err\n        except Exception as err:\n            raise LockDisconnected(str(err)) from err\n        return True\n\n    async def async_delete_credential(self, ref: CredentialRef) -> bool:\n        try:\n            await self._clear_code_on_device(ref.slot)\n        except Exception as err:\n            raise LockDisconnected(str(err)) from err\n        return True\n\n    # ─── Integration-specific helpers async def _set_code_on_device(self, slot: int, pin: str) -> None:\n        raise NotImplementedError\n\n    async def _clear_code_on_device(self, slot: int) -> None:\n        raise NotImplementedError\n```\n\n## Testing Your Provider\n\n### Unit tests\n\nCreate `tests/providers/smartlock/test_provider.py`. Mirror the structure of an existing provider's tests (`tests/providers/zwave_js/test_provider.py` for native-user, `tests/providers/akuvox/test_provider.py` for slot-only).\n\nKey fixtures to exercise:\n\n- `async_get_users()` returns the expected `User` list given seeded device state\n- `async_set_credential()` calls the integration's API with the right slot + pin and returns `True`\n- `async_delete_credential()` calls the integration's API and returns `True`\n- Exception mapping: device errors become `LockDisconnected`, duplicate-pin errors become `DuplicateCodeError`, rejections become `CodeRejectedError`\n- For native-user: `async_set_user()` does find-or-create-by-tag; legacy adoption picks up the pre-upgrade user; legacy pass skips users tagged for other slots\n\n### Manual testing\n\n1. Restart Home Assistant after registering the provider.\n2. Configure LCM with a lock using your integration.\n3. Verify:\n   - Codes can be set and cleared from LCM\n   - The code sensor shows correct values (or \"unreadable\" for write-only locks)\n   - Sync status updates correctly\n   - For native-user providers: lock-side users carry `lcm:<slot>:<name>` tags\n   - For push providers: changes made at the keypad show up in LCM in real time\n   - Hard refresh detects out-of-band changes\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n**\"Entity not found\" errors**: ensure the lock entity exists and is in the entity registry. Check that `domain` returns the correct integration domain.\n\n**Codes not syncing**: verify `async_get_users()` returns valid `User` objects with `pin_credentials` populated. Check that `async_set_credential()` actually writes to the device. Enable debug logging.\n\n**Push updates not arriving**: ensure `supports_push` returns `True`. Verify `subscribe_push_updates()` is called (the base seam calls it in `async_setup`). Check that `coordinator.push_update({slot: SlotCredential})` is called with the right slot.\n\n**For native-user providers, the wrong slot is reported on push**: under the user-tag identity model, the lock's user_id and credential_index may differ from the LCM slot. The push handler must resolve the LCM slot via `parse_tag` on the owning user's name, not from lock-side indices. See the Matter provider's `_dispatch_lock_user_change` for the canonical pattern.\n\n### Debug logging\n\n```yaml\n# configuration.yaml\nlogger:\n  default: info\n  logs:\n    custom_components.lock_code_manager.providers.smartlock: debug\n```\n\n## Next Steps\n\n- Review existing providers as references:\n  - **Slot-only**: `virtual.py`, `akuvox.py`, `schlage.py`, `zha.py`, `zigbee2mqtt.py`\n  - **Native-user**: `matter.py`, `zwave_js.py`\n- Read [[Provider-State-Management]] for the coordinator + exception contract in depth.\n- Read [[Architecture]] for the cross-cutting design (user-tag identity, persistent user anchor lifecycle, masked PINs, duplicate detection).\n- Submit a PR to add your provider to the main repository.\n"
